This is contrary to what the Arabs and the grammarians have agreed upon: that one never pauses on a vowelled letter at all, whether its vowel is one of inflection, of indeclinability, of transfer, for the meeting of two unvowelled letters, of assimilation (itbāʿ) or of quotation (ḥikāya). So in «قد أفلح», when you omit the hamza and transfer its vowel to the dāl of «قد», it is not permitted to pause on the dāl of «قد» with the fatḥa; rather, you unvowel it, with one view [only]. As for his saying 'Its parallel is «واحدِ اثنان», with their casting the vowel of the hamza onto the dāl': Sībawayh mentioned that they give a trace of the vowel (ishmām) to the end of «واحد» because of its full declinability, and he did not report the kasra as a dialect. If the kasra is sound, then «واحد» is not paused upon, as al-Zamakhsharī claimed, nor is its vowel a vowel of transfer from the connecting hamza; rather, it is connected to their saying «اثنان», so two unvowelled letters met — the dāl of «واحد» and the thāʾ of «اثنين» — and the dāl was given kasra for the meeting of the two unvowelled letters, and the connecting hamza was omitted because it is not established in continuous speech."

I say: When did al-Zamakhsharī claim that one pauses on the mīm of «ألف لام ميم» while it is vowelled, so that he [Abū Ḥayyān] could charge him with contravening the consensus of the Arabs and the grammarians? The man only claimed that this is intended as paused upon before its being vowelled with the vowel of transfer — not that [the vowel] was transferred to it and then it was paused upon. This he never said at all, nor did it occur to him. Then al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: Why did you not claim that it is a vowel for the meeting of two unvowelled letters? I say: Because the meeting of two unvowelled letters is of no account in the domain of the pause; that is your saying «هذا إبراهيمْ وداودْ وإسحاقْ». Had the meeting of two unvowelled letters in the state of pause required vowelling, the two mīms in «ألف لام ميم» would have been vowelled for the meeting of two unvowelled letters, and another unvowelled letter would not have been awaited."

The Shaykh said: "It is a sound question and a sound answer; but the one who said 'the vowel is for the meeting of the two unvowelled letters' cannot be imagined to have meant the meeting of the yāʾ and the mīm of «ألم» in the pause; he only meant the meeting of the two unvowelled letters that are the final mīm of «ميم» and the lām of definiteness, like the meeting of the nūn of «مِنْ» and the lām of «الرجل» when you say «من الرجل»." I say: This view is the one I presented earlier from some [scholars], namely Makkī and others.

Then al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: They did not vowel [the mīm] for the meeting of two unvowelled letters in «ميم» only because they intended the pause and it was possible for them to pronounce two unvowelled letters; but when a third unvowelled letter came, there was nothing but vowelling, so they vowelled. I say: The proof that the vowel is not for meeting the unvowelled letter is that they could have said «واحدْ اثنان» with the dāl unvowelled while dropping the hamza, thus combining two unvowelled letters, as they said «أُصَيْمٌّ» and «مُدَيْقٌّ»; so when they vowelled the dāl, it was known that its vowel is the vowel of the dropped hamza and nothing else, and that it is not for the meeting of two unvowelled letters."

The Shaykh said: "In his question there is obscurity, in his saying 'If you say: They did not vowel for the meeting of two unvowelled letters', meaning by the two unvowelled letters the yāʾ and the mīm; then comes the reasoning in his saying 'because they intended the pause and it was possible for them to pronounce two unvowelled letters', meaning the yāʾ and the mīm. Then he said 'but when a third unvowelled letter came' — meaning the lām of definiteness — 'there was nothing but vowelling' — meaning in the mīm — 'so they vowelled' — meaning the mīm, because of its meeting, unvowelled, with the lām of definiteness, since had they not vowelled it, three unvowelled letters would have come together, which is not possible. This is the explanation of the question. As for al-Zamakhsharī's answer to his own question, it does not match, because he argued that the vowel is not for meeting an unvowelled letter from the possibility of combining two unvowelled letters in their saying «واحدْ اثنان», by their unvowelling the dāl while the thāʾ is unvowelled and the hamza drops, and [claimed] they turned away from this possibility to transferring the vowel of the hamza onto the dāl. This is obstinacy against what is perceptible: that is not possible at all, nor is it within human capacity to combine in pronunciation the unvowelled dāl, the unvowelled thāʾ and the dropping of the hamza.

As for his saying 'thus combining two unvowelled letters', combining them is not possible, as we said. As for his saying 'as they said «أُصَيْمُّ» and «مُدَيْقٌّ»', this is possible, as in «رادٌّ» and «ضالٌّ», because in that there is a meeting of two unvowelled letters within their limit stipulated in grammar, so it is possible; and it is not like «واحدْ اثنان», because the first unvowelled letter is not a letter of prolongation (madd), nor is the second assimilated, so they cannot be combined. As for his saying 'so when they vowelled the dāl, it was known that its vowel is the vowel of the dropped hamza and nothing else, and not for the meeting of two unvowelled letters': since he built on [the premise] that combining two unvowelled letters in «واحدْ اثنان» is possible, and that the vowel for the meeting of two unvowelled letters is only in what cannot be combined in pronunciation, he claimed that the vowel of the dāl is the vowel of the dropped hamza."

I say: This with which he rejected him is correct, and it is known necessarily, since it is not possible to pronounce what he mentioned. Someone has championed the opinion of al-Farrāʾ and the choice of al-Zamakhsharī [by saying] that these letters were brought for a meaning in something else, as was stated at the beginning of al-Baqara according to some, so their ends are paused upon and with what follows them a fresh start is intended; hence the hamza is treated as established, as in the half-lines of verses, as in the saying of Ḥassān:

1157 - لَتَسْمَعَُنَّ وشيكاً في ديارِهُمُ ... أللهُ أكبرُ يا ثاراتِ عثمانا
(You shall soon hear in their homes: "Allah is Greatest! O vengeance for ʿUthmān!")

Someone also supported it by what is reported from al-Mubarrad, that he permitted «الله أكبرَ الله أكبر» with fatḥa on the first rāʾ. He said: "Because they intend pausing on «أكبر» and beginning with what follows; so when they connected while intending to signal the pause at the end of each word of the takbīr, they transferred the vowel of the hamza that enters the lām of definiteness to the unvowelled letter before it, in regard of what was mentioned of their intention. And if they did that with the vowels of inflection and brought other [vowels] in their place, despite their need for the vowel as such, then that they should do it with what has its end paused is all the more fitting and appropriate."

The fourth: that the fatḥa is a fatḥa of inflection, on the basis that it is the object of an implied verb, i.e. «اقرؤوا ألم» "Recite Alif Lām Mīm"; it was made a diptote only because of being a proper name and of semantic femininity, when the name of the sūra is intended by it, as in «قرأت هود» "I recited Hūd". They have said this very view regarding the reading of whoever read «صادَ والقرآن» with fatḥa on the dāl, so this may be like it.

The fifth: that the fatḥa is the sign of the genitive, and that by «ألف لام ميم» the sūra is also intended, and that it is sworn by; the particle of the oath was omitted and its effect remained, and it was made a diptote for the reason given above. This view is also stated regarding the reading of whoever read «صادَ» with fatḥa on the dāl, except that the reading there is anomalous (shādhdh) and here it is mass-transmitted (mutawātir). What is apparent is that it is the vowel for the meeting of two unvowelled letters, as is the doctrine of Sībawayh and his followers.

The sixth: Ibn Kaysān said: "The alif of «الله», and every alif with the lām of definiteness, is a disjunctive alif, on a par with «قد»; it was only made connective because of frequent use. So whoever vowels the mīm casts onto it the vowel of the hamza of «الله», which is on a par with the qāf of «قد», and so gave it fatḥa with the fatḥa of the hamza." Makkī transmitted it from him.

On this [view], this is a vowel of transfer from a disjunctive hamza. This doctrine is well known from al-Khalīl ibn Aḥmad, since he believes that definiteness is effected by «أل» as a whole, just as interrogation is effected by «هل» as a whole, and that the hamza is not augmentative; but despite believing that, he agrees that it drops in continuous speech, treating it like the connecting hamza because of frequent use; and for that reason it has been retained in poetic necessity, because necessity returns things to their origins. The discussion of that has a place more suited to it than here.

When Abū al-Baqāʾ transmitted this view without attributing it, he said: "This is valid on the view of whoever made the article of definiteness «أل»" — meaning al-Khalīl, because he is the one well known for this position. The report has already preceded from ʿĀṣim that he reads with a pause on «ميم» and begins «الله لا إله إلا هو», as is apparent from al-Zamakhsharī's account of him; others report from him that he unvowels the mīm and makes the hamza disjunctive without pausing on the mīm, as though treating continuous speech like the pause; and this is what agrees with most of the readers' transmission from him.

ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd — according to what al-Zamakhsharī transmitted — and al-Ruʾāsī — according to what Ibn ʿAṭiyya transmitted — and Abū Ḥaywa read «المِ الله» with kasra on the mīm. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is not acceptable." It is astonishing how he dared [to say this] against ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd, whose standing is well known to him; perhaps he means "it is not accepted from him", i.e. it is not authentically from him. And it seems that al-Akhfash was not aware that it is a reading, for he said: "If the mīm were given kasra for the meeting of two unvowelled letters, and «ألمِ الله» were said, it would be permissible."

Al-Zajjāj said: "This is a mistake by Abū al-Ḥasan [al-Akhfash], because before the mīm there is a yāʾ preceded by kasra, so by right it takes fatḥa for the meeting of two unvowelled letters, because of the heaviness of kasra with yāʾ." Although this is as he said, al-Fārisī championed Abū al-Ḥasan and rejected Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj]'s rejection, saying: "The kasra of the mīm, had it come by way of hearing [from the Arabs], analogy would not repel it; rather it would establish and strengthen it, because the basic [vowel] in vowelling for the meeting of two unvowelled letters is kasra, and it is changed to something else only because of some cause and dislike that arises. So when a thing comes according to its rule, there is no reason to reject it and no room to repel it. And Abū Isḥāq's saying 'what precedes the mīm is a yāʾ preceded by kasra, so by right it takes fatḥa' is refuted by their saying «جَيْرِ» and «كان من الأمر ذَيْتِ وذِيْتِ وكَيْتِ وكِيْتِ» 'such-and-such happened', where the unvowelled letter after the yāʾ was vowelled with kasra, just as it was vowelled after it with fatḥa in «أَيْنَ». And just as fatḥa is permitted after the yāʾ in their saying «أَيْنَ», so kasra is permitted after it, as in their saying «جَيْر». What indicates the permissibility of vowelling with kasra for the meeting of two unvowelled letters in what is preceded by a yāʾ is the permissibility of vowelling it with ḍamma, as in their saying «حيثُ»; and if ḍamma is permitted, kasra is more permissible and easier."

[Translator's note: the source text contains several evident typographical slips — e.g. «بوجب» for «يوجب», «عم المبرد» for «عن المبرد», «منه منا» for «منه هنا», «السكانين» for «الساكنين», «أردوا» for «أرادوا» — which have been translated according to the evidently intended forms.]

semin-durr:48-48.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَيُعَلِّمُهُ}: Nāfiʿ and ʿĀṣim read «ويُعَلِّمُه» with the yāʾ of the absent [third person], and the rest with the nūn of the speaker magnifying himself. On both readings there are several views on the position of this sentence. The first: it is conjoined to «يُبَشِّرُكِ», i.e. "Allah gives you glad tidings of a word, and He will teach that child expressed as 'the word'". The second: it is conjoined to «يَخْلُق», i.e. "Thus Allah creates what He wills, and He will teach him". A group held these two views, among them al-Zamakhsharī and Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī. These two views are apparent on the reading with yāʾ. As for the reading with nūn, these two views are not apparent on it except by interpreting it as a shift (iltifāt) from the pronoun of absence to the pronoun of the speaker, signalling grandeur and magnification. As for conjoining it to «يُبَشِّرُكِ», the Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] considered it very far-fetched. He said: "Because of the long separation between the conjoined element and what it is conjoined to." As for conjoining it to «يَخْلُق», the Shaykh said: "It is conjoined to it, whether it — meaning «يخلق» — is a khabar (predicate) about Allah the Exalted or an explanation of what is before it, if you parse the word «الله» as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and what is before it as the khabar." He means that several views preceded in the iʿrāb of «كذلك الله» in the story of Zakariyyā, among them what he mentioned; so «يعلّمه» is conjoined to «يخلق» under both of the considerations mentioned, since nothing prevents that. On what the Shaykh and others mentioned, the conditional sentence is parenthetical between the conjoined element and what it is conjoined to. The sentence «يعلّمه», on the two preceding views, is in the position of the nominative, because what it is conjoined to is in the position of the nominative.
The third: it is conjoined to «يكلّم», so it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); the implied form is: "He gives you glad tidings of a word, speaking and teaching the Book". Ibn ʿAṭiyya and others permitted this view.
The fourth: it is conjoined to «وجيهاً», because it is interpretable as a noun in the accusative as a ḥāl, as its explanation preceded at His words «ويكلّم». Al-Zamakhsharī permitted this view. The Shaykh considered these last two views — I mean the third and fourth — far-fetched. He said: "Because of the long separation between the conjoined element and what it is conjoined to; the like of it is not found in the speech of the Arabs."
The fifth: it is conjoined to the sentence reported by the saying, namely «كذلك الله يخلق». The Shaykh said: "On both readings it is conjoined to the sentence that is said; that is because the pronoun in His words «قال كذلك» is Allah the Exalted, and the sentence after it is what is said — whether the word «الله» is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is what is before it, or a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is «يخلق», according to what has passed in the iʿrāb of «قال: كذلك الله يفعل ما يشاء». So this is part of what was said to Maryam, by way of making her rejoice and giving her glad tidings of this child whom Allah would bring into being from her."
The sixth: it is resumptive (mustaʾnaf), having no grammatical position. Al-Zamakhsharī, after mentioning that it may be conjoined to «نبشّرك» [Translator's note: so in the source, for «يبشّرك»] or «يخلق» or «وجيهاً», said: "Or it is a speech begun afresh", meaning resumptive.
The Shaykh said: "If he means that it is a resumption of informing from Allah or about Allah, according to the difference between the two readings, then since the wāw is present it must be conjoined to something before it, so it cannot be the beginning of a speech — unless the wāw in «ويعلّمه» is claimed to be redundant (zāʾida), in which case it may properly be the beginning of a speech. And if he means that it is not conjoined to what he mentioned, then he ought to have made clear what it is conjoined to, and that what it is conjoined to is the beginning of a speech, so that the conjoined element would be likewise." I say: this objection is not binding, because making it a resumptive speech does not entail claiming that the wāw is redundant, nor that there must be something it is conjoined to, since the grammarians and the scholars of rhetoric (bayān) have stated explicitly that the wāw may be for resumption, as evidenced by poets using it at the beginnings of their poems without anything preceding to which what follows it could be conjoined; poems are packed with that, and they call it the wāw of resumption. Whoever prohibits that supposes that the poet conjoined his speech to something intended in his mind; but the first is the better known of the two views.
Al-Ṭabarī said: "The reading with yāʾ is conjoined to His words «يخلق ما يشاء», and the reading with nūn is conjoined to His words «نوحيه إليك»." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "This view he expressed on the two readings corrupts the meaning," but Abū Muḥammad [Ibn ʿAṭiyya] did not make clear in what way it corrupts the meaning. [Translator's note: the source prints «أو محمد», evidently for «أبو محمد».] The Shaykh said: "As for the reading with nūn, the corruptness of conjoining it to «نوحيه» is evident in wording and in meaning. In wording, the like of it does not occur in the speech of the Arabs, because of the excessively distant separation, the convolution of the construction and the disharmony of the speech. In meaning, the element conjoined with wāw shares [the ruling of] what it is conjoined to, so the meaning of His words {ذلك مِنْ أَنَبَآءِ الغيب} would become: your being informed, O Muḥammad, of the story of the wife of ʿImrān and her giving birth to Maryam, and Zakariyyā's taking charge of her, and his story of the birth of Yaḥyā to him, and the angels' giving Maryam glad tidings of being chosen and purified — all of that is among the reports of the unseen; We teach him, i.e. We teach ʿĪsā the Book. This is speech whose meaning does not cohere with the meaning of what is before it. As for the reading with yāʾ and conjoining «ويعلّمه» to «يخلق», it does not corrupt the meaning; rather, it is the most fitting and most correct thing on which the conjoining of «ويعلّمه» can be construed, because its wording is near and its meaning sound. We have mentioned its permissibility before. Allah would then be informing Maryam that He, the Exalted, creates strange things the like of which is not customary — just as He created a child for you without a father — and that He, the Exalted, will teach this child whom He creates what He had not taught anyone before him of the Book, the wisdom, the Torah and the Gospel. In this informing there would be the greatest glad tidings for her of this child and a manifestation of his blessing, and that he does not resemble the children of people among the Children of Israel, but differs from them in the origin of his coming into being and in the knowledge that Allah the Exalted teaches him. This appears to me to be the best thing on which the conjoining of «ويعلّمه» can be construed." End of quote.
Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is read with nūn, construing it (ḥamlan) on His words {ذلك مِنْ أَنَبَآءِ الغيب نُوحِيهِ إِلَيكَ}, and it is read with yāʾ, construing it on «يبشّرك»; its position is a ḥāl conjoined to «وجيهاً»." The Shaykh said: "One of them said: «ونعلّمه» with nūn, construing it on «نوحيه». If by 'construing' he means conjoining, nothing is more far-fetched than this analysis; and if by 'construing' he means that it is of the type of shift (iltifāt), then it is correct." I say: it is necessary that by his word "construing" he means the shift and nothing else; he cannot mean conjoining by it, because of his words "its position is a ḥāl conjoined to «وجيهاً»". How could it be right that he intends conjoining it to «نبشّرك» or «نوحيه» while judging that it is conjoined to «وجيهاً»? This could never be right.

semin-durr:62-62.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {إِنَّ هذا لَهُوَ القصص}: it is possible that «هو» is a separating pronoun (faṣl), «القصص» the khabar (predicate) of «إنَّ», and «الحقُّ» its naʿt (adjective). It is possible that «هو» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «القَصَصُ» its khabar, the clause being the khabar of «إنَّ». The reference by «هذا» is to what has been mentioned before of the accounts of ʿĪsā, peace be upon him. It was also said: rather it refers to what comes after it, namely His saying {وَمَا مِنْ إله إِلاَّ الله}. This was judged weak for two reasons. One is that this is not a narrative (qaṣaṣ). The second is that it is joined with a conjunction. Some offered an excuse for the first, saying: if by «القصص» is meant the report, it is valid on this basis, and the implied meaning would be: "the true report is that there is no god but Allah" [Translator's note: the printed text reads «ما من إلا إلا الله», evidently a misprint for «ما من إله إلا الله»]. But the second objection remains and has not been answered.

«القَصَصُ» is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of their saying «قَصَّ فلان الحديثَ يَقُصَّه قَصَّاً وقَصَصَاً» (so-and-so related the story). Its origin is following the track; it is said «فلان خَرَجَ يَقُصُّ أثرَ فلان», i.e. he follows him to know where he went. From this is His saying {وَقَالَتْ لأُخْتِهِ قُصِّيهِ} [al-Qaṣaṣ: 11], i.e. follow his track. Likewise the storyteller (al-qāṣṣ) in speech, because he follows one report after another. Attention has already been drawn to the two readings «لَهْو» with sukūn on the hāʾ and with ḍamma, the former treating it like «عَضُد» [Translator's note: i.e. like «عَضْد» from «عَضُد»].

Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: why is it permissible for the lām to enter the separating pronoun? I say: if it is permissible for it to enter the khabar, then its entering the separating pronoun is more permissible, because it is nearer to the mubtadaʾ than the khabar is, and the lām's origin is to enter the mubtadaʾ."

His saying: {وَمَا مِنْ إله إِلاَّ الله}: two views are possible on it. One is that «من إله» is a mubtadaʾ, with «مِنْ» redundant (zāʾida) in it, and «إلا اللهُ» its khabar, the implied meaning being «ما إله إلا اللهُ»; «مِنْ» was added for comprehensiveness and generality. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«مِنْ» in His saying {وَمَا مِنْ إله إِلاَّ الله} is equivalent to the construction on fatḥa in «لا إله إلا اللهُ» in conveying the meaning of comprehensiveness." I say: we did not derive the comprehensiveness in «لا إله إلا اللهُ» from the construction on fatḥa; rather we derived it from an implied «مِنْ» indicating comprehensiveness. The grammarians stated this explicitly and adduced as evidence its appearing overtly in the poet's saying:

1317 - فقام يذودُ الناسَ عنها بسيفِه ... فقال ألا لا مِنْ سبيلٍ إلى هندِ
(He stood driving people away from her with his sword, and said: Lo, there is no way at all to Hind.)

The second is that the khabar is implied, its implied form being «وما من إلهٍ لنا إلا الله» (there is no god for us except Allah), and «إلا اللهُ» is a badal (substitute) from the position of «من إله» [Translator's note: the printed text reads «مضع», a misprint for «موضع»], since its position is nominative as a mubtadaʾ. In such a case substitution from the word itself is not permissible, lest it entail the redundancy of «مِنْ» in an affirmative context, which is not permissible according to the majority. In such a construction it is permissible to put what follows «إلا» in the accusative as an exception, but it was not read so, though it is permissible in the language. You say «لا إله إلا اللهُ» with the divine name in the nominative as a substitute from the position, and in the accusative as an exception from the latent pronoun in the implied khabar, since the implied form is «لا إله استقر لنا إلا الله» (no god is established for us except Allah).

His saying: {وَإِنَّ الله لَهُوَ العزيز الحكيم} is like His saying {إِنَّ هذا لَهُوَ القصص}.

semin-durr:63-63.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {فَإِن تَوَلَّوْاْ}: it is possible that it is an imperfect verb from which one of the two tāʾs has been dropped [for lightness, in the manner of] the reading {تَنَزَّلُ الملائكة} [al-Qadr: 4] and «تَذَكَّرون». This is supported by the sequence and composition of the discourse in addressing those mentioned before, in His saying «تعالوا», after which He continued addressing them until He said to them: «فإنْ تَوَلَّوا». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is possible that it is future, its implied form being «فإنْ تتولَّوا»; al-Naḥḥās mentioned it, but it is weak, because the prefix of the imperfect is not dropped." I say: this is nothing, because the prefix of the imperfect is dropped in this kind of case without disagreement, and a great number of such cases will come; and they agreed on the dropping in His saying {تَنَزَّلُ الملائكة والروح فِيهَا} [al-Qadr: 4]. It is also possible that it is a past verb, i.e. "if the delegation of Najrān, with whom mutual imprecation was sought, turn away"; on that basis there is iltifāt (a shift of person) in the discourse, since it moves from direct address to the third person.

His saying: {بالمفسدين} is a case of the overt noun occurring in place of the pronoun, to draw attention to the cause requiring the recompense. The original would have been «فإنَّ الله عليمٌ بكم» (Allah knows you) on the first view, and «بهم» (them) on the second.

semin-durr:64-64.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {إلى كَلِمَةٍ}: attached (mutaʿalliq) to «تعالَوا». Here He mentioned the object of «تعالوا», unlike the «تعالَوا» before it, for there He did not mention its object, because the intent was mere approach. It is also possible that it was omitted because it is indicated, its implied form being «تعالوا إلى المباهلة» (come to the mutual imprecation).

The majority read «كَلِمة» with fatḥa on the kāf and kasra on the lām, and this is the original form. Abū al-Sammāl read «كِلْمة» on the pattern of «سِدْرة», and «كَلْمة» like «ضَرْبة»; this has preceded shortly. «كلمةٍ» is explained by what follows it, namely His saying {أَلاَّ نَعْبُدَ}; so what is meant by it is a large amount of speech. This is of the type of using the part while meaning the whole; from it is their calling a whole ode «قافية» (a rhyme), though the rhyme is a part of it. He said:

1318 - أُعَلِّمه الرمايةَ كلَّ يومٍ ... فلمَّا اشْتَدَّ ساعِدُه رماني
وكم عَلَّمْتُه نظمَ القوافي ... فلمَّا قال قافيةً هجاني
(I taught him archery every day, and when his arm grew strong he shot at me; how often I taught him to compose rhymes, and when he composed a qāfiya he satirised me.)

They say «كلمةُ الشهادة» (the word of testimony), meaning: lā ilāha illā Allāh, Muḥammad rasūl Allāh. And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «أصدقُ كلمةٍ قالها شاعر كلمةُ لبيد» ("The truest word a poet has said is the word of Labīd"), meaning his saying:

1319 - ألا كلُّ شيءٍ ما خلا اللهَ باطلُ ... وكلُّ نعيمٍ لا محالةَ زائلُ
(Lo, everything other than Allah is vain, and every bliss must inevitably pass away.)

This is as they name a thing by one of its parts among concrete things, because that part is what is intended of it: they said of the people's lookout (rabīʾa) [Translator's note: printed «ربيبة»; the usual word is «ربيئة»], who watches out for them for what they need, «عَيْن» (an eye), so they applied "eye" to him [Translator's note: the printed text reads «بجزأيه», presumably for «بجزئه», "by its part"]. Some said: the singular has been put in place of the plural, as the poet said:

1320 - بها جِيَف الحَسْرى فأمَّا عِظامُها ... فَبيضٌ وأَمَّا جِلْدُها فَصَلِيبُ
(In it are the carcasses of the exhausted beasts: as for their bones, they are white, and as for their hide [lit. "skin", singular], it is hard.)

It was also said: «الكلمة» was applied to the words because they are bound to one another, so they became equivalent to a single word: if a part of it is impaired, the word is impaired. For the word of tawḥīd, lā ilāha illā Allāh, consists of words in which the intended predication — restricting divinity to Allah — is not complete except by all of them together.

The majority read «سواءٍ» in the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of «كلمة», meaning «عدل» (just). This is indicated by the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [Translator's note: Ibn Masʿūd]: «إلى كلمة عدل», but this is an explanation, not a reading. «سواء» is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun), so in using it as a description there are the three well-known interpretations; for that reason it is not made feminine, just as «عدل» is not made feminine in «امرأة عدل» (a just woman).

Al-Ḥasan read «سواء» in the accusative, and there are two views on it. One is that it is accusative as a maṣdar; al-Zamakhsharī said: "in the sense of «استوت استواءً» (it was level, levelly)", and likewise al-Ḥūfī. The second is that it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), the ḥāl coming from an indefinite noun; Sībawayh stated this explicitly and treated it as analogical, and al-Shaykh [Translator's note: Abū Ḥayyān] said the same, though the well-known view is otherwise. What made its coming from an indefinite noun acceptable here is that description by a maṣdar is contrary to the norm, while the adjective and the ḥāl meet in meaning. It is as though al-Shaykh disparaged the derivation of al-Zamakhsharī and al-Ḥūfī, for he said: "The ḥāl and the adjective meet in meaning, whereas the maṣdar requires implying a governing word and interpreting «سواء» as meaning «استواء»; the better-known usage of «سواء» is in the sense of an active participle, i.e. «مُسْتَوٍ» (level)." I say: so Ibn ʿAbbās explained it, saying: «إلى كلمةٍ مستوية» (to a level word).

His saying: {أَلاَّ نَعْبُدَ}: there are six views on it. The first is that it is a badal (substitute) from «كلمة», a substitute of the whole for the whole. The second is that it is a badal from «سواء»; Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted it, but it is not clear, because what is intended is the described noun, not its adjective, so ascribing the substitution to the described noun is more appropriate. On both of these views, «أنْ» and what lies within its scope are in the position of the genitive. The third is that it is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), the clause being a resumption answering an implied question: when it was said «تعالَوا إلى كلمة», someone said: "What is it?", and it was said: "It is that we worship not …". On these three views, «بين» is accusative by «سواء», an adverbial for it, i.e. the equality occurs in this respect. Zuhayr stated this explicitly when he said:

1321 - أرُونا خطةً لا غيبَ فيها ... يُسَوِّي بيننا فيها السَّواءُ
(Show us a course in which there is nothing hidden, in which equity makes us equal between us.)

The complete pause in that case is at His saying {مِّن دُونِ الله}, because the discourse is bound together in meaning and in grammar. The fourth is that «أن» and what lies within its scope are in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, the khabar being the adverbial before it.

The fifth: Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted that it be the fāʿil (agent) of the adverbial before it. This is only feasible on the view of al-Akhfash, since the adverbial does not rest on anything [Translator's note: i.e. it is not preceded by a negation, interrogative, or a noun it qualifies]. In that case the pause is at «سواء», and then one begins with His saying {بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَكُمْ أَلاَّ نَعْبُدَ}; this is far-fetched in terms of meaning. Then they made this clause an adjective of «كلمة», and this is a mistake, because there is no link between the adjective and the described noun, and implying a returning pronoun is not easy. On this basis, the saying of Abū al-Baqāʾ — "It was said: the speech is complete at «سواء», then He began anew and said {بيننا وبينكم أنْ لا نعبد}, i.e. between us and you is tawḥīd; on this view «أن لا نعبد» is a mubtadaʾ, the adverbial its khabar, and the clause an adjective of «الكلمة»" — is not clear: having made it an adjective, how can he properly say "the speech is complete at «سواء», then He began anew"? Rather, on this parsing the correct view would have been that the clause is resumptive, as has preceded.

The sixth is that «أن لا نعبد» is nominative as the fāʿil of «سواء». Al-Rummānī [Translator's note: printed «الزماني»] held this, for in his view the implied form is: «إلى كلمةُ مُسْتَوفيها بيننا وبينكم عدمُ عبادة غير الله تعالى» [Translator's note: so printed; the sense is «إلى كلمةٍ مُسْتَوٍ فيها …», "to a word in which non-worship of other than Allah is equal between us and you"]. Al-Shaykh said: "Except that it involves implying the link, namely «فيها», and that is weak."

His saying: {فَإِن تَوَلَّوْاْ فَقُولُواْ}: Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is a past verb, and it is not permissible for the implied form to be «فإن تتولوا», because that would corrupt the meaning, since His saying {فَقُولُواْ اشهدوا} is addressed to the believers while «تتولَّوا» would be addressed to the polytheists; in that case no apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) would remain in the speech. The implied form is: «فقولوا لهم» (then say to them)." What he said is very evident.

semin-durr:65-65.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {لِمَ تُحَآجُّونَ}: this is the interrogative «ما», which a preposition has entered, so its alif was dropped; the verification of this has preceded in al-Baqara. The lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to what follows it, and putting it before its governing word is obligatory because it puts into the genitive something that must stand at the head of the sentence. His saying {في إِبْرَاهِيمَ} requires an omitted muḍāf, i.e. «في دينِ إبراهيم وشريعته» (concerning the religion of Ibrāhīm and his law), because there is no disputing about persons themselves.

His saying: {وَمَآ أُنزِلَتِ التوراة}: the evident view is that the wāw is like the one in His saying {لِمَ تَكْفُرُونَ بِآيَاتِ الله وَأَنْتُمْ تَشْهَدُونَ} [Āl ʿImrān: 70] [Translator's note: i.e. a circumstantial wāw], i.e. how do you dispute about his law when the state is that the Torah and the Gospel came later than him? They also permitted it to be a conjunction, but that is not clear. This interrogative is for disapproval and expressing wonder. His saying {إِلاَّ مِن بَعْدِهِ} is attached to «أُنزلت», and it is an emptied exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh).

semin-durr:188-188.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لاَ تَحْسَبَنَّ الذين يَفْرَحُونَ}: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read: «لا يَحْسَبَنَّ … فلا يَحْسَبُنَّهم» with yāʾ in both, and with ḍamma on the bāʾ of «يَحْسَبُنَّهم». [Translator's note: the printed text writes the first verb as «لاتَحْسَبَنَّ», but the description "with yāʾ in both" requires «لا يَحْسَبَنَّ».] The Kufans read with the tāʾ of address and fatḥa on the bāʾ in both together; Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir with the yāʾ of the third person in the first and with address in the second, and fatḥa on the bāʾ in both. It was read irregularly (shādhdh) with the tāʾ of address and ḍamma on the bāʾ in both together. [It was also read with the yāʾ of the third person in both and fatḥa on the bāʾ in both as well; so these are five readings.] [Translator's note: the square brackets are in the printed source.]

As for the reading of Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr, there are five analyses in it. That is because one either makes the first verb attributed to an absent pronoun or to the relative noun. If we make it attributed to an absent pronoun — either the Messenger, upon him be peace, or another — then there are two analyses in the question. The first: «الذين» is the first object, and the second is omitted because the second object of the verb after it indicates it, namely «بمفازة»; the implied form being: let not the Messenger, or any thinker, think those who rejoice to be in safety; so let him not think them to be in safety. So the second verb was attributed to the pronoun of «الذين» [Translator's note: so in the text; on this analysis the second verb has the same absent subject as the first, and the pronoun of «الذين» is its object], and its two objects are the accusative pronoun and «بمفازةٍ».

The second analysis: «الذين» is also the first object, and its second object is «بمفازة», which is pronounced after the second verb; and the object of the second verb is omitted because the object of the first indicates it; the implied form being: let not the Messenger think those who rejoice to be in safety; so let him not think them so; and the governing is as stated. This is very far-fetched, because of the separation [of «بمفازة»] as the second object of the first verb by long speech without need. On these two analyses the fāʾ is conjunctive, and the causality in it is evident.

If we make it attributed to the relative noun, there are three analyses in it. The first of them: the first verb had its two objects omitted for brevity, because the two objects of the second verb indicate them; its implied form being: let not those who rejoice think themselves successful; so let them not think themselves successful — like the saying of the other poet:
1508 - بأيَّ كتابٍ أم بأيةِ سُنَّةٍ ... ترى حُبَّهم عاراً علي وتَحْسَبُ
(By what scripture, or by what sunna, do you see love of them as a shame upon me, and reckon [it so]?)
i.e. and you reckon love of them a shame; he omitted the two objects of the second verb because the two objects of the first indicate them, which is the reverse of the noble verse, where the omission was from the first verb.

The second analysis: the first verb did not need two objects here. Abū ʿAlī [al-Fārisī] said: "«يَحْسَبَنَّ» did not fall on anything, and «الذين» is nominative by it. These verbs sometimes come as void (laghw), in the status of informative clauses, as in the poet's saying:
1509 - وما خِلْتُ أَبْقَى بيننا من مودةٍ ... عِراضُ المَذَاكي المُسْنِفِاتِ القلائِصا
(And I did not suppose — the [raiding] of full-grown steeds, outpacing the young she-camels, has left no affection between us.)
And al-Khalīl said: 'The Arabs say: ما رأيتُ يقول ذلك إلا زيدٌ (I did not see [anyone] saying that except Zayd), and ما ظننته يقول ذلك إلا عمرو (I did not think [anyone] would say that except ʿAmr).'" Abū ʿAlī means that in these places they are cancelled (mulghāh), having no object.

The third: that the first object be omitted, the second being «بمفازة» itself, and «فلا يَحْسَبُنَّهم» an emphasis of the first verb. This is the view of al-Zamakhsharī, for he said after relating this reading: "On the basis that the verb belongs to those who rejoice, and the first object is omitted, with the meaning: «لا يَحْسَبَنَّهم الذين يفرحون بمفازةٍ», meaning: let not those who rejoice think themselves successful; and «فلا يَحْسَبُنَّهم» is an emphasis." End. [Translator's note: the printed text reads «الفعلَ اللذين», evidently for «الفعلَ للذين» (the verb belongs to those who).]

The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "Our refutation of al-Zamakhsharī in his implied form «لا يَحْسَبَنَّهم الذين» has preceded at His saying {لاَ يَحْسَبَنَّ الذين كَفَرُواْ أَنَّمَا نُمْلِي} [Āl ʿImrān: 178], and that this implied form is not valid." I say: that, and the answer to it, has preceded in a long discussion; but it is not at His saying {لاَ يَحْسَبَنَّ الذين كَفَرُواْ أَنَّمَا نُمْلِي}, but at His saying {وَلاَ تَحْسَبَنَّ الذين قُتِلُواْ فِي سَبِيلِ الله} [Āl ʿImrān: 169] in the reading of whoever read it with the yāʾ of the third person; there he refuted him with what he said, and I have answered it, praise be to Allah. I have only pointed out the place so that this discussion is not sought in the place he mentioned and not found.

It may be said, in establishing this third analysis: he deleted from one of the two verbs what he kept the counterpart of in the other. That is, «بمفازة» is the second object of the first verb, deleted from the second verb; and «هم» in «فلا يَحْسَبُنَّهم» is the first object of the second verb, deleted from the first. When you know that, then the second verb, on these three analyses, is an emphasis of the first.

Makkī said: "The second verb is a badal (substitute) of the first." Calling the like of this a badal is open to question, which is not hidden; it is as though he means that it has the status of the repeated, so it returns to the meaning of tawkīd (emphasis). Hence someone said: "The second is repeated by way of badal, tinged with the meaning of emphasis." On these two views — I mean its being an emphasis or a badal — the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), neither conjunctive nor an apodosis.

His saying «فَلاَ يَحْسَبُنَّهُمْ»: its origin is «يَحْسَبُونَنَّهم» with two nūns, the first being the nūn of the indicative and the second for emphasis; its morphology is not hidden from the rules that preceded. Here the verb of a detached [i.e. separate-referent] subject pronoun passes to its attached pronoun; this is specific to the chapter of thinking (ẓann) and to «عَدِمَ» and «فَقَد», as opposed to all other verbs; if you said «أكرمتُني», i.e. "I honoured myself", it would not be permissible; and the place for establishing this is elsewhere. [Translator's note: «المضمر المنفصل» here appears to mean the subject pronoun of the verb; the rule concerns a verb whose subject and object pronouns refer to the same person.]

As for the reading of the Kufans, the two verbs in it are attributed to the pronoun of the one addressed: either the Messenger, upon him be peace, or anyone fit to be addressed. The discussion of the two objects of the two verbs is like the discussion of them in the reading of Abū ʿAmr and Ibn Kathīr, on our view that the first verb is attributed to an absent pronoun. The second verb is an emphasis of the first or a badal of it, and the fāʾ is redundant, as preceded in the analysis of the reading of Abū ʿAmr and Ibn Kathīr on our view that the two verbs are attributed to the relative noun, because the agent in it is one. They cited as proof that the fāʾ is redundant the poet's saying:
1510 - لا تَجْزَعي إنْ مُنْفِساً أهلكتُه ... وإذا هَلَكْتُ فعند ذلك فاجْزَعي
(Do not grieve if I have squandered something precious; but when I perish, then at that time grieve.)
And another says:
1511 - لَمَّا اتَّقى بيدٍ عظيم جِرْمُها ... فتركْتُ ضاحي كَفِّه يَتَذَبْذَبُ
(When he shielded himself with a hand of great bulk, I left the exposed part of his palm dangling.)
i.e. I left. And another's saying:
1512 - حتى تَرَكْتُ العائداتِ يَعُدْنَه ... فيقلن: لا يَبْعَدْ وقلت له: ابعَدِ
(Until I left the visiting women visiting him [in sickness], saying: "May he not perish!" — and I said to him: "Perish!")
However, the redundancy of the fāʾ is not the view of the majority; only al-Akhfash held it.

As for the reading of Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir, with the third person in the first and address in the second, its analysis is that they made the two agents differ. The discussion of it is taken from what preceded: the discussion of the first verb is taken from the discussion of the reading of Abū ʿAmr and Ibn Kathīr, and of the second from the discussion of the reading of the Kufans, as befits it; except that here it is impossible for the second verb to be an emphasis of the first or a badal of it, because their agents differ; so the fāʾ here is conjunctive and nothing else. Abū ʿAlī said in «al-Ḥujja»: "The fāʾ is redundant and the second is a badal of the first"; he said: "This is not a place for conjunction, because the speech is not complete; do you not see that the second object has not yet been mentioned?" This is open to question because the two verbs differ by the difference of their agents.

As for the reading with address in both and ḍamma on the bāʾ in both, the two verbs are attributed to the pronoun of the believers being addressed, and the discussion of the two objects is like the discussion of them in the reading of the Kufans.

As for the reading with the third person and fatḥa on the bāʾ in both, the two verbs are attributed to an absent pronoun, i.e. let not the Messenger, or any thinker, think; the discussion of the two objects of the two verbs is like the discussion in the reading before it. The second of the two verbs is an emphasis or a badal, and the fāʾ is redundant on these two readings because the agent is one.

Al-Nakhaʿī and Marwān ibn al-Ḥakam read: «بما آتَوا» with the long vowel, i.e. [what] they gave. Ubayy read «أُوتوا», passive.

His saying: {مِّنَ العذاب}: there are two analyses in it. The first: it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) something omitted, as a naʿt (adjective) of «مفازة», i.e. in a place of safety being from the punishment, on our making «مفازة» a place, i.e. a place of success. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "because المفازة is a place, and a place [noun] does not govern", meaning: so it cannot be attached to it, but to something omitted as a naʿt of it. However, making it a naʿt is problematic, because المفازة is not described as being from the punishment — unless that omitted item to which the preposition is attached is implied as something specific [so that] the meaning is sound, its implied form being: in a place of safety that saves from the punishment. And in this there is the well-known difficulty, namely that the omitted item in such a case is implied only as general being (kawn muṭlaq).

The second analysis: it is attached to «مفازة» itself, as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of الفوز (escape, success); you say «فزت منه», i.e. I escaped from it. Its being feminine with the tāʾ does no harm, because it is built on it, and it is not the [tāʾ] indicating singularity. So it is like the poet's saying:
1513 - فلولا رجاءُ النصرِ منك ورهبةٌ ... عقابَك قد كانوا لنا كالمَوارِدِ
(Were it not for hope of help from you, and fear of your punishment, they would have been to us like watering-places.)
He made «رهبةٌ» govern «عقابَك», which is an explicit object; so this [case] is all the more fitting. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The implied form would be: so do not think them successful; so the maṣdar is in the place of the active participle." End. If he means an explanation of the meaning, then [very well]; but if he means that the attachment is valid only by this implied form, there is no need for it, since the maṣdar is independent in that, in wording and meaning.

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {نَزَّلَ عَلَيْكَ الكتاب}: the majority read «نَزَّل» with doubling (tashdīd) and «الكتاب» in the accusative. Al-Aʿmash, al-Nakhaʿī and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «نَزَلَ» with the zāy undoubled and «الكتاب» in the nominative. As for the first reading, it has already been stated that this clause may be a khabar (predicate) or may be resumptive (mustaʾnafa). As for the second reading, what is apparent is that the clause in it is resumptive, and it may be a khabar, in which case the returning pronoun (ʿāʾid) is omitted, its implied form being: «نَزَل الكتابُ من عنده» "the Book came down from Him".

His saying: {بالحق}: there are two analyses of it. The first: that the bāʾ is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb before it, the bāʾ then being causal, i.e. "He sent it down because of the truth". The second: that it is attached to something omitted, as a ḥāl (circumstantial): either from the agent, i.e. "He sent it down being in the right", or from the object, i.e. "He sent it down bound up with the truth", as in «جاء بكرٌ بثيابه» "Bakr came with his clothes", i.e. bound up with them.

Makkī said: "The bāʾ is not attached to «نَزَّلَ», because it is already transitive to two objects, one of them by a particle, so it does not extend to a third." What Makkī mentioned is not evident, for a verb extends to its attached elements through various particles according to what is [meant], and it has been stated that the meaning of the bāʾ is causal; so what impediment prevents that?

His saying: {مُصَدِّقاً}: there are several analyses of it. The first: that it is accusative as a ḥāl from «الكتاب»; if it is said that «بالحق» is a ḥāl, this is a second ḥāl according to those who permit multiple ḥāls, and if that is not said, it is a first ḥāl. The second: that it is accusative as a ḥāl by way of substitution (badal) from the position of «بالحق»; that is according to those who forbid multiple ḥāls without conjunction or substitution. The third: that it is accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun latent in «بالحق», if we make it a ḥāl, because it then bears a pronoun, as it stands in place of the ḥāl that bears it; it would then be an interlocking ḥāl (ḥāl mutadākhila), i.e. a ḥāl from a ḥāl. On all these views it is a confirmatory ḥāl (ḥāl muʾakkida), because it cannot be otherwise, so transience is inconceivable in it. It is a parallel of his saying:

1158 - أنا ابنُ دارةَ معروفاً بها نسبي ... وهَلْ بدارَةَ يا لَلْناسِ مِنْ عارِ
(I am the son of Dāra, my lineage being known by her — and is there, O people, any shame in Dāra?)

His saying: {لِّمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ} is the object of «مصدِّقا»; the lām was added in the object to strengthen the governing word, because it is secondary [in governance], being an active participle, as in His saying, the Exalted: {فَعَّالٌ لِّمَا يُرِيدُ} [Hūd: 107]. We claimed that only because this root is transitive by itself.

His saying: {التوراة والإنجيل}: people differ about these two words: do derivation and morphological analysis enter them, or do they not enter them because they are foreign (aʿjamī)? A group, such as al-Zamakhsharī and others, held the second, saying: because these two words are Hebrew names for these two noble books. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The strained effort to derive them from «الوَرْي» and «النَّجْل», and to weigh them on the patterns tafʿila and ifʿīl, is valid only after they are established as Arabic." [The Shaykh said: "His words are correct, except that there is a point to be added, namely his saying 'tafʿila': he did not mention the doctrine of the Basrans,] which is that its pattern is fawʿala, nor did he point out whether tafʿila has kasra or fatḥa on the ʿayn." I say: He did not need to point it out because both are well known; he only mentioned what is unusual.

What supports al-Zamakhsharī's statement that it is foreign is what al-Wāḥidī transmitted, namely that «التوراة», «الإنجيل» and «الزبور» are Syriac and they Arabized them. He said: "For that reason they say for them in Syriac: «تُوري ايكليونُ زَفوتا»", and they Arabized them into what you see.

Then those who hold that they are derived differ. Some said: «التَوْرَاة» is derived from their saying «ورِي الزَّنْدُ» "the fire-stick gave fire", when it is struck and fire appears from it. One says «وَرِيَ الزَّنْدُ» and «أَوْرَيْتُه أنا» "I made it give fire". The Exalted said: {أَفَرَأَيْتُمُ النار التي تُورُونَ} [al-Wāqiʿa: 71]; so its triliteral form is intransitive and its quadriliteral form is transitive. The Exalted said: {فالموريات قَدْحاً} [al-ʿĀdiyāt: 2]. One also says «وَرَيْتُ بكل زِنادي» "I struck fire with all my fire-sticks", where the triliteral is used transitively; but al-Māzinī claims that one does not go beyond this expression with it, i.e. one does not draw analogies from it so as to say, for example, «وَرَيْتُ النارَ». Once that is established: since the Torah contains light and illumination by which one is brought out of error [into] guidance, just as one is brought by light out of darkness into light, this Book was named «التوراة». This is the view of al-Farrāʾ, and it is the doctrine of the majority of people.

Others said: rather, it is derived from «وَرَّيْتُ في كلامي» "I spoke allusively", from «التورية», which is indirect allusion (taʿrīḍ). In the hadith: «كان إذا أراد سفراً وَرَّى بغيره» "When he intended a journey, he would allude to another". The Torah was named thus because most of it is intimations and allusions. This was the view of al-Muʾarrij al-Sadūsī and a group.

Regarding its pattern there are three views. The first, which is the view of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, is that its pattern is fawʿala; words of this pattern are attested, such as «الدَّوْخَلة», «القَوْصرة», «الدَّوْسَرة» and «الصَّوْمَعَة». The original is «وَوْرَيَة» with two wāws, because it is either from «وَرِي الزَّنْدُ» or from «وَرَيْتُ في كلامي». The first wāw was changed into a tāʾ, and the weak letter was vowelled with what precedes it having fatḥa, so it was changed into an alif, and the word became «تَوْرَاة» as you see. It was written with yāʾ as an indication of the origin, just as it was given imāla (inclination toward i) for that reason. The Arabs have substituted tāʾ for wāw in [other] words, such as «تَوْلَج», «تَيْقور», «تُخَمَة», «تُكَأَة», «تُراث», «تُجاه» and «تُكْلان», from «الوُلوج», «الوَقار», «الوَخَامة», «الوِكاء», «الوِراثة», «الوَجْه» and «الوَكالة». A parallel of the change of wāw into tāʾ in «التوراة» is its change also in their word for what a woman sees in her purity after menstruation: «التَّرِيَّة»; it is faʿīla from the word «الوراء», because it is seen after the yellowness and the turbidity.

The second, which is the view of al-Farrāʾ, is that its pattern is tafʿila with kasra on the ʿayn; then the kasra was changed into fatḥa, which is a dialect of Ṭayyiʾ: they say «ناصَاة» for «الناصية», and «بَقَى» for «بَقِي». The poet said:

1159 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... بحِرْبٍ كناصاة الأغَرِّ المُشَهَّرِ
(… with a war [or: spear] like the forelock of the famous white-blazed [horse].)

Another said:

1160 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . .
نفوساً بُنَتْ على الكَرَمِ
(… souls built upon nobility.)

And al-Farrāʾ recited:

1161 - وما الدنيا بباقاةٍ علينا ... وما حيٌّ على الدنيا بباقٍ
(This world will not remain for us, nor will any living being remain in this world.)

The Basrans rejected this in two ways. The first: that this form — I mean the form tafʿila — is very rare, unlike fawʿala, which is frequent, so construing it on the more frequent is preferable. The second: that it entails the addition of the tāʾ at the beginning, and the tāʾ is added at the beginning only in places of which this is not one; unlike its being changed [from wāw] at the beginning of a word, which is established. That is because when a wāw occurs at the beginning, it is changed either into a hamza, as in «أُجوه», «أُقِّتَتْ», «أَحَدَ», «أَناة», «إشاح» and «إعاء» for «وجوه», «وُقِّتَتْ», «وَحَدَ», «وَنَاة», «وِشاح» and «وِعاء»; or into a tāʾ, as in «تُجاه» and «تُخَمة» … etc. So following what is familiar is preferable to following what is unfamiliar.

The third: that its pattern is tafʿala with fatḥa on the ʿayn; this is the doctrine of the Kufans, just as they say «تَتْفَلَة» with fatḥa for «تَتْفُلة» with ḍamma. There is no need for this, and it is also a claim without proof.

Abū ʿAmr, al-Kisāʾī, and Ibn ʿĀmir in the transmission of Ibn Dhakwān pronounced «التوراة», wherever it occurs in the Quran, with full imāla; Ḥamza, and Warsh from Nāfiʿ, pronounced it with intermediate imāla (bayna bayna); there is disagreement in the transmission from Qālūn: intermediate imāla and fatḥ are both transmitted from him; and the rest read it with fatḥ only. The rationale of the imāla, if we say that its alif is changed from a yāʾ, is evident; and if we say that it is foreign without derivation, the rationale of the imāla is the resemblance of its alif to the alif of femininity, in that it occurs as the fourth letter. So the cause of its imāla is either the change [from yāʾ] or the resemblance to the alif of femininity.

«الإنجيل»: it has been said that it is ifʿīl, like «إجْفيل». Regarding its pattern there are views. The first: that it is derived from «النَّجْل», which is the water that seeps from the ground and comes out of it; and from it is «النَّجْل» for the offspring. It was named «الإنجيل» because it is extracted from the Preserved Tablet. It has been said: from «النَّجْل» meaning the origin, and from it is «النَّجْل» for the parent; so it is one of the words with opposite meanings (aḍdād), since it is applied to both the offspring and the parent. Al-Aʿshā said:

1162 - أَنْجَبَ أيَّامُ والِداهُ به ... إذ نَجَلاه فنِعْمَ ما نَجَلا
(Noble were the days when his two parents begot him — how excellent was what they begot!)

It has been said: from «النَّجَل», which is wideness; and from it is «العَيْنُ النجلاءُ» "the wide eye", because of its wideness. The Gospel was named thus because in it there is a latitude that was not in the Torah, since things that had been forbidden were made lawful in it.

It has been said: it is derived from «التَناجل», which is mutual contention; one says «تَنَاجل الناسُ», i.e. they contended. The Gospel was named thus because of people's disagreement about it. Abū ʿAmr al-Shaybānī said this.

The majority read «إنجيل» with kasra on the hamza. Al-Ḥasan read it with fatḥa. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "This indicates that it is foreign, because «أفعيل» with fatḥa on the hamza does not exist among the patterns of the Arabs." I say: unlike «إفعيل» with kasra, which exists, as in «إِجْفيل», «إخْريط» and «إصْليت».

Al-Zamakhsharī distinguished between «نَزَّل» and «أنزل», as is his habit, saying: "If you say: Why was it said «نَزَّل الكتابَ» but «وأنزل التوراة والإِنجيل»? I say: Because the Quran came down in instalments, while the two [earlier] Books came down all at once." The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "The rejection of this view has already preceded in al-Baqara, [where it was shown] that transitivization by doubling indicates neither multiplicity nor instalments. Both «أَنْزَل» and «نَزَّل» have come in the Quran; the Exalted said: {وَأَنْزَلْنَا إِلَيْكَ الذكر} [al-Naḥl: 44] and {نَزَّلَ عَلَيْكَ الكتاب} [Āl ʿImrān: 3]. What indicates that they have one meaning is the reading of whoever read the occurrences of «يُنَزِّلُ» with doubling in the undoubled form, except what was excepted. Had one of them indicated instalments and the other descent all at once, the reports would contradict each other, which is impossible." I say: Al-Wāḥidī preceded al-Zamakhsharī to this very distinction.

semin-durr:191-191.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {الذين يَذْكُرُونَ}: there are five analyses in it. The first of them: it is a naʿt (adjective) of «أُولِي», so it is genitive. The second: it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. they are those who. The third: it is accusative by an implied «أعني» (I mean). These two analyses are called cutting off (qaṭʿ), and that has preceded many times. The fourth: it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, its implied form being: they say: our Lord; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. The fifth: it is a badal (substitute) of «أُولي»; Makkī mentioned it. The first of the analyses is the best.

And {قِيَاماً وَقُعُوداً} are two ḥāls (circumstantial) from the agent of «يَذْكُرون». And {وعلى جُنُوبِهِمْ} is also a ḥāl, so it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) something omitted; the meaning is: they remember Him standing, sitting and lying down. So He conjoined the interpreted ḥāl to the explicit one — the reverse of the other verse, namely His saying {دَعَانَا لِجَنبِهِ أَوْ قَاعِداً أَوْ قَآئِماً} [Yūnus: 12], where He conjoined the explicit one to the interpreted one. «قياماً» and «قعوداً» are plurals of «قائم» and «قاعد». It has also been permitted that they be maṣdars (verbal nouns), in which case they are interpreted in the sense of "possessors of standing and sitting"; and there is no need for this.

His saying: {وَيَتَفَكَّرُونَ}: there are two analyses in it. The more evident of them: it is conjoined to the ṣila (relative clause), so it has no grammatical position. The second: it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, conjoined to «قياماً», i.e. they remember Him, reflecting. If it is said: this is an affirmative imperfect, so how did the wāw enter upon it? The answer is that this is the wāw of conjunction, and what is forbidden is only the wāw of the ḥāl.

And «خَلْق» has two analyses. The first: it is a maṣdar on its original [meaning], i.e. they reflect on the making of these wondrous created things; it is then a maṣdar annexed to its object. The second: it is in the sense of the object, i.e. on what is created of the heavens and the earth; and its annexation is, in meaning, to the container (ẓarf), i.e. they reflect on what Allah has deposited in these two containers of stars and other things. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "And it may be in the sense of the created, and it is then of the annexation of a thing to what it is in meaning." This is incoherent speech, since a thing is not annexed to itself, and whatever suggests that is interpreted [otherwise].

His saying: «ربَّنا»: this clause is in the position of the accusative by an omitted saying, its implied form being: they say. The clause of saying has two analyses. The more evident: it is a ḥāl from the agent of «يتفكرون», i.e. they reflect, saying: our Lord. If we parse «يتفكرون» as a ḥāl as preceded, then the two ḥāls are nested (mutadākhila). The second analysis: it is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of «الذين», on our view that it is a mubtadaʾ, as reported earlier from Abū al-Baqāʾ.

And «هذا» in His saying {مَا خَلَقْتَ هَذا} points to the creation (الخَلْق) if the created is meant by it. Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted, while it is pointed to by «هذا», that it be a maṣdar in its [original] state, not in the sense of the created; this is open to question. Or [it points] to the heavens and the earth, even though they are two things each of which is a plural, because they are interpreted as: this wondrous creation; or because they are in the sense of a plural, so they are pointed to as a plural word is pointed to. [Translator's note: so in the text; the point appears to be that «هذا» is singular though it refers to two things.]

His saying: {بَاطِلاً}: regarding its accusative there are five analyses. The first: a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. a vain creating; it has preceded that Sībawayh makes the like of this a ḥāl from the pronoun of that maṣdar. The second: it is a ḥāl from the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), which is «هذا». The third: it is on the dropping of a genitive-governing particle, namely the bāʾ; the meaning being: You did not create them in vain, but with truth and power. [Translator's note: the printed text reads «خلتقهما», a misprint for «خلقتهما».] The fourth: it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), since «فاعِل» sometimes comes as a maṣdar, like العاقبة and العافية. The fifth: it is a second object of «خَلَق»; they said: «خلق», when it is in the sense of «جعل» that takes two objects, takes two objects. This is not known among the scholars of Arabic; rather what is known is that «جَعَلَ», when it is in the sense of «خَلَقَ», takes one object only. The best of these parsings is that it be a ḥāl from «هذا», and it is a ḥāl that cannot be dispensed with, because if it were deleted the speech would be defective; it is like His saying {وَمَا خَلَقْنَا السماوات والأرض وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا لاَعِبِينَ} [al-Dukhān: 38].

And {سُبْحَانَكَ}: its parsing has preceded, and it is parenthetical between His saying «ربنا» and His saying «فَقِنا». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The fāʾ entered for the meaning of requital (jazāʾ); the implied form being: when we have declared You transcendent, or declared You one, then protect us." There is no need for this; rather the causation in it is evident: from their saying {رَبَّنَآ مَا خَلَقْتَ هَذا بَاطِلاً سُبْحَانَكَ} resulted their request for protection from the Fire. It is also said: it is for ordering the request upon the meaning of the verb contained in «سبحان», i.e. glory be to You, so protect us. And whoever held that it is for ordering upon what the vocative contains went far [from the mark].

semin-durr:192-192.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مَن تُدْخِلِ}: «مَنْ» is conditional, an advanced object, necessarily advanced because it has the head of the sentence; and «تُدْخِل» is jussive (majzūm) by it. And {فَقَدْ أَخْزَيْتَهُ} is its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). Abū al-Baqāʾ related from some two strange views. The first: that «مَنْ» be accusative by an implied verb explained by His saying «فقد أَخْزَيْتَه». This is a mistake, because among the conditions of ishtighāl (preoccupation) is the validity of the explaining [verb] having power over what is accusative; and the apodosis does not govern what is before the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), because it does not precede the condition. The second: that «مَنْ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the condition and its apodosis are the khabar (predicate) of this mubtadaʾ. These two analyses are a mistake; and Allah knows best. On all the views, this conditional clause is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of «إنَّ».

One says خَزَيْتُه and أَخْزَيْتُه, as triliteral and quadriliteral, and the quadriliteral is more frequent. خَزِيَ الرجلُ يَخْزَى خِزْياً when he is disgraced, and خَزاية when he is ashamed; so the verb is one, and it is distinguished only by the maṣdar (verbal noun), as preceded.

His saying: {وَمَا لِلظَّالِمِينَ مِنْ أَنْصَارٍ}: «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida), because the two conditions are present. Regarding the noun it governs there are two analyses. The first: it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the preposition-phrase before it; advancing it here is permissible, not obligatory, because the negation is what licenses [the indefinite], and what made its advancing good is that its mubtadaʾ is a verse-end (fāṣila). The second: it is a fāʿil (agent) of the preposition-phrase before it, because it relies on the negation; and this is permissible according to all.

semin-durr:66-66.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {هاأنتم هؤلاء}: discussion of this verse involves difficulty and complexity, so for that reason it requires extended treatment. Let us begin first by establishing its readings and explaining its meaning, since the i'rab depends on that. So I say: the readers fall into four grades on it. The first grade is that of the Kufans, Ibn ʿĀmir, and al-Bazzī from Ibn Kathīr: «ها أنتم» with an alif after the hāʾ and a fully pronounced hamza after it. The second grade is that of Abū ʿAmr and Qālūn from Nāfiʿ: with an alif after the hāʾ and a hamza after it eased to the intermediate sound (bayna bayna). The third grade is that of Warsh, who has two ways: one with a hamza eased bayna bayna after the hāʾ without an alif between them; the second with a clear alif after the hāʾ without any hamza at all. The fourth grade is that of Qunbul, with a fully pronounced hamza after the hāʾ without an alif.

As for the meaning: Qatāda, al-Suddī, al-Rabīʿ and a large group said: what they have knowledge of is their religion, which they found in their books and whose soundness was established for them; and what they have no knowledge of is the law of Ibrāhīm and what he was upon, which is not in their books, which their messengers did not bring them, and whose contemporaries they were not so as to know his religion; so their disputing about it is mere obstinacy and arrogance. It was also said: what they have knowledge of is the affair of our Prophet Muḥammad ﷺ, because it is present with them in their books with his description, and what they have no knowledge of is the affair of Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "He means: there you are, these foolish persons; and the explanation of your foolishness and the paucity of your minds is that you have argued [Translator's note: printed «جادلم», a misprint for «جادلتم»] about what you have knowledge of, of what the Torah and the Gospel speak of; so why do you dispute about what you have no knowledge of, and of which your Book does not speak, namely the religion of Ibrāhīm?"

People differed about this hāʾ. Some said: it is the «ها» of alerting (tanbīh) that enters demonstratives; separation between it and demonstratives by detached nominative pronouns is frequent, as in «ها أنت ذا قائماً», «ها نحن», and «ها هم هؤلاء قائمون»; and it is sometimes repeated with the demonstrative after entering the pronouns, for emphasis, as in this verse. Separation by other than that is rare, as in his saying:

1322 - تَعَلَّمَنْ هالعمرُ الله ذا قَسَماً ... قاقدِرْ بذَرْعِك وانظرْ أينَ تنْسَلِكُ
(Know well — ha, by the life of Allah, this is an oath — so measure by your own reach and look where you are going.) [Translator's note: «قاقدر» is as printed; the known form is «فاقدر»]

And al-Nābigha said:

1323 - ها إنَّ تا عِذْرَةٌ إن لا تكن نَفَعَتْ ... فإنَّ صاحبَها قد تاهَ في البلد
(Lo, this is an excuse; if it has not availed, then its owner has gone astray in the land.)

Others said: it is substituted for the interrogative hamza, the original being «أأنتم», and it is an interrogative of disapproval. Substitution of hāʾ for hamza is frequent, even though it is not analogical: they said «هَرَقْت», «هَرَحْت» and «هَبَرْت» [Translator's note: for «أَرَقْت», «أَرَحْت», «أَبَرْت»]. This is the view of Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, Abū al-Ḥasan al-Akhfash and a group, and Abū Jaʿfar [Translator's note: al-Naḥḥās] considered it good. But it is open to question in that this has not been established for the interrogative hamza: it has not been heard from them «هَتَضْرِبُ زيداً» in the sense of «أتضرب زيداً» (do you hit Zayd?). If that is not established, how can this be construed on it? This is the sense of the objection al-Shaykh [Translator's note: Abū Ḥayyān] raised against these imams. But once substitution of hāʾ for hamza is established, the matter is easy, and no regard is paid to whether it is an interrogative hamza or something else.

This — I mean its being an interrogative hamza replaced by hāʾ — is evident on the reading of Qunbul and Warsh, because they do not insert an alif between the hāʾ and the hamza of «أنتم»; for the insertion of the alif is only due to the heaviness of two successive hamzas, and when the hamza was replaced by hāʾ the heaviness was removed in pronunciation, so a separating alif was not needed. Substitution of hāʾ for the interrogative hamza has indeed occurred; the poet said:

1324 - وأتَى صواحِبُها يَقُلْنَ: هذا الذي ... مَنَحَ المودَة غيرَنا وجَفانا
(And her companions came, saying: Is this the one who granted his affection to others than us and shunned us?)

meaning «أذا الذي». Making it, on their reading, the «ها» of alerting is weak, because the dropping of its alif has not been preserved: one does not say «هذا زيد» with the alif of «ها» dropped [Translator's note: i.e. pronounced «هَذا» without the long ā] — so it was said. I say: Ibn ʿĀmir dropped it in three places, except that he gave ḍamma to the remaining hāʾ after dropping the alif; he read in continuous recitation {ياأيه الساحر} [al-Zukhruf: 49], {أَيُّهَ المؤمنون} [verse 31] in al-Nūr, and {أَيُّهَ الثقلان} [verse 31] in al-Raḥmān. But he did that only in following the script, because the alif was dropped in the written text of the Syrian copy of the Muṣḥaf in these three. In sum, the dropping of the alif of the «ها» of alerting is established.

As for those who keep the alif between the hāʾ and the hamza of «أنتم», the evident view is that «ها» is for alerting, and it is weak that it be a substitute for the interrogative hamza, because of what preceded, namely that the alif is only inserted on account of heaviness, and the heaviness has been removed by replacing the hamza with hāʾ. Some said: "What reflection requires is that «ها» in the reading of the Kufans, al-Bazzī and Ibn Dhakwān be for alerting, because the alif is present in their reading and it is not their practice to separate two hamzas by an alif; and that in the reading of Qunbul and Warsh it be substituted for a hamza, because Qunbul reads with a hamza after the hāʾ, and had «ها» been for alerting he would have brought an alif after the hāʾ. He did not ease the hamza, as he eased it in «أأنذرتهم» and the like, only because replacing the first with hāʾ made that unnecessary for him; and because Warsh did in it what he did in «أأنذرتهم» and the like, easing the hamza and not inserting the alif; and it is as though the reason for his reading with the alif is construing it as substitution, like the second way in «أأنذرتهم» and the like.

As for those other than the ones mentioned — namely Abū ʿAmr, Qālūn and Hishām — it is possible that «ها» is for alerting, and possible that it is a substitute for the interrogative hamza. As for the first way: because the «ها» of alerting entered «أنتم», Hishām pronounced the hamza fully, as he pronounced it fully in «هؤلاء» and the like, while Qālūn and Abū ʿAmr lightened it because it became medial through the particle of alerting entering it, and lightening a medial hamza is strong. As for the second way, the hāʾ is a substitute for the interrogative hamza, because they separate two hamzas by an alif; so Abū ʿAmr and Qālūn are following their own principle in inserting the alif and easing, and Hishām his own principle in inserting the alif and full pronunciation. The second way, namely easing [Translator's note: so printed], was not read, because replacing the first hamza with hāʾ makes it unnecessary."

Others said: "It is possible that «ها» in the reading of all of them is substituted for a hamza, and possible that it is the one of alerting that entered «أنتم»"; Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī, al-Mahdawī and Makkī mentioned this, among others. As for the possibility of these two ways in the reading of Abū ʿAmr, Qālūn from Nāfiʿ, and Hishām from Ibn ʿĀmir, its explanation and clarification have preceded. As for their possibility in the reading of the others, I say: as for the Kufans, al-Bazzī and Ibn Dhakwān, the explanation of «ها» being for alerting in their reading has preceded. The explanation of its being a substitute for the hamza in their reading is that the original is «أأنتم», and they separated with the alif according to the dialect of the one who said:

1325 - . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . أاأنت أَمْ أُمُّ سالمِ
(… is it you, or Umm Sālim?)

and they paid no attention to the replacement of the first hamza by hāʾ, because the substitution in it is accidental. Even though separation is not their practice, they combined the two dialects. As for the explanation of «ها» being a substitute for the hamza in the reading of Qunbul and Warsh, it has preceded. As for the explanation of its being for alerting in their reading even though there is no alif in it, it is that the alif was dropped because of frequent use; and on the view of one who substitutes, like Warsh, one of the two alifs was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescents.

Abū Shāma said: "I say: the better view for this word in all its readings is that «ها» is for alerting, because if we made it a substitute for a hamza, that hamza would be an interrogative hamza, whereas «ها أنتم», wherever it has come in the Qurʾān, has come only for statement, not for question. Nothing prevents this except the easing of those who ease and the dropping of those who drop. As for the easing, its likening to His saying {لأَعْنَتَكُمْ} [al-Baqara: 220] and the like has preceded. As for the dropping, he would say: «ها» is like «أَما», both being particles of alerting, and the permissibility of dropping the alif of «أما» is established, so likewise the dropping of the alif of «ها»; on that basis is their saying «أمَ واللهِ لأفعلن» (lo, by Allah, I will do it). The Basrans construed their saying «هَلُمَّ» as originally «هالمَّ», then the alif of «ها» was dropped; so likewise «ها أنتم»." I say: these are good words, except that his saying "«ها أنتم» wherever it has come is a statement, not a question" is not conceded; rather that is possible, and a question is possible. End.

Al-Farrāʾ also mentioned here an inquiry concerning shortening and lengthening. He said: "Whoever keeps the alif in «ها» and holds it to be for alerting, and whose practice is to shorten in the separated case (al-munfaṣil), then the analogy for him here is to shorten the alif, whether he pronounces the hamza fully or eases it. As for whoever makes it for alerting and whose practice is lengthening in the separated case, or who makes the hāʾ a substitute for an interrogative hamza, the analogy for him is to lengthen, whether he pronounces the hamza fully or eases it." As for Warsh, two ways have preceded from him: replacing the hamza of «أنتم» with an alif, and easing it bayna bayna; when he replaces, he lengthens, and when he eases, he shortens. This suffices for what concerns the readings and the branching of the readers' practices on them; they have said more than this, but this is not its place.

When you have understood all that preceded, there are several views on the i'rab of this verse. The first: «أنتم» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «هؤلاء» its khabar (predicate), and the clause «حاججتم» is a resumptive clause explaining the first clause, meaning: you are these foolish persons, and the explanation of your foolishness and the paucity of your minds is that you have argued about what you have knowledge of, of what the Torah and the Gospel speak of; so why do you dispute about what you have no knowledge of? Al-Zamakhsharī mentioned that.

The second: «أنتم هؤلاء» is a mubtadaʾ and khabar, and the clause «حاجَجْتم» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). This is indicated by the Arabs' explicitly keeping the ḥāl in its place in their saying «ها أنا ذا قائماً» (here I am, standing); in their view this ḥāl is one of the necessary ḥāls which the speech cannot do without.

The third: «أنتم هؤلاء» is also as preceded, but «هؤلاء» here is a relative noun that is not complete except with a ṣila (relative clause) and a returning pronoun [Translator's note: the printed text reads «بصفة», presumably for «بصلة»], these being the clause «حاجَجْتُم». Al-Zamakhsharī mentioned it; this is only tenable according to the Kufans, its implied form being «ها أنتم الذين حاجَجْتُم» (there you are, the ones who disputed).

The fourth: «أنتم» is a mubtadaʾ, «حاججتم» its khabar, and «هؤلاء» a vocative. This too is only tenable according to the Kufans, because the vocative particle is not dropped from demonstratives; but the Kufans permitted it and recited:

1326 - إنَّ الأُولى وُصِفوا قومي لهم فبِهِمْ ... هذا اعتصِمْ تَلْقَ مَنْ عاداكَ مَخذولا
(Those who have been described are my people; [it is] theirs, so with them — O you — take refuge, and you will find whoever is hostile to you forsaken.)

meaning «يا هذا اعتصم», and the saying of another:

1327 - لا يَغُرَّنْكُمُ أولاءِ من القو ... مِ جُنوحٌ للسِّلْمِ فَهْو خِداعُ
(Let not — O you there — an inclination to peace on the part of the people deceive you, for it is a trick.)

meaning «يا أولاء».

The fifth: «هؤلاء» is accusative by specification (ikhtiṣāṣ) with an implied verb, «أنتم» a mubtadaʾ and «حاجَجْتم» its khabar, the clause of specification being parenthetical.

The sixth: it is on the omission of a muḍāf, its implied form being «ها أنتم مثل هؤلاء» (there you are, like these), the clause after it explaining the point of resemblance, or being a ḥāl.

The seventh: «أنتم» is a fronted khabar and «هؤلاء» a postponed mubtadaʾ.

These seven views have been mentioned before, together with those to whom they are attributed and the refutation of some who held some of them, in a way that makes repeating it unnecessary, in Sūrat al-Baqara at His saying {ثُمَّ أَنْتُمْ هؤلاء تَقْتُلُونَ} [al-Baqara: 85]; I have repeated it only as a reminder, so do turn to it.

His saying: {فِيمَا لَيْسَ لَكُمْ بِهِ عِلْمٌ}: «ما» may mean «الذي», or be an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective; it may not be maṣdariyya, because the pronoun refers back to it, and it is a particle according to the majority. «لكم» may be a fronted khabar and «علم» a postponed mubtadaʾ, the clause being the ṣila of «ما» or its adjective.
