Were it not for these meanings which the scholars drew out and understood from Allah the Exalted, the mere statement of the laysa-clause would have no meaning, since everyone knows that the male is not like the female.
His words: {وَإِنِّي سَمَّيْتُهَا مَرْيَمَ}: this clause is conjoined to His words {إِنِّي وَضَعْتُهَآ} on the reading of whoever put a ḍamma on the tāʾ in His words «وضَعْتُ»; so it and what precedes it are in the position of the accusative by the verb "said", the implied form being: she said: I have delivered her; and she said: and Allah knows best what I delivered; and she said: and the male is not like the female; and she said: I have named her Maryam. On the reading of whoever made the tāʾ vowelless or gave it a kasra, «إني سَمَّيْتُها» is likewise conjoined to «إني وضعتُها», and He has separated the two conjoined clauses by two parenthetical clauses, as in the words of the Exalted {وَإِنَّهُ لَقَسَمٌ لَّوْ تَعْلَمُونَ عَظِيمٌ} [al-Wāqiʿa: 76]; al-Zamakhsharī said this.
The Shaykh said: "What he mentioned, that they are two parenthetical clauses, is not necessary, because it is possible that {وَلَيْسَ الذكر كالأنثى} in this reading is part of her words, the parenthesis being a single clause, just as it was part of her words in the reading of whoever read «وضعْتُ» with ḍamma on the tāʾ. Indeed, this ought to be the necessary view, since its being part of her words is established in that reading, and because there is disagreement about two clauses being parenthetical: the position of Abū ʿAlī is that two clauses are not inserted parenthetically. Moreover, his likening these two clauses, by which on his claim he made a parenthesis between the conjoined and what it is conjoined to, to His words {وَإِنَّهُ لَقَسَمٌ لَّوْ تَعْلَمُونَ عَظِيمٌ} is not a likening that matches the verse, because there two clauses were not inserted between a requiring and a required element; rather a single clause was inserted between the oath, which is {فَلاَ أُقْسِمُ بِمَوَاقِعِ النجوم}, and its answer, which is {إِنَّهُ لَقُرْآنٌ كَرِيمٌ} — namely His words {وَإِنَّهُ لَقَسَمٌ لَّوْ تَعْلَمُونَ عَظِيمٌ}. But within the parenthetical clause, between some of its parts and others, there came a parenthesis by a clause, namely His words «لو تعلمون», inserted between the described noun «لقسمٌ» and its adjective «عظيم». So this is a parenthesis within a parenthesis, and it is not a separation by two parenthetical clauses as in His words {والله أَعْلَمُ بِمَا وَضَعَتْ وَلَيْسَ الذكر كالأنثى}." I say: haggling over such things is of no great use. His statement "it is not a separation by two parenthetical clauses" is not conceded; rather it is a separation by two parenthetical clauses, and its coming as a parenthesis within a parenthesis does not harm that nor impair his statement "he separated by two clauses".
«سَمَّى» is transitive to two objects: to one of them by itself and to the other by a preposition, which may be omitted. You say: سمَّيت ابني زيداً ("I named my son Zayd"), the origin being: يزيد «[Translator's note: so in the text; evidently بزيد, "with Zayd"]». The poet combined the origin and the derived form:
1243 - وسُمِّيْتَ كَعْباً بشَرِّ العِظَامِ ... وكان أبوكَ يُسَمَّى الجُعَلْ
(You were named Kaʿb, after the worst of bones, and your father used to be named al-Juʿal, the dung beetle.)
i.e.: named with al-Juʿal. The discussion of «مريم», its derivation, its meaning and its being irregular in relation to its counterparts, has preceded.
His words: {وِإِنِّي أُعِيذُهَا}: conjoined to «إني سَمَّيْتُها». Here the khabar of «إنَّ» was brought as an imperfect verb to indicate her asking for the seeking of refuge to continue without interruption — unlike her words «وضَعْتُها» and «سَمَّيْتُها», where the two khabars were brought as past verbs because they were completed. And what refuge is sought in (Allah) was put before the conjoined element out of concern for it.
Nāfiʿ gave a fatḥa to the yāʾ of the speaker before this hamza with ḍamma, and likewise every yāʾ followed by a hamza with ḍamma, except in two places where all agreed on its being vowelless: {بعهدي أُوفِ} [al-Baqara: 40] and {آتوني أُفْرِغْ} [al-Kahf: 96]. The rest are ten places, the one in this sūra being one of them.

semin-durr:51-51.t:
The generality read {إِنَّ الله رَبِّي وَرَبُّكُمْ} with kasra on the hamza, as a resumptive statement. This is apparent on our view that «جئتكم» is emphatic (tawkīd). But if you make it establishing [a new meaning] (taʾsīs) and make the sign His words {إِنَّ الله رَبِّي وَرَبُّكُمْ} in the sense I mentioned first, then resumption is not valid; rather, the kasra is on the basis of an implied saying, and that saying is a badal (substitute) from «آية», as if the implied form were: "And I have come to you with a sign from your Lord: my saying 'Allah is…'"; so "my saying" is a badal from «آية», and «إنّ» with what falls in its scope is governed by "my saying", and His words {فاتقوا الله وَأَطِيعُونِ} are parenthetical (iʿtirāḍ) between the badal and what it substitutes for.
It was also read with fatḥa on the hamza, and there are several views on it. The first: it is a badal from «آية», as if the implied form were: "And I have come to you with [the fact] that Allah is my Lord and your Lord", i.e. I have come to you with the doctrine of divine oneness; and His words {فاتقوا الله وَأَطِيعُونِ} are also parenthetical. The second: it is on the basis of an implied lām of cause, and the lām of cause is attached to (mutaʿalliq) what follows it, His words «فاعبدوه»; the implied form is: "So worship Him, because Allah is my Lord and your Lord", like the words of Allah the Exalted {لإِيلاَفِ قُرَيْشٍ} [Quraysh: 1] up to His words «فليعبدوا», since the implied form is: "So let them worship… for the accustomed security of Quraysh." According to Sībawayh and his followers this is prohibited, because whenever the governed element is «أنّ» with its ṣila (complement), it cannot be put before its governor; they do not permit «أنَّ زيداً منطلقٌ عَرَفْتُ» meaning «عَرَفْتُ أنَّ زيداً منطلقٌ», because of the ugliness of the wording, since its standing at the head of the wording requires kasra. The third: «أنّ الله» is on the basis of dropping the preposition, namely «على», and «على» is attached to «آية» itself; the implied form is: "And I have come to you with a sign that Allah…", as if it were said: "with a mark and an indication of the oneness of Allah the Exalted". Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this. On this view the two imperative sentences are also parenthetical, and it is far-fetched.
His words: {هذا صِرَاطٌ}: «هذا» refers to the divine oneness indicated by His words {إِنَّ الله رَبِّي وَرَبُّكُمْ}, or to «إنّ الله» itself, in view of this wording being the straight path.

semin-durr:52-52.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {مِنْهُمُ}: there are two views on it. The first: it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أحسّ», and «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the extent, i.e. the perceiving began from their direction. The second: it is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الكفر», i.e. "the disbelief, it issuing from them".
Al-iḥsās is perceiving by one of the five senses, which are taste, smell, touch, hearing and sight. One says أَحْسَسْتُ الشيءَ and أحسستُ بالشيءِ, and حَسَسْتُه and حَسَسْتُ به; one also says حَسَيْتُ, changing its second sīn into yāʾ, and أحَسْتُ, omitting the first of its sīns. The poet said:
1307 - سِوى أنَّ العِتاقَ من المطايا ... أَحَسْنَ به فَهُنَّ إليه شُوسُ
(Except that the noble among the mounts sensed him, so they look at him askance.)
Sībawayh said: "Among the irregularities of the doubled [verbs] — meaning in omission — is something resembling the type أقمت, though it is not regular; that is their saying أَحَسْتُ and أَحَسْنَ, meaning أَحْسَسْتُ and أَحْسَسْنَ. The same is done with every form in which the verb is built and the vowel does not reach it; but if you say لم أُحِسَّ, you do not omit." It was also said: al-iḥsās is finding and seeing; one says: "Have you perceived (aḥsasta) your companion?", i.e. found him or seen him.
His words: {مَنْ أنصاري}: «أنصار» is the plural of «نصير», like شَريف and أَشْراف. Some said: it is the plural of «نَصْر», by which the maṣdar (verbal noun) is meant, and it needs the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "who are the people of my support?" «إلى» is in its usual sense and is attached to an omitted element, because it is a ḥāl; its implied form is: "Who are my helpers, adding themselves to Allah?" So Abū al-Baqāʾ rendered it. Some said that «إلى» is in the sense of «مع» (with), i.e. "with Allah". Al-Farrāʾ said: "It is a good view." «إلى» may only be put in the place of «مع» when you join a thing to a thing that was not with it, as in the Arabs' saying: "A small herd (dhawd) added to a small herd makes camels", i.e. [with] the herd — unlike your saying: "So-and-so arrived and with him much wealth", for it is not proper to say "and to him much wealth"; and likewise you say "So-and-so arrived with his family", whereas if you said "to his family" it would not be correct. They also counted among this His words {وَلاَ تأكلوا أَمْوَالَهُمْ إلى أَمْوَالِكُمْ} [al-Nisāʾ: 2]. Abū al-Baqāʾ rejected its being in the sense of «مع», saying: "It is nothing, for «إلى» is not fit to be in the sense of «مع», and no analogy supports it."
It was also said: «إلى» is in the sense of the lām, i.e. "Who are my helpers for Allah?", as in His words {يهدي إِلَى الحق} [Yūnus: 35], i.e. "to the truth"; so al-Fārisī rendered it. It was also said: rather, «أنصاري» was made to include the meaning of adding [oneself], i.e. "who will add himself to Allah in supporting me?", so «إلى الله» is attached to «أنصاري» itself. It was also said: it is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from the yāʾ in «أنصاري», i.e. "Who are my helpers, [me] going to Allah, taking refuge in Him?"; al-Zamakhsharī said this.
His words: {الحواريون}: the plural of «حَوارِيّ», which is the helper. It is fully declinable even though it resembles [the pattern] mafāʿil, because the relational (nisba) yāʾ in it is incidental. Like it is حَوالِيّ, which is the crafty one. These two are unlike قَمَارِيّ and بَخاتِيّ, which are diptotes. The difference is that the yāʾ in حواريّ and حواليّ is incidental, unlike it in قماريّ and بخاتيّ, where it exists before pluralisation in your saying قُمْرِيّ and بُخْتِيّ.
Al-ḥawāriyy is the helper, as preceded. That is because ʿĪsā, peace be upon him, passed by some people and asked them for help and called them to faith, and they followed him; they were fullers (bleachers) of clothes. So everyone who follows a prophet and supports him was called ḥawāriyy, naming him by the name of those people, likening him to them, even if he is not a fuller. In the ḥadīth from him, peace be upon him, about al-Zubayr: "My paternal aunt's son and my ḥawāriyy from my community"; and from it also: "Every prophet has a ḥawāriyy, and my ḥawāriyy is al-Zubayr." This is the sense of the words of Abū ʿUbayda and other lexicographers. It was also said: the ḥawāriyy is a man's choice and sincere companion. Its derivation is from «حُرْتُ الثوبَ», i.e. I made its whiteness pure by washing; from it the fuller was called ḥawāriyy because he cleans clothes. In the exegesis it is that the followers of ʿĪsā, peace be upon him, were fullers. Abū ʿUbayda said: "The companions of ʿĪsā were called ḥawāriyyūn because of whiteness, and they were fullers. Al-Farazdaq said:
1308 - فقلتُ: إنَّ الحواريَّاتِ مَعْطَبَةٌ ... إذا تَفَتَّلْنَ من تحتِ الجلابيبِ
(So I said: the fair-skinned women are a cause of ruin when they sway beneath their outer garments.)
meaning the women." I say: he means that women, because of their whiteness and the purity of their complexion — especially those living in luxury — are called al-ḥawāriyyāt. For that reason al-Zamakhsharī said: "The ḥawāriyy is a man's choice and sincere companion; from it town-dwelling women are called al-ḥawāriyyāt because of the purity and cleanness of their complexions." And he recited, from Abū Jilda al-Yashkurī:
1309 - فَقُلْ للحوارِيَّاتِ يبكِينَ غيرَنا ... ولا يَبْكِنا إلا الكلابُ النوابِحُ
(Tell the fair town-women to weep for others than us; let none weep for us but the barking dogs.)
End of quote. From it the ḥūr (houris) were called ḥūr because of their whiteness and cleanness. The derivation is from al-ḥawar, which is whitening clothes and other things. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: "They are the washers; in the language of the Nabataeans they are hawārī, with hāʾ in place of ḥāʾ." Ibn al-Anbārī said: "Whoever holds this view says: this is a word in which the language of the Arabs and the language of the Nabataeans share; and it is the view of Muqātil ibn Sulaymān that the ḥawāriyyūn are the fullers." It was also said: they are the fighters in the path [of Allah]; so Ibn al-Anbārī reported it, and he recited:
1310 - ونحنُ أناسٌ تملأ البيضَ هامُنَا ... ونحن الحوارِيُّونَ يومَ نُزاحِفُ
جماجِمُنَا يومَ اللقاء تَراسُنا ... إلى الموت نَمْشي ليس فينا تَجانُفُ
(We are a people whose heads fill the helmets, and we are the ḥawāriyyūn on the day we advance; our skulls on the day of encounter are our shields; to death we walk, with no swerving among us.)
Al-Wāḥidī said: "The preferred of these views according to the lexicographers is that this name attached to them because of whiteness." Then he mentioned what I mentioned from Abū ʿUbayd. [Translator's note: earlier the source attributes this to Abū ʿUbayda.]
Al-Rāghib said: "حَوَّرْتُ الشيءَ means I whitened it and rounded it; from it is al-khubz al-ḥuwwārā (white bread). The ḥawāriyyūn are the helpers of ʿĪsā. It was also said: their derivation is from حار يَحُور, i.e. he returned; Allah the Exalted said: {إِنَّهُ ظَنَّ أَن لَّن يَحُورَ} [al-Inshiqāq: 14] [Translator's note: the source prints 4; the verse is 84:14], i.e. that he would never return; so it is as if they are those who return to Allah the Exalted. One says حار يَحُور حَوْراً, i.e. he returned; and حار يحور حَوْراً when one goes back and forth in a place; from it: حارَ الماءُ في الغَدير (the water eddied in the pool), and حار في أمره and تحيَّر فيه (he was perplexed in his affair). The origin of the latter is تَحَيْوَر; the wāw was changed into yāʾ, so its pattern is tafayʿal, not tafaʿʿal, since if it were tafaʿʿal it would have been said تَحَوَّر, like تَجَوَّز. From it the axle on which the pulley turns is called miḥwar, because of its going back and forth; and the maḥāra of the ear [is so called] for its hollow outer part, likening it to the maḥāra of water (a shell), because the air goes back and forth in it with the sound, as water goes back and forth in the shell. «القومُ في حَوْر», i.e. the people are going back towards decline. From it: 'We seek refuge in Allah from al-ḥawr after al-kawr.'" [Translator's note: the source does not mark clearly where al-Rāghib's quotation ends.]
There are two interpretations of it. The first: we seek refuge in Allah from wavering in a matter after proceeding in it. The second: we seek refuge in Allah from decline and wavering in one's state after increase in it. One says: حارَ بعد ما كارَ (he declined after he had prospered). Al-muḥāwara is answering one another in speech, and likewise al-taḥāwur and al-ḥiwār; from it: {وَهُوَ يُحَاوِرُهُ} [al-Kahf: 34] and {والله يَسْمَعُ تَحَاوُرَكُمآ} [al-Mujādila: 1], i.e. your answering each other in speech. From it also: "I spoke to him, but he made no reply (ḥawār, ḥawīr or maḥwara)", and "he does not live by ḥawr", i.e. by a mind he can return to. Al-ḥawar is the appearance of a little white in the eye amid the black, and that is the utmost beauty in the eye; one says from it أَحْوَرَتْ عينُه; the masculine is aḥwar and the feminine ḥawrāʾ, and the plural in both is ḥūr, like ḥumr as the plural of aḥmar and ḥamrāʾ. It was said the ḥūr were called ḥūr for that reason. It was also said: their [the ḥawāriyyūn's] derivation is from purity of heart, its sincerity and truthfulness; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this, and it goes back to the first meaning, purity of whiteness; so it is figurative for being cleansed of sins and of what adulterates the religion.
The yāʾ in حواريّ and حواليّ is not for relation (nisba); rather it is added (zāʾida), like its addition in كرسيّ. [Translator's note: earlier in this entry the yāʾ was called a relational yāʾ that is incidental; the source is translated as written.]
The generality read «الحواريُّون» with a doubled yāʾ throughout the Qurʾān; al-Thaqafī and al-Nakhaʿī read it with an undoubled yāʾ throughout the Qurʾān. They said: because the doubling is heavy. The regular form on this reading would have been to say «الحوارُون», because the ḍamma is felt heavy on a yāʾ preceded by kasra, so the ḍamma of the yāʾ is transferred to what precedes it and the yāʾ becomes quiescent; two quiescent letters then meet and the yāʾ is omitted because of the meeting of the two quiescents. This is like «جاء القاضُون», whose origin is القاضِيُون, and what was mentioned was done to it. They said: the ḍamma of the yāʾ was kept on it only to indicate that the doubling is intended, because the doubled letter can bear the ḍamma — as al-Akhfash held regarding «يستهزيون», where he changed the hamza into a yāʾ with ḍamma, and the ḍamma was kept only to indicate the hamza.

semin-durr:53-53.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {مَعَ الشاهدين}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object of «اكتبنا». There is an omission in the speech, i.e. "with those who bear witness to You of [Your] oneness".

semin-durr:54-54.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَمَكَرُواْ وَمَكَرَ الله}: this is of the type of correspondence (muqābala), i.e. Allah may not be described as plotting except because of what is mentioned with it — another word attributed to whom it befits. This is as preceded with deception (khidāʿ); so it was said. But it has come without correspondence in His words {أَفَأَمِنُواْ مَكْرَ الله فَلاَ يَأْمَنُ مَكْرَ الله} [al-Aʿrāf: 99].
Al-makr (plotting) in the language has the root sense of concealing. One says مَكَر اللَّيلُ, i.e. the night grew dark and concealed with its darkness what is in it. They also said: its derivation is from al-makr, which is an intertwined [kind of] tree; they imagined in it that the plot entwines itself around the one plotted against and envelops him. A woman is «ممكورة الخَلْق», i.e. compact of body, and likewise «ممكورة البطن». Then al-makr was applied to malice and deception; for that reason some lexicographers expressed it as "striving to cause corruption". Al-Zajjāj said: "It is from مَكَر الليلُ and أَمْكَرَ, i.e. it grew dark." Some expressed it by saying: it is turning another away from what he intends by a stratagem, and that is of two kinds: praiseworthy, which is when a good act is sought by it — and on that basis are His words {والله خَيْرُ الماكرين} — and blameworthy, which is when an evil act is sought by it, as in {وَلاَ يَحِيقُ المكر السيىء إِلاَّ بِأَهْلِهِ} [Fāṭir: 43].

semin-durr:55-55.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {إِذْ قَالَ الله}: there are three views on what puts it in the accusative. The first: His words «ومكر الله», i.e. "and Allah plotted against them at this time". The second: it is «خير الماكرين». The third: an implied «اذكر» (remember), so it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), as its explanation has preceded more than once.
His words: {إِنِّي مُتَوَفِّيكَ وَرَافِعُكَ}: there are two views on it. The more apparent of them: the speech is in its [natural] order, without claiming any fronting and postponement in it, in the sense: "I will take your term in full, postpone you and protect you from the disbelievers' killing you, until you die a natural death without being killed at the hands of the disbelievers, and I will raise you to My heaven."
The second: there is fronting and postponement in the speech, the original being «رافعك إليّ ومتوفيك», because he was raised to heaven and will be taken in death after that; and the wāw is for combining, so there is no difference between fronting and postponing. Abū al-Baqāʾ said this and began with it. But there is no need for that, since each one can be kept in its place with the meaning that preceded — except that Abū al-Baqāʾ took al-tawaffī to mean death, and that will only be after his being raised, his descending to the earth and his ruling by the law of Muḥammad ﷺ.
In His words {والله خَيْرُ الماكرين} [Āl ʿImrān: 54] there is the placing of the overt noun in the place of the pronoun, since the original is: "They plotted and Allah plotted, and He is the best of plotters."
His words: {وَجَاعِلُ الذين اتبعوك}: there are two views on it. The more apparent of them: it is an address to ʿĪsā, peace be upon him. The second: it is an address to our Prophet ﷺ; the pause on His words {مِنَ الذين كَفَرُواْ} is then complete, and one begins with what follows. This is permissible because the context indicates it. {فَوْقَ الذين كَفَرُواْ} is the second of the two objects of «جاعل», because it is in the sense of "making into" (muṣayyir) only.
{إلى يَوْمِ} is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the making, meaning that this making continues until that day. It may also be attached to the [notion of] being settled (istiqrār) implied in «فوق», i.e. "making them dominant over them until the Day of Resurrection", meaning that they prevail over the Jews and other disbelievers by victory in this world; as for the Day of Resurrection, Allah will judge between them and admit the obedient to Paradise and the disobedient to the Fire. The meaning is not that the believers' elevation over the disbelievers ends after this world and its passing, because they have another ascendancy besides this ascendancy. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "The apparent thing is that «إلى» is attached to an omitted element, which is what governs «فوق», and it is the second object of «جاعل», since «جاعل» here means 'making into'; so the meaning is: being above them until the Day of Resurrection. This is on the basis that the aboveness is figurative. But if the aboveness is literal — namely aboveness in Paradise — then «إلى» is not attached to that omitted element but to something preceding: «متوفيك», «رافعك» or «مطهّرك», since its attachment to each of them is valid. Its attachment to «رافعك» or «مطهّرك» is clear; to «متوفيك», it is on some of the views." By "some of the views" he means that al-tawaffī means "taking you from the earth without death" — the view of a group such as al-Ḥasan, Ibn Zayd, Ibn Jurayj and others — or it means what al-Zamakhsharī mentioned, namely "taking your term in full", its meaning being: "I will protect you from the disbelievers' killing you, postpone you to a term I have written for you, and cause you to die a natural death, not killed at the hands of the disbelievers". But on the view of whoever says he was literally made to die, its attachment to it cannot be conceived, because whoever holds that does not hold that the death continues until the Day of Resurrection; rather, one says he was made to die for three hours, and another says he was made to die for seven hours, the time it took for him to be raised to His heaven, so that no fear or alarm would overtake him in a waking state. On what the Shaykh mentioned, the question may be one of iʿmāl (rival governors): three governors would contend over this preposition with its genitive noun, and if we add to them the aboveness being figurative, four governors would contend over it. The apparent thing is that it is attached to «جاعل».
It has preceded that Abū ʿAmr makes the mīm of «أحكمُ» and the like quiescent before the bāʾ.

semin-durr:10-10.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لَن تُغْنِيَ}: the majority read «تُغْني» with the tāʾ, in regard to the femininity of the plural. Al-Ḥasan and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān read it with the yāʾ, in the masculine, according to the basic form. Al-Ḥasan unvowelled the yāʾ of «تُغْني», finding the vowel on a weak letter heavy and treating it like the alif; some restrict this to poetic necessity.

His saying: {مِّنَ الله}: there are four analyses of «من» here. The first: that it is for the starting point of the extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya), figuratively, i.e. "from Allah's punishment and His requital". The second: that it means «عند». Abū ʿUbayda said: it means «عند», as in His saying {أَطْعَمَهُم مِّن جُوعٍ وَآمَنَهُم مِّنْ خَوْفٍ} [Quraysh: 4], i.e. "at [the time of] hunger and at [the time of] fear". This is weak according to the grammarians.

The third: that it means «بدل» "in place of". Al-Zamakhsharī said: "His saying «من الله» is like His saying {إَنَّ الظن لاَ يُغْنِي مِنَ الحق شَيْئاً} [Yūnus: 36]; the meaning is: they will not avail them anything against [i.e. in place of] the mercy of Allah or obedience to Him, i.e. in place of His mercy and obedience to Him, and in place of the truth. Of this is «ولا يَنْفع ذا الجَدِّ منك الجَدُّ» 'and the fortune of the fortunate will not benefit him against You', i.e. his fortune and his share of this world will not benefit him in place of You, i.e. in place of obedience to You and what is with You. Of similar meaning is His saying, the Exalted: {وَمَآ أَمْوَالُكُمْ وَلاَ أَوْلاَدُكُمْ بالتي تُقَرِّبُكُمْ عِندَنَا زلفى} [Sabaʾ: 37]." This that he mentioned — its meaning «بدل» — the majority of grammarians reject; for the majority interpret otherwise most of what those who permit it adduce. Of it is his saying:

1182 - جاريةٌ لم تأْكِلِ المُرَقَّقا ... ولم تَذُقْ من البقولِ الفُسْتقا
(A girl who has not eaten thin bread, nor tasted pistachios in place of herbs.)

and the saying of the other:

1183 - أخذوا المَخَاضَ من الفصيلِ غُلُبَّةً ... ظُلْماً ويُكتبُ للأميرِ أَفِيلا
(They took the pregnant she-camels in place of the weanling, by force and unjustly, and it is written down for the governor as a young camel.)

And the Exalted said: {وَلَوْ نَشَآءُ لَجَعَلْنَا مِنكُمْ مَّلاَئِكَةً} [al-Zukhruf: 60], {أَرَضِيتُمْ بالحياة الدنيا مِنَ الآخرة} [al-Tawba: 38].

The fourth: that it is partitive (tabʿīḍiyya). However, when the Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] permitted this analysis, he made it built on parsing «شيئاً» as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), in the sense of "it will not repel or hold off". He said: "On this [view], «مِنْ» may be in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «شيئاً», because had it come later it would have been in the position of a naʿt (adjective) of it; so when it was advanced it became accusative as a ḥāl; and «مِنْ» would then be partitive." This should not be permitted at all, because partitive «مِنْ» is interpreted by the word «بعض» "part" annexed to what «مِنْ» puts in the genitive. Do you not see that when you say «رأيت رجلاً من بني تميم» "I saw a man of Banū Tamīm", its meaning is "part of Banū Tamīm", and «أخذت من الدراهم» "I took of the dirhams" means "part of the dirhams"? Here that is not conceivable at all. Making it a naʿt of «شيئاً» is valid only if we make «مِنْ» for the starting point of the extent, as when you say «عندي درهم من زيد» "I have a dirham from Zayd", i.e. being or lodged from Zayd; and partition is barred in it. And the ḥāl is like the naʿt in meaning; so it is barred that «مِنْ» be partitive while «من الله» is made a ḥāl from «شيئاً». The Shaykh followed Abū al-Baqāʾ in that; except that Abū al-Baqāʾ, when he said that, supplied a muḍāf by which his statement became valid, the implied form being: «شيئاً من عذاب الله» "anything of Allah's punishment". So he [the Shaykh] ought to have followed him [in this analysis, stating explicitly what repels] this objection that I have mentioned.

[Translator's note: the source contains evident typographical slips — «للتعبيض» for «للتبعيض», «الدارهم» for «الدراهم», «الغايةى» for «الغاية» — translated according to the intended forms.]

«شيئاً» is either accusative as a mafʿūl bihi — and its interpretation has preceded — or as a maṣdar (absolute object), i.e. "anything of availing". His saying: {وأولئك هُمْ وَقُودُ}: this clause admits two analyses. The first: that it is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). The second: that it is conjoined (mansūqa) to the khabar (predicate) of «إنَّ». «هم» may be a mubtadaʾ (subject) or a pronoun of separation (faṣl). The majority read «وَقود» with fatḥa on the wāw, and al-Ḥasan with ḍamma. The verification of that has preceded in al-Baqara, as has [the point] that the maṣdar sense is also possible in the form with fatḥa on the wāw, and that where it is a maṣdar it must be interpreted; so there is no need to repeat it here.

semin-durr:11-11.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {كَدَأْبِ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ}: there are two analyses of this kāf. The first: that it is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being: "Their way in that is like the way of the people of Pharaoh". Al-Zamakhsharī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya began with this.

The second: that it is in the position of the accusative, and concerning what makes it accusative there are nine views. The first: that it is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), the governor in which is «كفروا», its implied form being: «إنَّ الذين كفروا كفراً كدأبِ آل فرعون» "those who disbelieved with a disbelief like the way of the people of Pharaoh", i.e. like their habit in disbelief. This is the opinion of al-Farrāʾ. This view is rejected because [on it] He would have predicated of the relative noun before its ṣila (relative clause) was complete, which necessarily entails separating the parts of the ṣila with an extraneous element, and that is not permitted. The second: that it is accusative by «كفروا», but an implied one, because this uttered one indicates it. The third: that what makes it accusative is implied, indicated by His saying «لَنْ تُغني», i.e. their benefiting from wealth and children came to nothing, like the habit of the people of Pharaoh in that. The fourth: that it is accusative by the word «وقود», i.e. "the Fire is kindled with them as it is kindled with the people of Pharaoh", as you say «إنك لتظلم الناس كدأبِ أبيك» "you wrong people like your father's way", meaning "like your father's wronging"; al-Zamakhsharī said this. It is open to question, because «الوَقود» on the well-known reading most evidently is a noun for that with which [fire] is kindled, and if it is a noun it has no governing power. If it is said that it is a maṣdar, or on the reading of al-Ḥasan, it is valid. The fifth: that it is accusative by «لن تُغْني» itself, i.e. "they will not avail them, just as they did not avail those"; al-Zamakhsharī mentioned it. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] declared it weak because it entails separating the governor from what it governs by the clause {وأولئك هُمْ وَقُودُ النار}. He said: "[This holds] on either of the two construals we gave for it: that it is conjoined to the khabar of «إنَّ», or to the clause emphasized by «إنَّ»." He said: "If you make it parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya) — and that is far-fetched — what al-Zamakhsharī said is permissible." The sixth: that the governor in it is an implied verb indicated by the word «الوقود», its implied form being: "[the Fire] is kindled with them, like the habit of the people of Pharaoh", the comparison being in the burning itself; Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this. The seventh: that the governor is «يُعَذَّبون» "they are punished, like the habit of the people of Pharaoh", indicated by the context of the discourse. The eighth: that it is accusative by «كَذَّبوا بآياتنا», the pronoun in «كَذَّبوا» on this [view] referring to the disbelievers of Mecca and others among the contemporaries of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, i.e. "they denied with a denial like the habit of the people of Pharaoh in that denial". The ninth: that the governor in it is His saying {فَأَخَذَهُمُ الله}, i.e. "So Allah seized them with a seizing like His seizing of the people of Pharaoh". This is rejected, for what comes after the conjunctive fāʾ does not govern what is before it; it is not permitted to say «قُمْتُ زيداً فضربْتُ». As for «زيداً فاضربْ» "Zayd — strike [him]", the discussion of it has preceded in al-Baqara. Some grammarians have reported from the Kufans that they permit placing the governed word before the conjunction; on this [basis] this view is permissible.

In al-Zamakhsharī's words there is an oversight, for he said: "The position of the kāf may be made accusative by «لن تُغْني» or by «خالدون», i.e. they will not avail them, just as they did not avail those; or they will abide therein eternally just as those abide." But in the wording of the noble verse there is no «خالدون»; the arrangement of the Quran is only {وأولئك هُمْ وَقُودُ النار}. It is unlikely that it should be said that he meant an implied «خالدون» indicated by the context of the discourse.

His saying: {والذين مِن قَبْلِهِمْ} may be genitive, conjoined (nasaq) to «آل فرعون», or nominative as a mubtadaʾ, the khabar being His saying after that: {كَذَّبُواْ بِآيَاتِ الله}. These two possibilities are permissible absolutely. Abū al-Baqāʾ restricted the permissibility of the nominative to the kāf being in the position of the nominative, saying: "On this [view] — i.e. its being in the position of the nominative as the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ — two analyses are possible for {والذين مِن قَبْلِهِمْ}. The first: it is also genitive by conjunction, and «كَذَّبوا» is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), with «قد» implied along with it; or it may be resumptive, with no position, mentioned to explain their state. The other analysis: that the discourse is complete at «فرعون», and «الذين مِنْ قبلِهم» is a mubtadaʾ and «كَذَبوا» its khabar."

«الدَّأْب» is habit. One says «دَأَبَ يَدْأَبُ», i.e. he persevered and kept at it; and from it is «دَأَبا», i.e. continually. Imruʾ al-Qays said:

1184 - كدَأْبِك من أمِّ الحُوَيْرث قبلها ... وجارتِها أمِّ الرَّبابِ بمَأْسَلِ
(As was your way with Umm al-Ḥuwayrith before her, and her neighbour Umm al-Rabāb, at Maʾsal.)

One says «دَأَبَ يدأَبُ دؤُوبا». Zuhayr said:

1185 - لأرتَحِلَنْ بالفجر ثم لأدْأَبَنْ ... إلى الليلِ إلاَّ أن يُعَرِّجَني طِفْلُ
(I shall set off at dawn and keep on until night, unless a tender [beauty] makes me halt.)

Al-Wāḥidī said: «الدأَب» is exertion and toil; one says «سار فلان يومه كلَّه يدأَبُ فيه فهو دائِبٌ» "So-and-so travelled all day, toiling in it, so he is «دائب»", i.e. he exerted himself in his travel. This is its origin in the language; then «الدأب» came to express state, affair and habit, because work and effort comprise all of this. For that reason al-Zamakhsharī said: "[«الدأب»] is the maṣdar of «دَأَب في العملِ» when one labours at it; then it was put in place of the affair and state a person is in." One says «دَأْب» and «دَأَب», with the hamza unvowelled and with fatḥa; they are two dialectal forms of the maṣdar, like «الضَّأْن» and «الضَّأَن», «المَعْز» and «المَعَز». Ḥafṣ read «سَبْعَ سنينَ دَأَبا» with fatḥa. Al-Farrāʾ said: "The Arabs make heavy [i.e. vowel] what has a guttural letter as its second [radical], as in «النَّعْل» and «النَّعَل», «النَّهْر» and «النهَر», «الشَّأْم» and «الشَّأَم»", and he recited:

1186 - قد سار شرقيُّهم حتى أَتوا سَبَأً ... وانساح غربيُّهم حتى هوى الشَّأَما
(Their eastern ones travelled until they reached Saba', and their western ones spread out until they came down to Syria.)

His saying: {كَذَّبُواْ بِآيَاتِنَا}: it has been stated that it may be the khabar of «الذين» if it is said to be a mubtadaʾ. If it is not a mubtadaʾ, it has also been stated that it is an elucidation of «الدأب» and an explanation of it, as if it were said: "What did they do, and what was done to them?" and it was said: "They denied Our signs" — so it is the answer to an implied question; or that it is a ḥāl. In His saying «بآياتنا» there is a shift (iltifāt), because before it is «من الله», which is an overt noun. The bāʾ in «بذنوبهم» may be causal, i.e. "He seized them because of what they committed", or for the ḥāl, i.e. "He seized them while they were bound up with sins, not repenting of them".

[«الذَّنْب» is in origin what follows and comes after; the crime was called «ذنب»] because its punishment follows, i.e. comes after, the one who commits it. «الذَّنُوب» is the bucket, because it follows the rope in pulling. The origin of that is «ذَنَب» "the tail" of an animal, because it «يَذْنُبُه», i.e. follows it; one says «ذَنَبه يَذْنُبُه ذَنْباً», i.e. he followed him.

His saying: {شَدِيدُ العقاب} is like His saying {سَرِيعُ الحساب} [al-Baqara: 202], i.e. "severe is His punishment"; its verification has preceded. These verses, from the beginning of the sūra up to here, have comprised kinds of the sciences of meanings (al-maʿānī), clarity (al-bayān) and embellishment (al-badīʿ) that are not hidden from one who reflects on them.

[Translator's note: «سياق اكلام» in the source is evidently «سياق الكلام» "the context of the discourse".]

semin-durr:12-12.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {سَتُغْلَبُونَ وَتُحْشَرُونَ}: the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read these two verbs in the third person (ghayba), and the rest in the second person (khiṭāb). The third and second person in a construction like this are clear, as when you say «قل لزيد: قم» "Say to Zayd: Stand!" by way of quotation (ḥikāya), and «قل لزيد: يقوم» "Tell Zayd [that] he is to stand". Something like this has preceded at His saying {لاَ تَعْبُدُونَ إِلاَّ الله} [al-Baqara: 83]. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said about the third-person reading: "What is apparent is that the pronoun refers to those who disbelieved, and the clause is then not quoted by «قل» but by another [verb of] saying, the implied form being: 'Say to them my saying: They will be overcome', and 'my informing that being overcome will befall them', as He said: {قُل لِلَّذِينَ كفروا إِن يَنتَهُواْ يُغَفَرْ لَهُمْ مَّا قَدْ سَلَفَ} [al-Anfāl: 38]. So with the tāʾ he informs them in the sense of what he was informed of — that they will be overcome — and with the yāʾ he informs them in the very words in which he was informed that they will be overcome."

What he said was said before him by al-Zamakhsharī, and he took it from him; but Abū al-Qāsim's wording is clearer, so let us cite it. He said, may Allah have mercy on him: "If you say: What difference is there between the two readings in terms of meaning? I say: The meaning of the reading with the tāʾ is the command to inform them of what will befall them — being overcome and being gathered to Hell — so it is an informing in the sense of 'you will be overcome and gathered', which comes from the very content of what is threatened; and that is what the wording indicates. The meaning of the reading with the yāʾ is the command to relate to them, in its wording, what He informed him of their threat, as if He said: 'Convey to them this saying, which is My saying to you: They will be overcome and gathered.'"

Al-Farrāʾ and Thaʿlab allowed that the pronoun in «سَيُغْلبون ويُحْشرون» refers to the disbelievers of Quraysh, and that by «الذين كفروا» the Jews are meant, the meaning being: "Say to the Jews: Quraysh will be overcome." This is tenable only on the third-person reading. Makkī said: "What strengthens the reading with the yāʾ is their consensus on the yāʾ in His saying {قُل لِلَّذِينَ كفروا إِن يَنتَهُواْ}." He said: "The tāʾ is dearer to me, because of the consensus of the two Ḥaram [readers, i.e. of Mecca and Medina], ʿĀṣim and others on it." I say: Like their consensus on His saying {قُل لِلَّذِينَ كفروا إِن يَنتَهُواْ} is their consensus on His saying {قُلْ لِّلْمُؤْمِنِينَ يَغُضُّواْ} [al-Nūr: 30] and {قُل لِّلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ يَغْفِرُواْ لِلَّذِينَ لاَ يَرْجُونَ} [al-Jāthiya: 14].

Al-Farrāʾ said: "Whoever reads with the tāʾ makes the Jews and the polytheists included in the address; then in this meaning both the yāʾ and the tāʾ are permitted, as you say in speech: «قل لعبد الله: إنه قائم وإنك قائم» 'Say to ʿAbd Allāh: he is standing / you are standing'. In the reading (ḥarf) of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] is {قُل لِلَّذِينَ كفروا إِن يَنتَهُواْ يُغَفَرْ لَهُمْ مَّا قَدْ سَلَفَ}. Whoever reads with the yāʾ takes it as addressing the Jews, with the overcoming befalling the polytheists, as if it were said: 'Say, O Muhammad, to the Jews: The polytheists will be overcome and gathered'; in this meaning only the yāʾ is permitted, because the polytheists are absent."

His saying: {وَبِئْسَ المهاد}: the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, i.e. "wretched is the resting-place: Hell". The omission of the specified one indicates the soundness of Sībawayh's doctrine that it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause before it is its khabar (predicate). Had it been, as others said, a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, or the reverse, it would not have been omitted a second time, because of the excessive curtailment through omitting the rest of the clause.

semin-durr:73-73.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {إِلاَّ لِمَن تَبِعَ}: there are two views on this lām. One is that it is redundant (zāʾida) and emphatic, like the one in His saying {رَدِفَ لَكُم} [al-Naml: 72], i.e. «رَدِفَكم» (is close behind you), and the saying of another:

1332 - فَلَمَّا أَنْ تواقَفْنَا قليلاً ... أَنَخْنا للكلاكِلِ فارتَمَيْنَا
(When we had stood facing each other a little while, we made the camels kneel on their breasts, and we shot at one another.)

and the saying of another:

1333 - ما كنتُ أخدَعُ للخليلِ بخُلَّةٍ ... حتى يكونَ لِيَ الخليلُ خَدُوعا
(I would not deceive a friend in friendship unless the friend were a deceiver to me.)

i.e. «أَنَخْنَا الكلاكل» and «أَخْدَعُ الخليلَ». Similar is:

1334 - يَذُمُّونَ للدنيا وهم يَرْضِعُونَها ... أَفاويقَ حتى ما يَدِرُّ لها ثَعْلُ
(They censure this world while they suckle it, draught after draught, until not a teat of it yields milk.)

meaning «يَذُمُّون الدنيا»; it is also transmitted as «بالدنيا» with bāʾ. I think the verse is «يَذُمُّونَ لي الدنيا» (they censure the world to me), and the wording became confused for the hearer; I have seen it so in some commentaries. This is not strong.

The second is that «أَمِنَ» [Translator's note: so printed; «آمَنَ» is meant] has been made to include (taḍmīn) the sense of «أَقَرَّ» and «اعترَفَ» (to acknowledge, admit), so it was made transitive with the lām, i.e. "and do not acknowledge or admit except to one who follows your religion". Similar are {فَمَآ آمَنَ لموسى} [Yūnus: 83] and {وَمَآ أَنتَ بِمُؤْمِنٍ لَّنَا} [Yūsuf: 17]. Abū ʿAlī said: "«آمَن» has been made transitive with the lām in His saying {فَمَآ آمَنَ لموسى}, {آمَنتُمْ لَهُ} [Ṭāhā: 71], and {يُؤْمِنُ بالله وَيُؤْمِنُ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ} [al-Tawba: 61]"; so he stated that it is transitive with it without taḍmīn. The correct view is what I have given of taḍmīn; I have verified this at the beginning of al-Baqara.

This is an emptied exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh). Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«إلاَّ لِمَنْ تَبع»: there are two views on it. One is that it is an exception from what precedes it, the implied meaning being «ولا تُقِرُّوا إلا لِمَنْ تَبع» (do not acknowledge except to one who follows); on this view the lām is not redundant. It may also be redundant, being construed according to the meaning, i.e. «اجْحَدُوا كلَّ أحدٍ مَنْ تَبعَ» [Translator's note: so printed; the sense seems to be "deny everyone except one who follows"]. The second is that it is intended to be placed later, the implied meaning being: «ولا تُصَدِّقوا أنْ يؤتَى أحَدٌ مثلَ ما أُوتيتم إلا مَنْ تَبع دينَكم» (do not believe that anyone will be given the like of what you were given, except one who follows your religion); on this view the lām is redundant and «مَنْ» is in the position of the accusative as excepted from «أحد»."

Al-Fārisī said: "Belief (al-īmān) does not take two objects, so it is not attached to two prepositional phrases either. It has been attached to the omitted preposition in His saying {أَن يؤتى}, so it cannot be attached to the lām in His saying {لِمَن تَبِعَ دِينَكُمْ}, unless «الإيمان» is construed according to its meaning, so that it takes two objects, the meaning being: «ولا تُقِرُّوا بأَنْ يُؤْتَى أحدٌ مثلَ ما أُوتيتم إلا لمَنْ تَبعَ دينكم» (do not acknowledge that anyone will be given the like of what you were given except to one who follows your religion), as you say «أَقْرَرْتُ لزيدٍ بألف» (I acknowledged a thousand to Zayd). So the lām is attached according to the meaning, and is not redundant in the manner of {رَدِفَ لَكُم} [al-Naml: 72] and {إِن كُنتُمْ لِلرُّؤْيَا تَعْبُرُونَ} [Yūsuf: 43]." I say: this is an explicit statement from Abū ʿAlī that «آمَنَ» has been made to include the sense of «أَقَرَّ».

His saying: {أَن يؤتى أَحَدٌ}: know that there is much discussion of this verse which must be reported from those who said it so that the matter becomes clear. So I say, and with Allah is help: people differed on this verse in [several ways].

The first is that {أَن يؤتى أَحَدٌ} is attached (mutaʿalliq) to His saying {وَلاَ تؤمنوا} with the preposition omitted, the original being «ولا تؤمنوا بأَنْ يُؤْتَى أحدٌ مثلَ ما أوتيتم إلا لِمَنْ تَبعَ دينَكم» (and do not believe that anyone will be given the like of what you were given except for one who follows your religion). When the preposition was dropped, the well-known disagreement between al-Khalīl and Sībawayh about the position of «أَنْ» applies; and His saying {قُلْ إِنَّ الهدى هُدَى الله} is a parenthetical clause. Al-Zamakhsharī said, in establishing this view, with which he began: "«ولا تُؤْمِنُوا» is connected with His saying «أَنْ يُؤْتَى أحد», and what is between them is a parenthesis, i.e. do not display your belief that anyone will be given the like of what you were given except to the people of your religion, not to others. They meant: keep secret your acknowledgement that the Muslims have been given the like of what you were given, and do not divulge it except to your partisans alone, not to the Muslims, lest it increase them in firmness, and not to the polytheists, lest it call them to Islam. «أو يُحاجُّوكم» is conjoined to «أَنْ يُؤْتَى». The pronoun in «يُحاجُّوكم» refers to «أحد», because it has the sense of a plural, meaning: do not believe for anyone other than your followers, for the Muslims will argue against you before your Lord with the truth and overcome you before Allah. If you say: what is the meaning of the parenthesis? I say: its meaning is that guidance is the guidance of Allah; whomever He wills to show kindness to, so that he embraces Islam or increases in firmness, that happens, and your scheming, your stratagems, and your keeping your acknowledgement hidden [Translator's note: printed «وزيُّكُم», apparently for «وزَيُّكم» / «وزَوْيُكم», "your withholding"] from the Muslims and the disbelievers do not avail. Likewise His saying {قُلْ إِنَّ الفضل بِيَدِ الله يُؤْتِيهِ مَن يَشَآءُ}: He means guidance and success (tawfīq)." I say: these are good words, were it not for what he intends by their inner meaning [Translator's note: an allusion to al-Zamakhsharī's Muʿtazilī reading of "kindness" (luṭf)]. On this view His saying {إِلاَّ لِمَن تَبِعَ} is excepted from something omitted, the implied meaning being: "do not believe that anyone will be given the like of what you were given, to anyone of the people, except to your partisans, not to others". This clause — I mean His saying «ولا تُؤْمِنُوا» to its end — is then part of the speech of the group (ṭāʾifa) mentioned before, i.e. "a group said such-and-such, and also said: and do not believe …", while the clause {قُلْ إِنَّ الهدى هُدَى الله} is the speech of Allah alone.

The second is that the lām in «لِمَنْ تَبعَ» is redundant, and it is excepted from the later «أحد», the implied meaning being: "do not believe that anyone will be given the like of what you were given except one who follows your religion"; so «مَنْ تَبعَ» is accusative as excepted from «أحد». On this view Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted three views on the position of «أن يؤتى»: the first and second are the doctrines of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, which have preceded; the third is the accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), its implied form being «مخافَةَ أَنْ يُؤْتَى» (for fear that … be given). This second view is not sound either in meaning or in grammatical technique. As for the meaning, that is clear. As for the technique, it involves placing the excepted before the thing from which it is excepted and before its governing word, and it also involves placing something within the ṣila of «أَنْ» before it, which is not permissible.

The third is that «أَنْ يُؤْتَى» is genitive by the particle of cause, namely the lām, the thing explained by the cause being omitted, its implied form being: «لأنْ يُؤْتَى أحدٌ مثلَ ما أُوتيتم قلتم ذلك ودَبَّرتموه، لا لشيء آخرَ» (because anyone should be given the like of what you were given, you said that and plotted it, and for nothing else). On this view the speech of the group is complete at His saying {إِلاَّ لِمَن تَبِعَ دِينَكُمْ}. Let us clarify this view by what al-Zamakhsharī said. He said, may Allah have mercy on him: "Or the speech is complete at His saying {إِلاَّ لِمَن تَبِعَ دِينَكُمْ}, in the sense: do not believe with this outward belief — namely their believing at the beginning of the day — except for one who follows your religion, i.e. except for those who were followers of your religion among those of you who embraced Islam; because their return was more hoped for, in their view, than the return of others, and because their Islam was more vexing to them. His saying {أَن يؤتى أَحَدٌ} means: because anyone should be given the like of what you were given, you said that and plotted it, and for nothing else; that is, the envy and transgression in you — that anyone should be given the like of what you were given of the excellence of knowledge and the Book — called you to say what you said. The proof of this is the reading of Ibn Kathīr «أَأَن يُؤْتَى أحد» with the addition of the interrogative hamza for affirmation (taqrīr) and rebuke, in the sense «ألأنْ يُؤْتَى أحدٌ؟» (is it because anyone should be given …?). If you say: what then is the meaning of His saying «أو يُحاجُّوكم» on this view? I say: its meaning is: you plotted what you plotted because anyone should be given the like of what you were given, and because of what is connected with it, upon your disbelieving in it, namely their arguing against you before your Lord."

The fourth is that «أَنْ يُؤْتَى» is accusative by an implied verb indicated by {وَلاَ تؤمنوا إِلاَّ لِمَن تَبِعَ دِينَكُمْ}, as though it were said: "Say: guidance is the guidance of Allah, so do not deny that anyone should be given the like of what you were given"; «فلا تُنْكِرُوا» governs «أنْ» and what lies within its scope in the accusative, because His saying {وَلاَ تؤمنوا إِلاَّ لِمَن تَبِعَ دِينَكُمْ} is a denial that anyone should be given the like of what they were given. Al-Shaykh [Translator's note: Abū Ḥayyān] said: "This is far-fetched, because it involves omitting the particle of prohibition and omitting what it governs, and that has not been preserved from their speech." I say: whenever there is evidence indicating the governing word, its omission is permissible in whatever state it is.

The fifth is that «هدى الله» is a badal (substitute) from «الهدى», which is the noun of «إنَّ», and the khabar (predicate) of «إنَّ» is {أَن يؤتى أَحَدٌ}, the implied meaning being: "Say: the guidance of Allah is that anyone be given …", i.e. the guidance of Allah is the giving to anyone of the like of what you were given; and «أو» means «حتى» (until), the meaning being: until they argue against you before your Lord, overcome you and refute your argument before Allah. On this view «أَوْ يُحاجُّوكم» is not conjoined to «أَنْ يُؤتى» nor included within the scope of «أَنْ».

The sixth is that «أَنْ يُؤْتَى» is a badal from «هدى الله», the meaning being: "Say: guidance is the guidance of Allah, and it is that anyone be given the like of what has come to us"; and His saying «أو يُحاجُّوكم» means "or let them argue against you, for they will overcome you". Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this. It is open to question, because it leads to omitting the particle of prohibition [Translator's note: so printed; the lām of command is meant] while keeping its effect.

The seventh is that the negating «لا» is implied before «أَنْ يؤتى», having been omitted because the speech indicates it, and «أو» means «إلاَّ أَنْ» (unless). The implied meaning is: "do not believe anyone in anything except one who follows your religion, in that it is not the case that anyone will be given the like of what you were given except one who follows your religion and brings its like and supports it; for that is not given to anyone other than you, unless they argue against you" — as in your saying «لألْزَمنَّك أو تقضيَني حقي» (I will stick to you until/unless you pay me my due). It is weak in that it omits the negating «لا», and what they mentioned about the speech indicating it is not evident.

The eighth is that «أَنْ يُؤْتى» is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi. The precise form of this view is that you make His saying {أَن يؤتى أَحَدٌ مِّثْلَ مَآ أُوتِيتُمْ أَوْ يُحَآجُّوكُمْ} not included under His saying «قل», but part of the completion of the group's speech, connected with their saying: "do not believe except one who comes with the like of your religion, for fear that anyone be given of prophethood and honour the like of what you were given, and for fear that they argue against you before your Lord through your having acknowledged them, if you do not persist in it". This saying of theirs is the fruit of their envy and disbelief despite their knowing the prophethood of Muḥammad ﷺ. When al-Mubarrad implied the mafʿūl li-ajlihi here, he implied the muḍāf: «كراهَة أن يُؤتَى أحدٌ مثلَ ما أوتيتم» (out of dislike that anyone be given the like of what you were given), i.e. of those who opposed the religion of Islam, because Allah does not guide one who is a liar and an ingrate, so the guidance of Allah is far from those other than the believers; and the address in «أوتيتم» and «يُحاجُّوكم» is to the community of the Prophet ﷺ. Some judged this weak and said: its being a mafʿūl li-ajlihi on the implied form «كراهةَ» requires implying a governing word for it, and implying it is difficult, since before it is a clause in which the explanation of the predication by dislike of the said giving is not evident.

The ninth is that the «أَنْ» with fatḥa comes for negation just as «لا» does; some reported this explicitly from al-Farrāʾ. He made «أو» mean «إلا», the implied meaning being: "no one is given the like of what you were given unless they argue against you", for his being given what you were given is coupled with overcoming you or arguing against you before your Lord, because whoever Allah has given revelation must argue against them before their Lord concerning their not following him. So His saying «أو يُحاجُّوكم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) necessary in terms of meaning, since Allah does not give revelation to a messenger except that he argues against those who oppose him. This view is worthless, since it has not been established in the speech of the Arabs.

They differed concerning the clause «ولا تُؤْمِنُوا»: is it part of what the group said, or part of what Allah the Exalted said — in the sense that Allah the Exalted addressed it to the believers to make their hearts firm and calm their spirits, lest they doubt when the Jews confused matters for them and falsified? Ibn ʿAṭiyya reported consensus of the people of interpretation that it is part of what the group said, but that is not correct, given the disagreement that people have reported.

«أحد» in the noble verse may be one of the nouns bound to negation, or may not be, but rather mean «واحد» (one). The difference between the two has preceded: the one bound to negation has an original hamza, while the one not bound to negation has a hamza substituted for a wāw. On making it bound to negation, the pronoun referring back to it in the plural is evident, out of regard for its meaning, since what is meant by it is generality; on this is His saying {فَمَا مِنكُمْ مِّنْ أَحَدٍ عَنْهُ حَاجِزِينَ} [al-Ḥāqqa: 47], where He made the khabar plural since «أحد» has the sense of a plural. On making it the one not bound to negation, the plural pronoun in «يُحاجُّوكُم» is with regard to the Messenger, peace be upon him, and his followers. In some of the preceding views it is valid to make the «أحد» mentioned the one bound to negation, namely when the speech is in the sense of denial; and when the speech is in the sense of affirmation, as has passed in some views, it is impossible to make it the one bound to negation. The matter is clear from what has preceded.

Ibn Kathīr read «أأن يؤتى» with an interrogative hamza, in keeping with his rule of easing the second hamza bayna bayna without lengthening between them. This reading has been explained in several ways. The first: «أن يُؤتى» is with the preposition omitted, namely the lām of cause, the thing explained being omitted, its implied form being: «أَلأنْ يؤتى أحدٌ مثل ما أوتيتم قلتم ذلك ودَبَّرتموه» (is it because anyone should be given the like of what you were given that you said that and plotted it?). I have given its verification; in that case the two views on the position of «أَنْ» are acceptable, I mean the accusative, the doctrine of Sībawayh, and the genitive, the doctrine of al-Khalīl.

The second: «أَنْ يُؤتَى» is in the position of the nominative [Translator's note: printed «رفعب», a misprint for «رفع»] as a mubtadaʾ (subject), the khabar being omitted, its implied form being: "Is it that anyone, O company of Jews, should be given the like of what you were given of the Book and knowledge, that you believe in, or acknowledge, or mention to others, or spread among people?" and the like of what may fittingly be implied. This is on the view of whoever says «أزيد ضربته», and it is the less preferred view. So al-Wāḥidī implied it, following al-Fārisī. Better than this implied form, because it is the original, is: «أإتيان أحدٍ مثلَ ما أُوتيتم ممكنٌ أو مُصَدَّقٌ به» (is the giving to anyone of the like of what you were given possible, or believed in?).

The third: it is accusative by an implied verb which this latent verb explains, the question belonging to the chapter of ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb), the implied form being: «أَتَذْكُرون أَنْ يُؤْتَى أحد تذكرونه» (do you mention that anyone be given — do you mention it?), so «تذكرونه» explains the first «تذكرون», in the manner of «أزيداً ضربته»; then the last, explaining verb was dropped because the speech indicates it, and it is as though it were pronounced, and because it is equivalent to what is pronounced it can explain an implied verb. This question is explicitly stated in the texts. This is preferable to the view before it, because it is like «أزيداً ضربته», which is preferred on account of the element that requires a verb [Translator's note: i.e. the interrogative hamza]. Similar to the omission of this implied verb, because what precedes the interrogative indicates it, is the omission of the verb in His saying {آلآنَ وَقَدْ عَصَيْتَ} [Yūnus: 91]; it was said its implied form is: «الآن آمنت ورَجَعْتَ وتُبْتَ» (now you believe, return and repent?) and the like.

Al-Wāḥidī said: "If it is said: how is the entry of «أحد» found in this reading, when it has been cut off from negation and interrogation, and when the speech is cut off as affirmation and confirmation the entry of «أحد» is not permissible? It is said: it is possible that «أحد» in this place is the «أحد» found in e.g. «أحد وعشرين» (twenty-one), and this occurs in affirmation; do you not see that it means «واحد»? Abū al-ʿAbbās said: «أحد», «وَحَد» and «واحد» have one meaning."

His saying «أو يُحاجُّوكم»: «أو» in this reading means «حتى», the meaning of the speech being: "Is it that anyone be given the like of what you were given — you mention it to others, until they argue against you before your Lord?" Al-Farrāʾ said: "Similar in ordinary speech is: «تَعَلَّقْ به أو يُعْطِيَكَ حقك» (cling to him until he gives you your due); and similar is the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:

1335 - فَقُلْتُ له: لاَ تَبْكِ عَيْنُكَ إنما ... نحاوِلُ مُلْكاً أو نموتَ فَنُعْذَرَا
(I said to him: let your eye not weep; we only seek a kingdom, or [until] we die and are excused.)

i.e. «حتى». From this is His saying {لَيْسَ لَكَ مِنَ الأمر شَيْءٌ أَوْ يَتُوبَ عَلَيْهِمْ} [Āl ʿImrān: 128]." He said: "This is one view; better than it is to make it conjoined to the interrogative, the meaning being: is it that anyone be given the like of what you were given, or that anyone argue against you before Allah, that you believe him?" All this is the sense of al-Fārisī's statement. It is also possible that «أن يؤتى أحد» is accusative by an implied verb, not by way of explanation but by mere indication of meaning, its implied form being «أتذكرون أو أَتَشِيعونَ أَنْ يُؤْتَى أحدٌ» (do you mention, or do you spread abroad, that anyone be given …); al-Fārisī mentioned this too. This is the fourth view.

The fifth: «أَنْ يؤتى» in his reading is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, on the basis that it is included under «قل» [Translator's note: printed «تحت القول»], not part of what the group said; this is more evident than making it part of what the group said.

Al-Fārisī judged the reading of Ibn Kathīr weak, saying: "This is a place where the reading of those other than Ibn Kathīr ought to be preferred over the reading of Ibn Kathīr, because it is not regular in singular nouns that they indicate multiplicity."

Al-Aʿmash and Shuʿayb ibn Abī Ḥamza read «إنْ يؤتى» with kasra on the hamza, and al-Zamakhsharī explained it as the negating «إنْ». He said: "On the basis of the negating «إن», and it is connected with the speech of the People of the Book, i.e. do not believe except one who follows your religion, and say to them: no one is given the like of what you were given until they argue against you before your Lord — meaning they are not given its like, so they will not argue against you."

Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "This reading allows the speech to be an address from the group that said it, and their saying «أو يحاجُّوكم» means 'or let them argue against you', this being on the firm resolve that no one is given the like of what was given; or it may mean 'unless they argue against you', this being on the allowance that someone may be given that if the proof is established for him." So it appears from what Ibn ʿAṭiyya mentioned that «أو» in this reading may keep its proper sense of choice and variety, or may mean «إلاَّ»; except that it involves omitting the jussive particle while keeping its effect, which is not permissible. On the view of others it means «حتى».

Al-Ḥasan read «أَنْ يُؤْتى أحدٌ» with the verb in the active voice [Translator's note: so vocalized in print; the active voice would be «يُؤْتِي»]. When some reported this reading they did not specify «أن» with fatḥa or kasra, like Abū al-Baqāʾ; others did specify it, with kasra on «إنْ», and explained it as the negating «إنْ». The apparent meaning is that Allah's bestowal of favour is not resembled by the favour of any of His creatures, and it is an address from the Prophet ﷺ to his community. The object is omitted, its implied form being «إنْ يؤتي أحدٌ أحداً مثلَ ما أوتيتم» (no one gives anyone the like of what you were given); the first object, «أحداً», was omitted because the meaning indicates it, and the second was kept.

This is the summary of what people have said about this verse, with its differences, and praise belongs to Allah. Al-Wāḥidī said: "This verse is among the difficult passages of the Qurʾān and the hardest of it to interpret. I have reflected on the statements of the exegetes and the scholars of meanings (maʿānī) concerning this verse, and I have not found a view that runs consistently through this verse from its beginning to its end while explaining the meaning and keeping the composition sound."

semin-durr:37-37.t:
The words of the Exalted: {فَتَقَبَّلَهَا}: the majority read «تَقَبَّلها» as a past verb on the pattern tafaʿʿala, with the middle radical doubled, and «ربُّها» is its fāʿil (agent). Tafaʿʿala allows two aspects. The first: that it has the meaning of the bare verb, i.e.: and He accepted her (qabilahā), meaning He was pleased with her in place of the vowed male, and He had not accepted a vowed female like Maryam — so it came in the exegesis. Tafaʿʿala comes with the meaning of the bare faʿila, as in تَعَجَّب and عَجِب "to wonder at such-and-such", and تبرَّأ and بَرِىء "to be clear of it". The second: that tafaʿʿala has the meaning of istafʿala, i.e.: and her Lord received her (istaqbalahā); one says استقبلْتُ الشيء, i.e. I took it at its first instance. The meaning is that Allah took charge of her at the beginning of her affair and at the time of her birth. Of this are his words — he is al-Quṭāmī:
1244 - وخيرُ الأمرِ ما استقبَلْتَ منه ... وليس بأَنْ تَتَبَّعَه اتِّباعاً
(The best of a matter is what you take up from its start, not by following after it.)
And of it is the proverb: «خُذِ الأمر بقَوابله» ("take the matter at its beginnings"). Tafaʿʿala with the meaning of istafʿala is frequent, as in تَعَظَّم and استعظم, تكبَّر and استكبر, تَقَصَّيْت الشيء and استقصَيْتُه, تَعَجَّلَته and استَعْجَلْتُه.
The bāʾ in His words {بِقَبُولٍ} has two aspects. The first: that it is redundant (zāʾida), i.e.: قَبولاً; on this view «قبولاً» is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) that came with the additional letters dropped, for had it come according to تقبَّل, it would have been said تَقَبُّلا, as in تكبَّر تكبُّرا. Qabūl is one of the maṣdars that came on faʿūl with a fatḥa on the first radical; they were mentioned at the beginning of al-Baqara. One says: قَبِلْتُ الشيء قَبولاً. Al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj allowed a ḍamma on the qāf of «قبول», and that is the analogical form, like الدُّخول and الخُروج. Ibn al-Aʿrābī reported it from the Arabs: قبلته قَبولاً وقُبولاً, with fatḥa and ḍamma on the qāf, as heard from the Arabs; and «على وجهه قُبول» ("there is acceptability on his face") and nothing else, meaning it is said here only with ḍamma. They recited:
1245 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . والوجه عليه القُبول
(… and the face has acceptability upon it.)
with ḍamma on the qāf; so some reported it.
Al-Zajjāj said: "This «قبولاً» is not accusative by this verb so as to be a maṣdar not following its verb; rather it is accusative by a verb that corresponds to it, i.e. a bare one." He said: "The implied form is: so He received her with a fine reception (يتقبُّل حسن «[Translator's note: so in the text; evidently بتقبُّل]») and accepted her with a fine acceptance (قَبِلها قَبولاً حسناً), i.e.: He was pleased with her." And there is a remoteness in it.
The second aspect: that the bāʾ is not redundant but remains in its sense, and what is meant by al-qabūl here is a noun for that by which a thing is accepted, like «اللَّدود» for what is administered into the side of the mouth, and al-saʿūṭ for snuff. The meaning thereby is His singling her out by setting her in the place of the male in the vow.
His words: {وَأَنبَتَهَا نَبَاتاً}: نبات is also a maṣdar not following its verb, since the analogical form is إنبات. It was also said: rather it is accusative by a concealed verb that likewise corresponds to it, its implied form being: so she grew a fine growing.
His words: {وَكَفَّلَهَا}: the Kufans read «وكَفَّلَها» with the middle radical doubled and «زكريا» with the short ending, except Abū Bakr, who read it with the long ending like the rest, but in the accusative, while the rest read it nominative, as will come.
Mujāhid read «فتقبَّلْها» with a vowelless lām and «ربَّها» accusative, «أنبِتها» with kasra on the bāʾ and a vowelless tāʾ, and «كَفِّلْها» with kasra on the fāʾ and a vowelless lām. Ubayy read «وأَكْفَلَها», like «أَكْرَمَها», as a past verb.
ʿAbd Allāh al-Muzanī read «وكَفِلَها» with kasra on the fāʾ and without doubling.
As for the reading of the Kufans, they made the verb transitive to two objects by the doubling, the second of them being «زكريا». Those who read it short, like the two brothers (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) and Ḥafṣ, have it with an implied accusative, and those who read it long, like Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim, show the fatḥa on it; and that is how I recited it.
As for the reading of the rest of the Seven, كَفَلَ is light according to them and transitive to one object, namely the pronoun of Maryam, and its fāʿil is «زكريا». There is no contradiction between the two readings, because when Allah made him her guardian, he became her guardian. In their reading it is long and nominative as the fāʿil.
As for the reading «أَكْفَلَها», he made it transitive by the hamza just as others made it transitive by doubling, as in خَرَّجْته and أَخْرجته, كَرَّمته and أَكْرمته. This is like the reading of the Kufans in meaning and parsing: the fāʿil is Allah the Exalted, the first object is the pronoun of Maryam, and the second is «زكريا».
As for the reading «وكَفِلها» with kasra on the fāʾ, it is a dialectal form of كَفَلَ. One says كَفَلَ يَكْفُل, like قَتَل يقتُل, which is the widespread form, and كَفِلَ يَكْفَلُ, like عَلِمَ يَعْلَم, on which this reading is based. Its parsing is like that of the reading of the majority, with «زكريا» as the fāʿil.
As for the reading of Mujāhid, all of it is in the wording of a prayer from Maryam's mother to Allah the Exalted that He do for her what she asked of Him. «ربَّها» is accusative as one addressed in the vocative, i.e.: so accept her, O her Lord, and make her grow and give her into guardianship, O her Lord. «زكريا» in this reading is likewise a second object, as in the reading of the Kufans.
Ḥafṣ and the two brothers read «زكريا» with the short ending wherever it occurs in the Qurʾān, and the rest of the Seven with the long ending. The long and short endings in this name are two widespread dialectal forms from the people of the Ḥijāz. It is a foreign noun, so they ought to have said of it: it is a diptote because of being a proper name and foreign, like its counterparts; yet they said only: it is a diptote because of the presence of the feminine alif in it, either the long one as in حَمْراء or the short one as in حُبْلى. What seems to have compelled them to that is that they saw it treated as a diptote both when definite and when indefinite. They said: if its diptote status were because of being a proper name and foreign, it would be declinable when indefinite, since one of the two causes of prevention would be gone; but the Arabs treated it as a diptote when indefinite, so we knew that the preventing cause is something else, and there is nothing here that is fit to prevent its declension except the feminine alif. They mean the likeness to the feminine alif; otherwise this is a foreign noun of which no derivation is known, such that it could be claimed that the alif in it is feminine. Moreover, Abū Ḥātim held that it is declinable when indefinite, as though he regarded in it what I set out earlier, foreignness and being a proper name; but they judged him mistaken and wrong in that.
Al-Fārisī said, discussing it at length: "The hamza in it must be either for the feminine, or for annexing to a pattern (ilḥāq), or changed from another letter. It cannot be changed, because the change must be either from a root letter or from a letter of ilḥāq. It cannot be from a root letter, because yāʾ and wāw are not root letters in what consists of four letters; nor can it be from a letter of ilḥāq, because there is nothing among the root patterns to which this could be annexed. Once that is established, it is established that it is for the feminine; and the same is said of the short alif."
What Abū ʿAlī said is sound if it were among words of which a derivation is known and which admit morphological inflection; but they treat foreign nouns the way Arabic ones are treated, in the sense of: if this occurred in the tongue of the Arabs, what would its rule be?
Beyond that there are two other dialectal forms of it. One of them: زَكَرِيٌّ, with a doubled yāʾ at its end only «[Translator's note: the text has فقد, evidently for فقط, "only"]», without alif; in this dialect it is declinable. Abū ʿAlī explained it, saying: "The account of it is that the two yāʾs that were in it, in the long and short forms, and what came after them were dropped, and the two yāʾs of relation (nisba) were attached." He said: "What shows that is the declension of the noun; had the two yāʾs been the ones that were in it, it would have had to be a diptote because of foreignness and definiteness." This dialect I have mentioned is the dialect of the people of Najd and those adjoining them. The second: «زَكْرٍ», on the pattern of عَمْرٍو; al-Akhfash reported it.
Al-kafāla is originally surety (al-ḍamān); then it is borrowed for joining (to oneself) and taking (into care). One says from it: كَفَل يكفُل and كَفِلَ يكفَل, like عَلِمَ يعلَم, كَفالة and كَفْلاً, so he is كافِل and كفيل.
His words: {المحراب}: there are two well-known aspects in it. The first, which is the position of Sībawayh, is that it is accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), and it departs from all its fellows specifically after «دخل». He means that every specified adverb of place is reached by the verb only through «في», as in «صَلَّيْت في المحراب» ("I prayed in the miḥrāb") — you do not say المحرابَ — and «نمت في السوق» ("I slept in the market") — you do not say السوقَ — except specifically with «دخل», as in دَخَلْتُ السوقَ والبيت ("I entered the market and the house"), and except other words which I mentioned in books of grammar. The second is the position of al-Akhfash: that what comes after «دخل» is accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), not as an adverb; so your saying «دخلت البيت» is like your saying «هَدَمْتُ البيت» ("I demolished the house") in that each is accusative as a direct object. This is the less preferred view, as shown by the fact that if «دخل» were applied to something other than a specified adverb, it would have to reach it through «في»: you say «دخلْتُ في الأمر» ("I entered into the matter") and not دخلت الأمر; this shows that it does not pass to a direct object by itself.
Al-miḥrāb: Abū ʿUbayda said: "It is the noblest of sitting places and the front of them, and it is so with respect to the mosque." Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ said: "It is the palace, because of its height and nobility." Al-Aṣmaʿī said: "It is the upper chamber," and he recited, from Imruʾ al-Qays:
1246 - وماذا عليه أَنْ ذكرتُ أوانساً ... كغِزْلانِ رملٍ في محاريبِ أَقْيالِ
(What harm is it to him that I mentioned gentle maidens like the gazelles of the sands, in the chambers of princes?)
They said: its meaning is: in the upper chambers of princes. Another recited, from ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa «[Translator's note: the text has ربعية, a slip for ربيعة]»:
1247 - رَبَّةُ مِحْرابٍ إذا جئتُها ... لم أدْنُ حتى أَرْتَقِي سُلَّما
(Mistress of a high chamber: when I come to her, I cannot draw near until I climb a ladder.)
It was also said: it is the miḥrāb of the known mosque, and that is most fitting for the verse. As for what I mentioned from those before, they mean by it the miḥrāb as such; as for this verse, no disagreement appears among them [over] its being the familiar miḥrāb. It was said: its derivation is from al-ḥarb (war), because people fight over it.
Ibn Dhakwān from Ibn ʿĀmir read «المحراب» with imāla (inclination of the alif) in two places in this sūra without disagreement, because the cause of imāla is strong in it: the alif is preceded by a kasra and followed by another kasra, so the motive for imāla is strengthened. This is unlike «المحراب» when not genitive, for both aspects are transmitted from Ibn Dhakwān in it, imāla and its absence, as in His words {إِذْ تَسَوَّرُواْ المحراب} [Ṣād: 21]: the reason for imāla is the preceding kasra, and the reason for full pronunciation (tafkhīm) is that it is the original. The difference has been given to you between its being genitive, where no disagreement is reported from him, and its not being genitive, where the disagreement applies. Likewise the disagreement from him also applies in «عمران», for the reason I mentioned, namely the preceding kasra.
His words: {وَجَدَ عِندَهَا رِزْقاً}: this «وَجَدَ» means "to come upon, meet, encounter", so it is transitive to one object, namely «رزقاً». «عندَها» is evidently an adverb of the finding. Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed it to be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «رزقاً», because it is fit to be an adjective of it originally; on this view it is attached to an omitted element. «وَجَدَ» is what puts كلما in the accusative, since it is adverbial; this has been verified earlier. Abū al-Baqāʾ called it its apodosis, because in his view it resembles a condition, as will come.
His words: «قال: يا مريم»: there are two aspects in it. The first: that it is resumptive. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It cannot be a badal (substitute) from «وَجَدَ», because it does not have its meaning." The second: that it is conjoined with fāʾ, and the conjunction was omitted. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "As it is omitted in the apodosis of a condition, as in His words {وَإِنْ أَطَعْتُمُوهُمْ إِنَّكُمْ لَمُشْرِكُونَ} [al-Anʿām: 121], and likewise the words of the poet:
1248 - مَنْ يَفعلِ الحسناتِ اللهُ يَشْكرها ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Whoever does good deeds, Allah will reward them …)
This place resembles the apodosis of a condition, because «كلما» resembles a condition in requiring an apodosis." End. I say: what he said is questionable, in that he imagined that in the words of the Exalted {وَإِنْ أَطَعْتُمُوهُمْ} the apodosis is «إنكم لمشركون» itself, with the fāʾ dropped from it. That is not so; rather the apodosis is omitted, and «إنكم لمشركون» is the answer of an implied oath before the condition — the verification of this question has preceded. So this is not at all among the cases where the fāʾ of the apodosis is dropped. How can he claim that and equate it with the line mentioned, when that is permissible only under poetic necessity? Furthermore, what appears is that the clause «وَجَدَ» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the fāʿil of «دخل», and the apodosis of «كلما» is «قال» itself, the implied form being: whenever Zakariyyā entered upon her, finding provision with her, he said. This is very clear. «رزقاً» was made indefinite to magnify it, or to indicate by it a certain kind of it.
His words: {أنى لَكِ هذا}: أنَّى is a fronted khabar (predicate) and «هذا» a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). The meaning of «أنى» here is "from where"; so Abū ʿUbayda explained it. It was also said: it may be a question about the manner, i.e.: how was this made ready for you? Al-Kumayt said:
1249 - أنَّى ومِنْ أين آبَكَ الطربُ ... مِنْ حيثُ لا صبوةٌ ولا رِيَبُ
(How and from where has longing come back to you, from where there is neither youthful passion nor doubts?)
Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed «أَنَّى» to be accusative as an adverb by the "being established" (al-istiqrār) contained in «لك», with «لك» making «هذا» nominative — he means as a fāʿil; there is no need for that. The discussion of «أنَّى» has preceded in al-Baqara.
{إنًّ الله يَرْزُقُ مَن يَشَآءُ}: its like has preceded. It may be resumptive [from the words of Allah the Exalted, or it may be from the words of Maryam, so that it is in the accusative position].

semin-durr:75-75.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {مَّنْ إِن تَأْمَنْهُ}: «مَنْ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «من أهل» its khabar (predicate), placed before it. «مَنْ» is either a relative noun or an indefinite noun. «إِنْ تَأْمَنْهُ يُؤدِّه» — this conditional clause is either a ṣila (relative clause), and so has no grammatical position, or an adjective, and so its position is nominative.

Ubayy read «تِئْمَنْهُ» in both places, and {مَا لَكَ لاَ تَأْمَنَّا} [Yūsuf: 11], with kasra on the prefix of the imperfect; so too Ibn Masʿūd and al-Ashhab al-ʿUqaylī, except that these two replaced the hamza with yāʾ.
