I think the Shaykh imagined that it was nominative, emphasis for the pronoun in «قُتلوا», and did not notice that he implied it only as an accusative first object. As for his making his statement go through on the majority's position, that suffices him; and what is it to him about Ibn Malkūn? There will come places where he and others are compelled to omit one of the two objects, as you will see shortly. The discussion on the root «حَسِب», its dialects and readings, has already preceded.
Ibn ʿĀmir read «قُتِّلوا» with shadda, and Hishām alone in «لو أطاعونا ما قُتِّلوا»; the rest read it without shadda. The shadda is for intensification, and the lightened form is fit for that.
The majority read «أحياءٌ» in the nominative, i.e. "rather they are alive". Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «أحياءً». Abū l-Baqāʾ analysed it in two ways. One: that it is conjoined to «أمواتاً». He said: "as you say: 'I supposed Zayd standing, rather sitting'." The second, to which al-Zamakhsharī also went: that it is accusative by an implied verb, its implied form being "rather I suppose them alive". This aspect was preceded to by Abū Isḥāq al-Zajjāj, except that al-Fārisī rejected it from him in «al-Ighfāl». He said: "Because the matter is settled, it is not permissible to be commanded in it with supposing, and nothing can be implied for it except a verb of supposing. So the way to Ibn Abī ʿAbla's reading is that you imply a verb other than supposing: 'consider them' or 'make them', and that is weak, since there is no indication in the speech of what is implied." End of quotation.
This is prejudice from Abū ʿAlī. As for his saying "the matter is settled", he means that their being alive is a certain matter, so how can one say of it "I suppose them", with a verb that requires doubt? That is not necessary, because «حَسِبَ» sometimes comes for certainty. He said:
1491 - حَسِبْتُ التُّقَى والجودَ خيرَ تجارةٍ ... رَباحاً إذا ما المرءُ أَصبح ثاقِلا
(I reckoned piety and generosity the best trade, in profit, when a man becomes weighed down.)
And another said:
1492 - شهدْتِ وفاتوني وكنتُ حَسِبْتُني ... فقيراً إلى أَنْ يَشْهدوا وتَغِيبي
(You were present and they missed me, and I had reckoned myself in need that they be present and you be absent.)
So «حَسِب» in these two verses is for certainty, because the meaning requires that. And his saying "that is weak" means from the standpoint of the lack of verbal indication, and it is not so; rather, when the meaning guides to something, that thing is implied because the meaning indicates it, without weakness, even though indication by the wording is better. As for his implication "or make them", the Shaykh said: "This is not valid at all, whether you make «أجْعَلْهم» mean 'create them' or 'turn them into' or 'name them' or 'find them'."
His saying: {عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ}: There are five aspects in it. One: that it is a second khabar of «أحياءٌ» according to the majority's reading. Second: that it is an adverb of «أحياء», because the meaning is "they live with their Lord". Third: that it is an adverb of «يُرْزقون», that is, their provision takes place in this noble location. Fourth: that it is an adjective of «أحياء», so it is in the position of nominative on the majority's reading and accusative on Ibn Abī ʿAbla's reading. Fifth: that it is a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in «أحياء»; and what is meant by "with" (ʿindiyya) is figurative, for their nearness by honour. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is on the omission of a muḍāf, that is: with the honour of their Lord"; there is no need of it, because the first is more fitting.
His saying: {يُرْزَقُونَ}: There are four aspects in it. One: that it be a third khabar of «أحياء», or a second if the adverb is not made a khabar. Second: that it is an adjective of «أحياء» in the two senses mentioned earlier; and if we also parse the adverb as an adjective, this came in the best order, namely that when a noun is qualified by an adverb and a sentence, the better is to put the adverb and its equivalent first, because it is nearer to the singular. Third: that it is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «أحياء», that is: "they live provided for". Fourth: that it is a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in the adverb, and the operator in it is in truth the operator in the adverb. Abū l-Baqāʾ said of this aspect: "It may be a ḥāl from the adverb if you make it an adjective", that is: if you make the adverb (an adjective). That is not specific to making it an adjective only; rather, if you made it a ḥāl that would also be permissible, and this is called the nested ḥāl (al-ḥāl al-mutadākhila); and if you made it a khabar it would be the same.

semin-durr:170-170.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {فَرِحِينَ}: There are five aspects in it. One: that it is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «أحياءٌ». Second: from the pronoun in the adverb. Third: from the pronoun in «يُرْزَقون». Fourth: that it is accusative as praise. Fifth: that it is an adjective of «أحياء», and this is specific to Ibn Abī ʿAbla's reading. «بما» is attached to «فرحين».
His saying: {مِن فَضْلِهِ}: There are two views about «مِنْ». One: that its meaning is causal (sababiyya), that is: "because of His bounty", that is, what Allah gave them is caused by His bounty. Second: that it is for the beginning of the range (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya), and on these two aspects it is attached to «آتاهم». Third: that it is partitive, that is, "some of His bounty", and on this it is attached to an omitted word as a ḥāl from the pronoun returning to the relative noun, which was omitted; the implied form is: "with what He gave them, being from His bounty".
His saying: {وَيَسْتَبْشِرُونَ}: There are four aspects in it. One: that it falls under the conjunction of a verb on a noun because the verb is in its interpretation, so it is conjoined to «فرحين», as though it had been said: "rejoicing and glad of tidings", and they compared it to His saying, the Exalted: {فَوْقَهُمْ صَافَّاتٍ وَيَقْبِضْنَ} [الملك: 19]. The second: that it also [falls] under the conjunction of a verb on a noun, but because the noun is in the interpretation of a verb. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It is conjoined to «فرحين», because the active participle here resembles the imperfect verb", meaning that «فرحين» is equal to «يفرحون», and it is as though he made it fall under His saying: {إِنَّ المصدقين والمصدقات وَأَقْرَضُواْ} [الحديد: 18]. The first implication is preferable, because for the noun «فرحين» we have no necessity to put it in the place of an imperfect verb so as to interpret the noun by it, the verb being a branch of it, so the branch should be returned to it; we did that in the verse only because the «أل» that is a relative noun has the meaning of «الذي», and «الذي» is connected only with a sentence or its equivalent, and that equivalent is in truth interpreted as a sentence.
Third: that it is resumptive, the wāw being for conjunction, conjoining a verbal sentence upon a nominal one.
Fourth: that it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is: "and they are glad of tidings", and then two aspects are allowed. One: that the sentence is a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in «فرحين» or from the omitted returning pronoun of «آتاهم»; we needed to imply a mubtadaʾ when making it a ḥāl only because the affirmative imperfect may not be joined with the wāw of ḥāl, as has preceded more than once. The second of these two aspects: that it is resumptive, conjoining a nominal sentence upon its like.
«استفعل» here is not for seeking (ṭalab), but has the meaning of the base form, like "Allah is self-sufficient (istaghnā) and the markh and ʿafār trees are glorious (istamjada)", meaning ghaniya and majuda. "The man was glad (bashira)" with kasra on the middle letter has also been heard, so istabshara would be of the same meaning; so said Ibn ʿAṭiyya. It is also possible that it be the passive-reflexive (muṭāwiʿ) of absharā, like "akanahu fastakāna" [Translator's note: the printed word is as in the source and is evidently corrupt; the intended example is a verb followed by its reflexive form], "arāḥahu fastarāḥa, ashlāhu fastashlā, aḥkamahu fastaḥkama", and it is frequent. The Shaykh made it the more evident, since the muṭāwaʿa indicates being affected by another, so the glad tidings came to them through Allah the Exalted's giving them glad tidings; and this is not necessary if it has the meaning of the base form.
His saying: {مِّنْ خَلْفِهِمْ}: There are two views about this preposition phrase. One: that it is attached to «يَلْحقوا», in the sense that they remained after them, while the latter had gone before them. The second: that it is attached to an omitted word as a ḥāl from the agent of «يلحقوا», that is: "they have not joined them, being left behind them", that is, in life.
His saying: {أَلاَّ خَوْفٌ}: There are two views about it. One: that «أَنْ» and what is within its scope are in the position of genitive, a badal for «بالذين», a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl), that is: "they rejoice at the absence of fear and grief for them", so that is the thing rejoiced at in truth, because persons are not rejoiced at. The second: that it is in the position of accusative as an object of purpose, that is: "because there is no fear for them". This «أَنْ» is the lightened one, its noun is the pronoun of the affair, and the negative sentence after it is in the position of the khabar; and persons are not rejoiced at, as has preceded, so a suitable muḍāf must be omitted, the implied form being: "and they rejoice at the safety of those, or their joining them in rank".
Makkī said, after relating that it is a badal of inclusion: "«أَنْ» may be in the position of accusative, in the sense of «بأن لا»." This is exactly the earlier badal aspect, the most that can be said being that he repeated the operator with the badal in his implication; unless he means that although it is a badal of «الذين», it is not in the position of genitive but accusative, because the bāʾ dropped from it, for the origin is «بأَنْ لا», and «أَنْ», when the preposition is dropped from it, is in the position of accusative in the view of Sībawayh and al-Farrāʾ. It is remote.

semin-durr:171-171.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَأَنَّ الله لاَ يُضِيعُ}: Al-Kisāʾī read «إنَّ» with kasra, as resumptive. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The reading with kasra is parenthetical." It was thought problematic that it be parenthetical, because it does not occur between two things that are mutually necessary. It could be answered that «الذين استجابوا» may be a follower of «الذين لم يلحقوا», as an adjective or badal, as will come; on this the parenthesis can be conceived. Supporting its being resumptive is the reading of ʿAbd Allāh (ibn Masʿūd) in his codex: «والله لا يُضيع». The rest of the Seven read it with fatḥa, as a conjunction upon His saying «بنعمةٍ», because it is in the interpretation of a maṣdar, that is: "they rejoice at a favour from Allah and a bounty from Him, and Allah's not wasting the reward of the believers."
His saying: {يَسْتَبْشِرُونَ} without a conjunction has several aspects. One: that it is resumptive, relating to them themselves, not to «الذين لم يلحقوا بهم», because of the difference in what the two glad tidings relate to. The second: that it is emphasis for the first, because by the favour and bounty he intended to explain what the first rejoicing relates to; to this al-Zamakhsharī went. Third: that it is a badal for the first verb, and the meaning of its being a badal is that, since what it relates to is an explanation of what the first relates to, it is good to say "a badal of it"; otherwise how can a verb be substituted for a verb that agrees with it in wording and meaning? In meaning this reverts to the emphasis aspect. Fourth: that it is a ḥāl from the agent of «يحزنون», and «يحزنون» operates in it, that is: "nor do they grieve, while being glad of tidings of a favour". It is remote for two reasons. One: that the apparent sense is that those of whom grief is negated differ from those who rejoice. The second: that the negation of grief is not restricted, so as to be more eloquent in the glad tidings, whereas the ḥāl is a restriction in it, so this meaning would be lost.

semin-durr:172-172.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {الذين استجابوا}: There are six aspects in it. One: that it is a mubtadaʾ and its khabar is His saying {لِلَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُواْ مِنْهُمْ واتقوا أَجْرٌ}. Makkī said here: "and its khabar is {مِن بَعْدِ مَآ أَصَابَهُمُ القرح}." This is a mistake, because this is not at all informative; rather «مِنْ بعد» is attached to «استجابوا». The second: the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, that is: "they are the ones who". The third: that it is accusative by an implied "I mean" (aʿnī). These two aspects are both covered by your term "cutting off" (qaṭʿ). The fourth: that it is a badal for «المؤمنين». The fifth: that it is a badal for «الذين لم يلحقوا»; so said Makkī. The sixth: that it is a badal for «المؤمنين» [Translator's note: the source repeats the fourth aspect here]. A seventh aspect is also allowed in it: that it be an adjective of His saying «الذين لم يلحقوا», by analogy with making it a badal of them according to Makkī. «ما» in «بعدما أصابَهم» is a maṣdar particle, and «للذين أحسنوا» is a fronted khabar.
As for «منهم», there are two views about it. One: that it is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «أحسنوا», and on this «مِنْ» is partitive. The second: that it is to explain the kind (bayān al-jins). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Like it in His saying {وَعَدَ الله الذين آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ الصالحات مِنْهُم} [الفتح: 29], because those who responded have all done good and been godfearing, not only some of them." «أجرٌ» is a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the sentence made of this mubtadaʾ and its khabar is either resumptive, or a ḥāl if we do not parse «الذين استجابوا» as a mubtadaʾ, or a khabar if we parse it as a mubtadaʾ, as its exposition has preceded.

semin-durr:13-13.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {قَدْ كَانَ}: the response to an omitted oath. {آيةٌ} is the ism (subject) of kāna. The verb is not made feminine because the feminine of āya is figurative (not true feminine), because it is in the sense of "proof" and "evidence", and because of the separation by «لكم»; for the separation justifies that even when the feminine is a true feminine, as in his saying:

1187 - إنَّ امرَأً غَرَّه منكنَّ واحدةٌ ... بَعْدي وبعدكِ في الدنيا لمغرورُ
(Indeed a man deceived by one of you women after me and after you in this world is surely deluded.)

In the khabar (predicate) of kāna there are two views. The first: that it is «لكم», and «في فئتين» is in the position of nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of «آية». The second: that it is «في فئتين». Then there are two views on «لكم»: the first, that it is attached to an omitted word as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «آية», because it was originally an adjective of «آية» and when it was fronted it became accusative as a ḥāl; the second, that it is attached to kāna, mentioned by Abū l-Baqāʾ, and this is according to one who holds that it governs adverbs and prepositions. But in making «في فئتين» the khabar there is a difficulty, namely that the ruling on the ism of kāna is the ruling on the mubtadaʾ, so only what may begin a sentence may be its ism; and here, if «آية» were made a mubtadaʾ and what follows it a khabar, it would not be permissible, as there is no justification for beginning with this indefinite noun; unlike when you make «لكم» the khabar, for that is permissible because of the presence of the justification, namely that the khabar, a preposition and its genitive noun, is fronted.

His saying: {التقتا}: in the position of genitive as a naʿt of «فئتين», that is: "two groups meeting".

His saying: {فِئَةٌ تُقَاتِلُ}: the majority read «فئة» in the nominative, and it has several views. The first: that it is nominative as a badal (substitute) for the agent of {التقتا}; on this an omitted pronoun referring to the two groups mentioned earlier is necessary, to justify the description by a clause, since without it being implied it would not be sound, as the descriptive clause would lack a pronoun; the implied form being: "in two groups that met: one group of them and another, disbelieving." The second: that it is nominative as the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, its implied form being: "one of them is a group fighting"; so he severed the speech from its beginning and made it a fresh start. Like it is what al-Farrāʾ recited for that:

1188 - إذا مِتُّ كان الناسُ صِنْفَيْنِ شامتٌ ... وآخرُ مُثْنٍ بالذي كنتُ أصنعُ
(When I die people will be two kinds: one gloating, and another praising what I used to do.)

that is: one of them is gloating and another is praising, that is, "and another kind is praising". Like it in severance also is the saying of another:

1189 - حتى إذا ما استقلَّ النجمُ في غَلَسٍ ... وغُودر البقلُ مَلْوِيٌّ ومَحْصودُ
(Until, when the star rose in the dark before dawn, and the herbage was left, some twisted and some reaped.)

that is: part of it twisted and part reaped. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "If you ask: when you imply «إحداهما» (one of them) as the mubtadaʾ in the first, the rule would be 'and the other', that is 'and the other group disbelieving'? It is said: since it is known that the division here is of the very thing whose mention preceded, definiteness and indefiniteness are the same." I say: the like of the noble verse in this question and its answer is the verse that preceded: «شامتٌ وآخرُ مُثْنٍ», where he brought it indefinite without the article.

The third: that it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is implied, its implied form being: "from them is a group fighting"; and likewise in the verse, that is: "among them one gloating and among them one praising". Like it is the saying of al-Nābigha:

1190 - تَوَهَّمْتُ آياتٍ لها فَعَرَفْتُها ... لستةِ أعوامٍ وذا العامُ سابعُ
(I made out signs of hers and recognized them after six years, and this is the seventh year.)
رمادٌ ككحل العينِ لأْياً أُبينُه ... ونُؤْيٌ كجِذْمِ الحَوْضِ أثلمُ خاشع
(Ashes like eye-kohl that I could barely discern, and a trench like the stump of a basin, notched and lowly.)

its implied form being "from them", that is, "among the signs are ashes, and among them a trench"; and the verse may bear what preceded of its being implied as a mubtadaʾ, with «رمادٌ» its khabar, as preceded in its parallel.

Al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid and Ḥumayd read «فئةٍ تقاتل» in the genitive as a badal of «فئتين», and this badal is called badal tafṣīl (distributive substitute), like the saying of Kuthayyir ʿAzza:

1191 - وكنتُ كذي رجلين رجلٍ صحيحةٍ ... ورجلٍ رَمَى فيها الزمانُ فَشَلَّتِ
(I was like one with two legs, one leg sound, and one that time struck so that it withered.)

It is a badal baʿḍ min kull (part for whole), and when that is so, a pronoun referring to what is substituted for is necessary, its implied form being: "a group of them".

Ibn al-Samayfaʿ and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «فئةً» in the accusative. It has four views. The first: accusative by an implied "I mean" (أعني). The second: accusative for praise. The verification of this view is to say: for praise in the first and for blame in the second, as if it were said: "I praise a group fighting in the way of Allah, and I blame another, disbelieving." The third: that it is accusative for specification (ikhtiṣāṣ); al-Zamakhsharī permitted it. The Shaykh said: "It is not good; because what is accusative [for specification] is neither indefinite nor vague." I say: al-Zamakhsharī does not mean the specification that has a chapter in grammar, such as "We, the company of prophets, are not inherited from"; he meant only the accusative by a suitable implied verb, and the people of bayān call this kind ikhtiṣāṣ. The fourth: that «فئةً» is accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of {التقتا}, as if it were said: "they met, one believing and one disbelieving"; on this «فئةً» and «أخرى» are a preface to the ḥāl (tawṭiʾa), because the aim is to mention its description, and this is like their saying "Zayd came to me, a righteous man", and like it in the chapter of predication: {بَلْ أَنْتُمْ قَوْمٌ مُّسْرِفُونَ} [al-Aʿrāf: 81] and the like.

His saying: {وأخرى كَافِرَةٌ}: «أُخْرى» is an adjective of an omitted described noun, the implied form being «وفئةٌ أخرى كافرةٌ». «كافرة» was read in the nominative and the genitive according to the two readings mentioned in «فئة تقاتل», and this is conjoined to it; and it would have been proper for one who read «فِئَةً تقاتل» in the accusative to read «وأخرى كافرةً» in the accusative, conjoined to the first, but I have not memorized that for them. In al-Zamakhsharī's wording there is something that suggests a reading with it, for he said: "It was also read «فئة تقاتل وأخرى كافرة» in the genitive as a badal of «فئتين», and in the accusative for specification or as ḥāl"; the apparent sense of his saying "and in the accusative" is [that is: in all that preceded, namely «فئة تقاتل وأخرى كافرة»]. The question of Abū l-Baqāʾ has preceded, namely why He did not say «والأخرى» with the article, I mean in the case of the nominative of «فئةُ تقاتل» as the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ whose implied form is «إحداهما», and the answer to it.

The majority read «تقاتل» in the feminine, because the verb is attributed to a feminine pronoun, and whenever it is attributed to a feminine pronoun, it must be feminine, whether the feminine is true or figurative, as in "al-shams ṭalaʿat" (the sun rose); this is the position of the majority. Ibn Kaysān differed and permitted "al-shams ṭalaʿa", citing the saying of the poet:

1192 - فلا مُزْنَةٌ وَدَقَتْ وَدْقَها ... ولا أرضَ أبقلَ إبقالَها
(No cloud has rained its rain, and no land has put forth herbage as hers has.)

He said «أبقل», which is attributed to the pronoun of the land, and did not say «أبقلَتْ»; others restrict it to poetic necessity. He said: "There is no necessity, for he could have transferred the vowel of the hamza to the silent feminine tāʾ and said: 'wa-lā arḍa abqalati bqālahā'." They rejected him: that necessity does not mean that; and even if we concede that, we do not concede that this poet's dialect included transfer (naql), because naql is not the dialect of all the Arabs.

Mujāhid and Muqātil read «يقاتل» with the yāʾ of the masculine, which is analyzed according to the position of Ibn Kaysān and strengthens it. They said: what made this good is that «فئة» is in the sense of "folk" and "people", and for that reason the pronoun returned to it as masculine.

His saying: {يَرَوْنَهُمْ}: Nāfiʿ alone of the Seven, Yaʿqūb and Sahl read «تَرَوْنهم» in the second person; the rest of the Seven read it in the third person. As for Nāfiʿ's reading, it has eight views. The first: that the pronoun in «لكم» and the nominative one in «تَرَوْنهم» are for the believers, and the accusative pronoun in «تَرَوْنهم» and the genitive one in «مِثْلَيْهم» are for the disbelievers. The meaning is: "There was for you, O believers, a sign in two groups, in that you saw the disbelievers as twice their own number", and this is greater in power, in that the believers saw the disbelievers at twice the number of the disbelievers, and nevertheless they were victorious over them, overcame them and inflicted on them what they inflicted. Like it: {كَم مِّن فِئَةٍ قَلِيلَةٍ غَلَبَتْ فِئَةٍ كَثِيرَةً بِإِذْنِ الله} [al-Baqara: 249]. Some of them considered this interpretation remote because of His saying, Exalted is He, in al-Anfāl: {وَإِذْ يُرِيكُمُوهُمْ إِذِ التقيتم في أَعْيُنِكُمْ قَلِيلاً} [verse 44], since the story is one, and the verse there indicates that Allah the Exalted made the polytheists few in the eyes of the believers so that they would not be cowardly toward them, whereas on the interpretation mentioned here He would have made them many in their eyes. It may be answered by the difference of two states, namely that at one time He showed them to them as twice their number in order to test and try them, then made them few in their eyes so that they would advance upon them; so it is the bringing of two considerations. Like it: {فَيَوْمَئِذٍ لاَّ يُسْأَلُ عَن ذَنبِهِ إِنسٌ وَلاَ جَآنٌّ} [al-Raḥmān: 39] with {فَوَرَبِّكَ لَنَسْأَلَنَّهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ} [al-Ḥijr: 92], and {وَلاَ يَكْتُمُونَ الله حَدِيثاً} [al-Nisāʾ: 42] with {هذا يَوْمُ لاَ يَنطِقُونَ} [al-Mursalāt: 35]. Al-Farrāʾ said: "What is meant by making few is belittling, as in your saying 'I saw their many as few' because of their insignificance in your eyes; it has nothing to do with reducing the number."

The second: that the address in «تَرَوْنهم» is to the believers also, and the accusative pronoun in «ترونهم» is for the disbelievers also, and the genitive pronoun in «مِثْلَيْهم» is for the believers, and the meaning is: "You see, O believers, the disbelievers as twice your own number." This is a reduction of the disbelievers in the believers' eyes (in the sight of the eye), in that the disbelievers were a thousand and more and the Muslims a third of them, so He showed them to them as twice their number, according to what was established for them of the standing of one against two in His saying, Exalted is He: {فَإِن يَكُنْ مِّنكُمْ مِّئَةٌ صَابِرَةٌ يَغْلِبُواْ مِئَتَيْنِ} [al-Anfāl: 66], after they had been charged that one should stand against ten in His saying, Exalted is He: {إِن يَكُن مِّنكُمْ عِشْرُونَ صَابِرُونَ يَغْلِبُواْ مِئَتَيْنِ} [al-Anfāl: 65]. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The reading of Nāfiʿ does not support this interpretation," and he did not explain the reason for the lack of support; and the reason in that, and Allah knows best, is that the construction ought to have been «تَرَوْنهم مثليكم» with the second person in «مثليكم», not the third. Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Fāsī said, after what I mentioned from al-Zamakhsharī: "I say: rather it supports it if the address in the verse is to the Muslims, and that has been said." End of quotation. Abū ʿAbd Allāh brought no answer, since the difficulty remains.

Some of them answered that with two answers. The first: that it is a case of iltifāt (shift of address) from the second person to the third, and that the proper speech was «مِثْلَيْكم» in the second person, but he shifted to the third; and he likened it to His saying, Exalted is He: {حتى إِذَا كُنتُمْ فِي الفلك وَجَرَيْنَ بِهِم} [Yūnus: 22]. The second: that the pronoun in «مِثْلَيْهم», although what is meant by it is the believers, refers back to His saying {فِئَةٌ تُقَاتِلُ فِي سَبِيلِ الله}, and the fighting group is an expression for the believers addressed; and the meaning is: "You see, O believers, the disbelieving group as twice the group fighting in the way of Allah", as if it were said: "you see them, O believers, as twice yourselves". This is a good answer and a clear meaning.

The third: that the address in «لكم» and in «تَرَوْنَهم» is to the disbelievers, namely Quraysh, and the accusative and genitive pronouns are for the believers, that is: "There was for you, O polytheists, a sign in that you see the believers as twice your own number", so He would have made them many in the eyes of the disbelievers so that they would be cowardly toward them; and the question mentioned between this verse and the verse of al-Anfāl, namely His saying, Exalted is He, {وَيُقَلِّلُكُمْ في أَعْيُنِهِمْ} [al-Anfāl: 44], returns: how can it be said here that He made them many? And the answer returns, by what preceded of the difference of two states, namely that He made them few at first so that the disbelievers would be emboldened against them, and when the two armies met, He made them many in their eyes so that weakness and failure would befall them.

The fourth: like the third, except that the pronoun in «مِثْلَيْهم» returns to the polytheists, so that question returns, namely that it ought to have been said «مِثْليكم» for the speech to agree; and the two answers return, which are either the shift from the second person to the third, or its returning to the wording of the disbelieving group, because it is an expression for the polytheists, just as that pronoun was an expression for the fighting group; and the implied form would be: "You see, O polytheists, the believers as twice your disbelieving group." On this they would have seen the believers as twice the polytheists themselves, two thousand and more; and this is reinforcement from Allah the Exalted, in that He showed the disbelievers the believers at twice the number of the polytheists until they failed and became cowardly, so the Muslims were encouraged against them and were victorious over them; and it is supported by {والله يُؤَيِّدُ بِنَصْرِهِ مَن يَشَآءُ}, for the showing here is in the position of reinforcement by angels in giving victory, by both. And the question returns then all the more: how did He multiply them to this extent given His saying in al-Anfāl: {وَيُقَلِّلُكُمْ في أَعْيُنِهِمْ}? And the answer returns.

The fifth: that the address in «لكم» and «تَرَوْنهم» is to the Jews, and the accusative and genitive pronouns on this refer to the Muslims, in the sense: "you see them, if you were to see them, as twice themselves"; in this assumption there is affectation with no need. It is as if this proponent chose that the address in the preceding verse, namely His saying {قَدْ كَانَ لَكُمْ}, be to the Jews, so he made it in «تَرَوْنهم» to them also; but going out from addressing the Jews to addressing other people is preferable to this affected assumption, since the Jews were not present at the battle that they should be addressed with their seeing them so. On this view it is permissible that the accusative and genitive pronouns refer to the disbelievers, that is: He multiplied the disbelievers in their eyes until they became twice the number of the disbelievers, and nevertheless the believers overcame them and were victorious over them, which is greater in power. It is also permissible that the accusative refer to the Muslims and the genitive to the polytheists, that is: "You see, O Jews, the Muslims as twice the number of the polytheists", out of awe of them and exaggeration of the matter of the believers, as was the case regarding the polytheists in the views that preceded. And it is permissible that the accusative refer to the polytheists and the genitive to the Muslims, the meaning being: "You see, O Jews, if you were to see the polytheists as twice the number of the Muslims", in that they were made few in their eyes so that dread and grief would come to them, because the fewness of the disbelievers grieved them and the multitude of the disbelievers and their victory over the Muslims pleased them, out of envy and transgression. These are three views arranged under the fifth view, so there are eight views in the reading of Nāfiʿ.

As for the reading of the rest, it has several views. The first: that it is like the reading in the second person; so everything said about what is meant by the address there is said here, but it came in the manner of iltifāt, that is, a shift from the second person to the third. The second: that the address in «لكم» is to the believers, and the nominative pronoun in «يَرَوْنَهم» is for the disbelievers, and the accusative and genitive for the Muslims, and the meaning is: "The polytheists see the believers as twice the number of the believers, six hundred and some twenty; Allah showed them, despite their fewness, to them as double, so that they would fear them and be cowardly toward them." The third: that the address in «لكم» is to the believers also, and the nominative in «يَرَوْنَهم» is for the disbelievers, the accusative for the Muslims and the genitive for the polytheists, that is: "The polytheists see the believers as twice the number of the polytheists; Allah showed them the believers as multiples of them", for what preceded in the previous view.

The fourth: that the nominative pronoun in «يَرَونهم» refer to the disbelieving group, because it is a plural in meaning, and the accusative and genitive pronouns as preceded of the possibility of their referring to the disbelievers, or the Muslims, or one of them to one and the other to the other.

What is strongest in this verse, of all that I presented, from the side of meaning, is that the axis of the verse be the reduction of the Muslims and the multiplication of the disbelievers, because the aim of the verse and its course is to point to the dazzling power of Allah and His support with victory for His believing servants despite the fewness of their number, and the abandonment of the disbelievers despite the multitude of their number and their banding together, so that it be known that victory is entirely from Allah, and its cause is not your multitude and the fewness of your enemy, but what He, blessed and exalted, did of casting terror into the hearts of your enemies; and it is supported by His saying after that: {والله يُؤَيِّدُ بِنَصْرِهِ مَن يَشَآءُ}, and He said in another place: {وَيَوْمَ حُنَيْنٍ إِذْ أَعْجَبَتْكُمْ كَثْرَتُكُمْ فَلَمْ تُغْنِ عَنكُمْ شَيْئاً} [al-Tawba: 25]. Shaykh Abū Shāma said, after mentioning this meaning and considering it strong: "The hāʾ in «تَرَوْنَهم» is for the disbelievers, whether read in the third person or the second, and the hāʾ in «مثليهم» is for the Muslims. If you ask: if this is what is meant, why was it not said: 'they see them as three times themselves'? That would have been more eloquent in the verse, which is the victory of the few over this many, and the number was so, or more. I say: He reported what happened, and it was another sign joined to the sign of sight, which is the reduction of the disbelievers in the eyes of the Muslims, and they were reduced to a limit at which the Muslims were promised victory over them, which is that one of the Muslims overcomes two; so there was no need for reduction beyond this, and in it is a benefit: the occurrence of what was guaranteed to them of victory in it." End of quotation. I say: al-Farrāʾ went to this meaning, I mean that they see them as three times themselves, for he said: "«مِثْليهم» is three times themselves, as the speaker says: 'I have a thousand and I need twice of it'." Abū Isḥāq (al-Zajjāj) held him mistaken in this, and said: "The mithl of a thing is what equals it, and its mithlān is what equals it twice." Ibn Kaysān said: "What led al-Farrāʾ to that is that the disbelievers on the day of Badr were three times their number, so he imagined that it is not permissible that they see them except at their number, and the meaning is not so; Allah showed them at other than their number for two reasons: one, that He saw the benefit in that, because the believers' hearts are strengthened by it; and the other, that it is a sign for the Prophet ﷺ."

On Nāfiʿ's reading the clause may be resumptive with no grammatical position, and it may have a position, and then there are two views: the first, accusative as a ḥāl from the «كم» in «لكم», that is: "there was for you, while you were seeing them"; the second, genitive as a naʿt of «فئتين», because it contains a pronoun referring to them; Abū l-Baqāʾ said this.

As for the reading in the third person, it may be resumptive, it may be nominative as an adjective of one of the two groups, and it may be genitive as an adjective of «فئتين» also, on the basis that the wāw in «يَرَوْنَهم» refers to the Jews, because the clause contains a pronoun referring to the two groups.

Ibn ʿAbbās and Ṭalḥa read «تُرَوْنَهم» as passive in the second person. Al-Sulamī read likewise, except in the third person. Both are clear from what has preceded, and the omitted agent is Allah the Exalted.

People have two opinions on the seeing here. The first: that it is seeing with the eye (baṣariyya), and this is supported by its being emphasized with the maṣdar, which is explicit in that; so it is an emphatic maṣdar. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "An open, unconcealed seeing in which there is no confusion." On this it takes one object, and «مثليهم» is accusative as a ḥāl. The second: that it is seeing of the heart (qalbiyya), so on this «مثليهم» is a second object.

Abū l-Baqāʾ rejected this, saying: "It is not permissible that the seeing be seeing of the heart on any of the views, for two reasons: one, His saying «رَأْيَ العين»; the other, that seeing of the heart is knowledge, and it is impossible for a thing to be known as two things."

The first reason has been answered by saying that its accusative is the accusative of a comparative maṣdar, that is: "a seeing like the seeing of the eye", that is, resembling the seeing of the eye, so it is not that in reality. The second reason has been answered by saying that "seeing" here means belief, so the mentioned impossibility does not follow. He said: "If they have applied 'knowledge' in the language to belief without certainty, then applying 'opinion' (raʾy) to it is more fitting."

Among the application of "knowledge" to belief is His saying, Exalted is He: {فَإِنْ عَلِمْتُمُوهُنَّ مُؤْمِنَاتٍ} [al-Mumtaḥana: 10]; for there is no way to certain knowledge in that, since none knows it so except Allah the Exalted, so the meaning is: "if you believe them to be". Belief may be sound and may be false. This interpretation is indicated by the reading of one who read «تُرَوْنَهم» or «يُرَوْنَهم» with tāʾ or yāʾ as passive; for their saying «أُرِيَ كذا» with ḍamma on the hamza is used where the speaker has doubt and conjecture, not certainty and knowledge; and since the belief in the doubling in the group of the disbelievers or in the group of the believers was conjecture and supposition, not certainty, a kind of doubt entered the speech. Also, just as it is impossible to take the seeing here as knowledge, it is likewise impossible to take it as seeing with the eye, by the very impossibility you mentioned; for just as knowledge cannot occur not matching the thing known, so visual sight cannot occur not matching the thing seen and looked at; so what is meant is conjecture and supposition, not certainty and knowledge. So it was said; but there is room for consideration in this, because we do not concede that sight never differs from the thing seen, since a defect may occur in it and a fault in the looking, so the viewer imagines one thing as two or more, and the reverse.

In the accusative of «رأيَ العين» there are three views, two of which have preceded: accusative as an emphatic maṣdar, or accusative as a comparative maṣdar, as you know with its verification. The third: that it is accusative as an adverb of place. Al-Wāḥidī said: "As you say: 'you see them in front of you'; and like it 'he is from me at the range of a dog's rebuke and the hanging-place of al-ʿAyyūq'." This is taking the word out of its setting with no support in meaning or technique.

"Raʾā" is a shared verb: "raʾā" in the sense of "he saw with the eye", whose maṣdar is raʾy and ruʾya; in the sense of "he believed", which has raʾy; and in the sense of "dream", which has ruʾyā, like dunyā. So the difference occurs in the maṣdar: ruʾya is for sight specifically, ruʾyā is for dreaming only, and raʾy is shared between the visual and the belief-related. One says: "this is the raʾy of so-and-so", that is, his belief. He said:

1193 - رَأَى الناسَ إلا مَنْ رَأَى مثلَ رأيِهِ ... خوارجَ تَرَّاكِين قَصْدَ المَخَارِجِ
(He regarded people, except those who shared his opinion, as seceders, abandoning the right course of the ways out.)

I say: people have said much on this verse, so I have followed it closely and joined each thing with what suits it.

His saying: {مَن يَشَآءُ}: the object of «يشاء» is omitted, that is: "whom He wills to support"; and the bāʾ is causal, that is: "by means of His support", and it is a taf'īl form from al-ayd, which is strength.

Warsh read «يُوَيِّدُ», changing the hamza into a pure wāw, which is a regular easing (tashīl). Abū l-Baqāʾ and others said: "It cannot be made bayna bayna because of its nearness to the alif, and the alif can only be preceded by a fatḥa; and for that reason the hamza that is at the beginning is not made bayna bayna, because beginning with an alif is impossible." I say: the position of Sībawayh and others concerning a hamza with fatḥa after a kasra is to turn it into a pure yāʾ, and after a ḍamma into a pure wāw, for the reason mentioned, namely that the hamza that is bayna bayna is close to the alif, and the alif is neither preceded by a ḍamma nor a kasra.

And {لأُوْلِي الأبصار} is an adjective of «عبرةً», that is: "a lesson belonging to those of insight". The ʿibra is a fiʿla form from ʿubūr (crossing), like rikba and jilsa, and ʿubūr is passing over, and from it: ʿabartu al-nahr (I crossed the river), and the maʿbar is the ship, because by it one crosses to the other side; and the ʿabra of the eye is its tear, because it passes over it. He expressed by ʿibra taking heed and awakening, because the one who takes heed crosses from ignorance to knowledge and from destruction to deliverance. Iʿtibār is the ifti'āl form from it, and ʿibāra is the speech that conveys to the aim because it contains a passing over; and ʿabartu al-ruʾyā and ʿabbartuhā, lightened and doubled, because you carry what you have of its interpretation across to its seer.

semin-durr:119-119.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {هَآأَنْتُمْ أولاء تُحِبُّونَهُمْ}: a parallel and its verification have already been given twice; we add here that «أولاء» may be in the position of accusative by an omitted verb, so that the matter is one of ishtighāl (pre-occupation), like «أنا زيداً ضربته». His saying {وَلاَ يُحِبُّونَكُمْ} may be a resumptive report, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause. As for «الكتاب», the alif-lām may be generic, the meaning being all the books, the singular sufficing; or it may be for a known referent, what is meant being a particular book.

His saying «عليكم» is attached to «عَضُّوا», and likewise «من الغيظِ»; «مِنْ» there is for the beginning of the extent, or it may mean the lām and so give the cause, i.e. "because of rage". Abū l-Baqāʾ allowed «عليكم» and «من الغيظ» both to be ḥāls, saying: "It may be a ḥāl, i.e. 'enraged against you'; «من الغيظِ» is also attached to «عَضُّوا», and «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the extent, i.e. 'because of rage'; and it may be a ḥāl, i.e. 'being furious'." End. His saying "«مِنْ» is for the beginning of the extent, i.e. because of rage" is discordant speech, because the «مِنْ» of beginning is not explained by the meaning of "because of", which is the meaning of cause, and cause and beginning are different; and in sum the ḥāl reading has no clear meaning, and his implying a ḥāl is not an technical (ṣināʿī) implication, since the technical implication is only with the absolute "beings" (akwān muṭlaqa).

al-ʿAḍḍ is clamping with the teeth, which is the pressing of the teeth on one another. One says ʿaḍiḍtu with kasra in the past, aʿaḍḍu with fatḥa, ʿaḍḍan and ʿaḍīḍan. Imruʾ al-Qays said:
1406 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... كفَحْلِ الهجانِ يَنْتَحي للعضيضِ
(… like a noble stud camel who turns to bite.) [Translator's note: the first half is elided in the source.]
It is used to express excessive regret, and from it {وَيَوْمَ يَعَضُّ الظالم على يَدَيْهِ} [al-Furqān: 27], even if there is no actual biting. Abū Ṭālib said:
1407 - وقد صالَحُوا قوماً علينا أَشِحَّةً ... يَعَضُّون غيظاً خَلْفَنا بالأنامِلِ
(They have made peace with a grudging people against us, who bite their fingertips in rage behind us.)
He made the bāʾ redundant in the object, as the original is «يَعَضُّون خلفَنا الأنامل», and there are parallels to this that preceded. Another said:
1408 - قدَ افنى أنامِلَه أزْمُهُ ... فَأَمْسَى يَعَضُّ عليَّ الوَظِيفا
(His clamping had worn away his fingertips, so he came to bite upon me the shank.) [Translator's note: gloss tentative.]
and al-Ḥārith ibn Ẓālim al-Murrī said:
1409 - وأقتلُ أقواماً لِئاماً أذِلَّةً ... يَعَضَّون مِنْ غيظٍ رؤوسَ الأباهِمِ
(I kill base, abased peoples who bite in rage the tips of their thumbs.)
and another:
1410 - إذا رَأَوْني أطالَ اللهُ غيظَهُمُ ... عَضُّوا من الغيظِ أَطْرَافَ الأباهيم
(When they see me — may Allah prolong their rage — they bite the tips of their thumbs in rage.)
al-ʿAḍḍ is all with ḍād, except in their saying «عَظَّ الزمانُ», meaning time became severe, and ʿaẓẓat al-ḥarb, for these are with ẓāʾ, the sister of ṭāʾ, and he recited:
1411 - وعَظَّ زمانٍ يا بنَ مروانَ لم يَدَعْ ... من المالِ إلاَّ مُسْحتاً أو مُجَلَّفُ
(And the severity of the time, O son of Marwān, left of wealth only what is destroyed or ruined.)
I have seen it in the handwriting of a group of the learned as «وعَضُّ زمان» with ḍād.
al-ʿAḍḍ, with ḍamma on the first letter [Translator's note: the source says "ḍamma on the fāʾ"], is fodder of crushed date-stones and the like, and from it: a camel ʿuḍāḍī, i.e. fat, as if related to it; and aʿaḍḍa l-qawm means their camels ate that. al-ʿIḍḍ with kasra is the formidable among men, as if they pictured his biting and severity. A zamanun ʿaḍūḍ is a barren time. al-Taʿḍūḍ is a kind of date, so called for the hardness and difficulty of chewing it.
al-Anāmil is the plural of anmula, which is the fingertips. al-Rummānī said: "Its derivation is from al-naml, this well-known animal [the ant]; it was likened to it for its fineness and the speed of its movement and motion; from it they called the slanderer namil and munmil." Hence he said:
1412 - ولستُ بذي نَيْرَبٍ فيهمُ ... ولا مُنْمِشٍ منهمُ مُنْمِلُ
(I am not one among them given to mischief, nor an agitator or slanderer among them.)
In its mīm both ḍamma and fatḥa occur.
al-Ghayẓ is the maṣdar of ghāẓahu yaghīẓuhu, i.e. he angered him. al-Rāghib explained it as the most intense anger, saying: "It is the heat a person feels from the surging of his heart's blood." He said: when Allah the Exalted is described by it, vengeance is meant. al-Taghayyuẓ is showing rage, and sometimes there is a sound with that. The Exalted said: {سَمِعُواْ لَهَا تَغَيُّظاً وَزَفِيراً} [al-Furqān: 12].
The sentence in His saying «وتؤمنون» is conjoined to «تُحِبُّونهم», so it has the well-known aspects. / al-Zamakhsharī said: "The wāw in «وتؤمنون» is of ḥāl, and its accusative position is from «لا يُحِبُّونكم», i.e. they do not love you while you believe in all your Book, and they, despite that, hate you; so what is the matter with you that you love them when they do not believe in any of your Book?" The Shaykh said: "It is good, except that there is in it, grammatically, something that mars it, namely that he made the wāw in «وتؤمنون» a wāw of ḥāl and its accusative position from «لا يحبونكم», whereas an affirmative imperfect that stands as a ḥāl does not take the wāw of ḥāl. You say «جاء زيدٌ يضحك» and it is not permitted «ويضحك». As for their saying «قمتُ وأَصُكُّ عينَه», it is extremely irregular, and has been interpreted as the implication of a mubtadaʾ, i.e. «وأنا أصُكُّ عينه», so the sentence becomes nominal; and this interpretation is possible here, i.e. «ولا يحبونكم وأنتم تؤمنون بالكتابِ كله», but the better is what we mentioned, that it is a conjunction." He means that it does not require an omission, unlike implying a mubtadaʾ, which is contrary to the basic rule. And there is an omitted sentence indicated by the context, the implied form being: "and you believe in the whole Book, and they do not believe in all of it, but say: we believe in some and disbelieve in some."

His saying: {بِغَيْظِكُمْ}: the bāʾ may be of ḥāl, i.e. "die accompanied by your rage, which does not leave you", and it is a metonymy for the abundance of Islam and its spread, because the more faith increases the more their rage increases. It may also be of causation, i.e. "because of your rage".
His saying {مُوتُواْ}: its form is an imperative and its meaning is a supplication. It is also said that its meaning is a report, i.e. that the matter is so. Some said: "It cannot be in the sense of supplication, because had he been commanded to call upon them with it, they would all have died in that state, for his supplication is not rejected, yet many of them believed after this verse; and it cannot be a report, because had it been a report it would have occurred as reported and none would have believed afterwards. When these two meanings are negated, nothing remains but that its meaning is rebuke and threat, like {اعملوا مَا شِئْتُمْ} [Fuṣṣilat: 40] and «إذا لم تَسْتَح فاصنع ما شئت» ('If you have no shame, do as you wish')." What he said is nothing, because whoever of them believed does not fall under the supplication, if supplication is intended, nor under the report, if reporting is intended.

semin-durr:120-120.t:
The majority read {إِن تَمْسَسْكُمْ} with the feminine form, observing the wording of «حسنة». Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān read it with yāʾ, because its femininity is figurative; its analogy is that «وإنْ يصبكم سيئة» also be read in the masculine, but I do not remember anything from him on it.

His saying: {إِنَّ الله عَلِيمٌ بِذَاتِ الصدور}: this sentence may be resumptive, the Exalted reporting it because they used to conceal their rage as far as they could, so He mentioned this to them by way of threat. It may also be a sentence of what is said, i.e. "Say to them such and such", in which case it is in the position of accusative by "say". The meaning of His saying «بذات» is "the hidden things that are possessors of the breasts"; so «ذات» here is the feminine of «ذي» meaning "possessor", the qualified noun being omitted and its adjective standing in its place, i.e. "Knowing of the hidden things that are companions of the breasts"; they were made companions of the breasts because of their constant attachment to them and non-separation from them, like "companions of Paradise" and "companions of the Fire".

They disagreed about stopping on this word: is it stopped at with tāʾ or with hāʾ? al-Akhfash, al-Farrāʾ and Ibn Kaysān said: "Stopping is with tāʾ, following the Mushaf's script." al-Kisāʾī and al-Jarmī said: "It is stopped at with hāʾ, because it is the tāʾ of femininity, as in «صاحبه»." Agreement with the script is preferable, since stopping at the explicit feminine tāʾ with tāʾ is established for us, so if we stop here with tāʾ we agree with that dialect and with the script, unlike the reverse.

His saying: {لاَ يَضُرُّكُمْ}: Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read «يَضِرْكم» with kasra on the ḍād and jussive rāʾ, as the apodosis of the condition, from ḍārahu yaḍīruhu; one also says ḍārahu yaḍūruhu, so there are two dialectal forms in the middle letter. One says ḍārahu yaḍīruhu ḍayran, so he is ḍāʾir and he is maḍīr; and ḍārahu yaḍūruhu ḍawran, so he is ḍāʾir and he is maḍūr, like qultuhu aqūluhu, so I am qāʾil and he is maqūl.

The others read «يَضُرُّكم» with ḍamma on the ḍād and a doubled rāʾ with ḍamma. In this reading there are several aspects. One: that the verb is nominative and is not the apodosis of the condition, but only indicates the apodosis. That is because it is intended to be put first, the implied form being: "It will not harm you if you are patient and fear Allah; it will not harm you", and the «فلا يضركم», which is the apodosis, was omitted because what precedes indicates it, then what indicates the apodosis was put later. What I have mentioned is the explanation of Sībawayh and his followers. They had to commit this strain only because they saw the lack of jussive in an / imperfect verb where nothing prevents the jussive particle from acting on it. Like it is the saying of another:
1413 - يا أقرعُ بنَ حابسٍ يا أقرعُ ... إنَّك إنْ يَصْرَعْ أخوكَ تُصْرعُ
(O Aqraʿ ibn Ḥābis, O Aqraʿ, if your brother is thrown, you will be thrown.)
with the last «تُصْرع» in the nominative, and likewise his saying:
1414 - وإنْ أتاهُ خليلٌ يومَ مسألةٍ ... يقولُ لا غائبٌ مالي ولا حَرِمُ
(If a friend comes to him on a day of asking, he says: "My wealth is neither absent nor forbidden.")
with «يقول» in the nominative. However this type is regular, unlike the former, I mean the condition and the response both being imperfect; for what is reported from Sībawayh and his followers is that the jussive is obligatory except in necessity, like «إنْ يُصْرعَ أخوك تُصْرعُ». His explanation of this verse as I have related from him shows that this is not restricted to necessity; so know that.

The second aspect: that the verb is nominative because it occurs after an implied fāʾ, and that and what follows it is in truth the apodosis; whenever a verb occurs after the fāʾ it is nominative, nothing else, as in His saying, the Exalted: {وَمَنْ عَادَ فَيَنْتَقِمُ الله مِنْهُ} [al-Māʾida: 95], the implied form being «فلا يَضُرُّكم». The fāʾ is omitted in a place other than the disputed one, as in the saying:
1415 - مَنْ يَفعلِ الحسناتِ اللهُ يشكُرها ... والشرُّ بالشر عند الله سِيَّانِ
(Whoever does good deeds, Allah thanks them; and evil by evil is the same with Allah.)
that is «فالله يشكرها». I have seen some report this aspect from al-Mubarrad, and there is room for objection in it, since when they recited the verse mentioned they reported from al-Mubarrad that he does not permit the omission of this fāʾ at all, neither in necessity nor otherwise, and they report that he used to say: "The transmission in this verse is rather:
مَنْ يفعلِ الخيرَ فالرحمنُ يَشْكُرُه ...
(Whoever does good, the Merciful thanks him …)"
and they replied to him that when a transmission is sound, another does not impugn it. I have seen some report it from al-Farrāʾ and al-Kisāʾī, and this is nearer.

The third aspect: that the vowel is a vowel of assimilation (ḥarakat ittibāʿ). The original is «لا يَضْرِرْكم» with unmerging, because of the sukūn of the second letter by jussive; and it will be mentioned that when two identical letters meet at the end of a verb with the second made sākin by jussive or by pause, the Arabs have two ways: merging (idghām), which is the dialect of Tamīm, and unmerging (fakk), which is the dialect of the Hijaz. But there is no way to merge except with a vowelled letter, so we were forced to vowel the second identical letter, and we vowelled it with the vowel nearest to it, namely the ḍamma on the letter before it, and merged what precedes into it; so it is jussive in implied form, and this vowel is in truth a vowel of assimilation and not a vowel of i'rab, unlike the two earlier aspects, in which it is a vowel of i'rab.

Know that whenever this type is merged, its first letter is either ḍamma-vowelled, fatḥa-vowelled or kasra-vowelled. If ḍamma-vowelled, like the noble verse and their saying «مُدَّ», there are three aspects in the state of merging: ḍamma for assimilation, fatḥa for lightness, and kasra on the basis of the meeting of two sākin letters; so you say muddu, muddа and muddi, ruddu, rudda and ruddi. They recite for this Jarīr's saying:
1416 - فَغُضِّ الطرفَ إنَّك من نُمَيْرٍ ... فلا كعباً بَلَغْتَ ولا كِلابا
(Lower your gaze, for you are of Numayr; you have reached neither Kaʿb nor Kilāb.)
with ḍamma, fatḥa and kasra on the ḍād as I have told you; and it will be mentioned that the verse was recited with the three aspects. If fatḥa-vowelled like ʿaḍḍa, or kasra-vowelled like firra, the final letter has two aspects: fatḥa and kasra, since there is no way for ḍamma; but with something like «فِرَّ» you may say kasra for two reasons, either assimilation or the meeting of two sākin letters, and likewise with fatḥa like «عَضَّ» you have two reasons also, either assimilation or lightness. All this holds when no third-person pronoun is attached to the verb; when a third-person pronoun is attached, like «رُدَّه», there are details and dialectal forms that are long to discuss and it is not fitting to go into them in this kind of work.

ʿĀṣim, in what al-Mufaḍḍal related from him, read with ḍamma on the ḍād and a doubled rāʾ with fatḥa, on the lightness I mentioned to you, / and it is, in their view, a better aspect than ḍamma on the rāʾ.
al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Muzāḥim read «لا يَضُرِّكم» with ḍamma on the ḍād and a doubled rāʾ with kasra, on the meeting of two sākin letters I mentioned to you. It seems that Ibn ʿAṭiyya did not know it as a reading, for he said: "As for the kasra, I do not know it as a reading." al-Zajjāj's expression on that is loose, since it appears from the flow of his speech that it is a reading. I say: I have shown that it is a reading as al-Zajjāj said, and praise be to Allah.

al-Kayd is scheming and guile. al-Rāghib said: "It is a kind of guile, and may be praised or blamed, though it is used more in the blameworthy." Ibn Qutayba said: "Its origin is from hardship, from their saying «فلان يكيدُ بنفسِه», meaning he passes through the pangs of death, and its derivatives." One says kidtu fulānan akīduhu like bʿtuhu abīʿuhu. He said:
1417 - مَنْ يَكِدْني بسيِّءٍ كنتُ منه ... كالشَّجا بين حَلْقِه والوَرِيد
(Whoever schemes against me with evil, I shall be to him like a bone stuck between his throat and his jugular vein.)
Ubayy read «لا يَضْرِرْكم» with unmerging, which is the Hijazi dialect, and on it is His saying, the Exalted: {إِن تَمْسَسْكُمْ حَسَنَةٌ}.
His saying «شيئاً» is accusative like the maṣdars, i.e. "any harm"; a parallel has been given. The majority read «بما يعملون محيطٌ» in the third person, which is clear. al-Ḥasan read it in the second person, either on iltifāt, or on the implication «قل لهم يا محمد» ("Say to them, O Muḥammad").

semin-durr:146-146.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَكَأَيِّن مِّن نَّبِيٍّ}: It is said that this word is a compound of the kāf of comparison and «أيٍّ», and after the compounding there arose in it the meaning of multiplicity understood from the khabar-type «كم». Similar to it in compounding and conveying multiplicity is «كذا» in their saying «له عندي كذا كذا درهماً» ("he has with me so and so many dirhams"); the origin is the kāf of comparison and «ذا», which is a demonstrative; when the two were compounded, the meaning of multiplicity arose in them. The khabar-type «كم», «كأيِّن» and «كذا» are all of one meaning, and we have known compounding to produce another meaning; do you not see that «لولا» acquired a new meaning? «كأيِّن» by right, on this account, should be paused upon without nūn, because tanwīn is dropped in pause; but the Companions wrote it «كأيِّن» with the nūn retained, and so the majority of the readers paused upon it with the nūn, following the codex orthography. Abū ʿAmr, and Sawra ibn Mubārak from al-Kisāʾī, paused upon it as «كأي» without nūn, by analogy. Al-Fārisī gave reasons for pausing with the nūn, which he elaborated at length, among them that when the word was compounded it departed from its like, so the tanwīn was made as if it were an original letter of the structure of the word. It has five dialectal forms. The first: «كَأَيِّنْ», which is the origin, and by it the group read, except Ibn Kathīr. The poet said:

1456 - كَأَيِّنْ في المعاشِر من أُناسٍ ... أخوهُمْ فوقَهم وهمُ كِرامُ
(How many among the tribes are people whose brother is above them while they are noble.)

The second: «كائِنْ» on the pattern of «كاعِنْ», by which Ibn Kathīr and a group read; it is more used than «كَأَيِّن» even though that is the origin. The poet said:

1457 - وكائن بالأباطحِ مِنْ صديقٍ ... يَراني لو أُصِبْتُ هو المُصَابا
(How many a friend in the valley-beds who, were I afflicted, would see himself the afflicted.)

And he said:

1458 - وكائِنْ رَدَدْنا عنكُمُ مِنْ مُدَجَّجٍ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(How many an armoured warrior have we turned back from you ...)

They differed in the justification of this reading. It is transmitted from al-Mubarrad that it is an active participle from kāna yakūnu, so it is kāʾin; Makkī considered this remote, saying: "because «مِنْ» comes after it and because it is built on sukūn." Likewise Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is far from sound, because if it were so it would be declinable (muʿrab) and would not have the meaning of multiplicity." It cannot be said that this is to be charged against al-Mubarrad alone, for this also applies to them (the others), since indeclinability and the meaning of multiplicity are incidental as well, because compounding has been known to produce the like of that, as already said of «كذا» and «لولا» and the like; but a single word being transferred to a meaning and made indeclinable without a cause has no parallel. It is said: the origin of this reading is «كأيِّنْ», like the reading of the group, except that transposition (qalb) entered the word and it became «كائِن» like «جاعِن».

They differed on how it became so by transposition, on four views. The first: the doubled yāʾ was put before the hamza, so its pattern became kaʿlaf, because you put forward the ʿayn and lām, which are the doubled yāʾ; then the second yāʾ was dropped because of its heaviness with the vowel and the doubling, as they said of «أيُّهما»: «أيْهُما»; then the quiescent yāʾ was turned into alif, as they turned it in the like of «آية», the origin being ayya, and as they said ṭāʾī, the origin being ṭayʾī; so the word became kāʾin like jāʿin, as you see, and its pattern is «كَعْفٍ», because the fāʾ was moved back to the place of the lām and the lām was dropped.

The second view: the quiescent yāʾ which is the ʿayn was dropped and the vowelled one which is the lām was put forward, so the hamza, which is the fāʾ, was put back, and the yāʾ was turned into alif because it has a vowel and what precedes it has fatḥa, so it became «كائِن», and its pattern is «كَلْفٍ».

The third view, attributed to al-Khalīl: one of the two yāʾs was put in the position of the hamza and given the vowel of the hamza, namely fatḥa, and the hamza became quiescent in the position of the yāʾ; the yāʾ took a vowel with fatḥa before it, so it was turned into alif, and two quiescents met, the alif turned from yāʾ and the quiescent hamza after it, so the hamza was given kasra on the basis of the meeting of two quiescents; and one of the two yāʾs remained final, and the tanwīn removed it after its vowel was stripped, like the yāʾ of qāḍin and ghāzin.

The fourth view: the vowelled yāʾ was put forward and turned into alif, and the other remained quiescent and the tanwīn dropped it, like qāḍin; its pattern on these two views is also «كَلْفٍ», because of the dropping of the ʿayn and the postponement of the fāʾ, the operations differing only.

The third dialect: «كَأْيِن» with a light yāʾ after the hamza, on the pattern kaʿyin, by which Ibn Muḥayṣin and al-Ashhab al-ʿUqaylī read. Its aspect is that the origin is «كَأَيِّن» like the reading of the group; the second yāʾ was dropped for heaviness, so two quiescents met, the yāʾ and the tanwīn, so the yāʾ was given kasra for the meeting of two quiescents; then the hamza was made quiescent for lightness because of the heaviness of the word by compounding, so it became like a single word, as they made «فهو» and «فهي» quiescent.

The fourth dialect: «كَيْئِن», with a quiescent yāʾ followed by a hamza with kasra; this is the transposition of the reading before it, and some read by it.

The fifth dialect: «كَئِنْ» on the pattern kaʿ in, which al-Dānī reported as a reading from Ibn Muḥayṣin also. The poet said:

1459 - كَئِنْ مِنْ صديقٍ خِلْتُه صادقَ الإِخا ... أبانَ اختباري أنَّه لي مُداهِنُ
(How many a friend I thought truthful in brotherhood; my testing made clear that he was flattering me.)

There are two views on it. One: that he dropped the two yāʾs at once because of the blending of the two words through compounding; the second: that he dropped one of the two yāʾs as explained above, then dropped the other because it met the tanwīn while quiescent; and its pattern on this is «كَفٍ», with the ʿayn and lām dropped from it.

They differed about «أيٍّ»: is it originally a maṣdar or not? A group held that it is not a maṣdar, and this is the apparent meaning of Abū al-Baqāʾ's statement, for he said: "The origin of «كأيِّن» is «أي», which is part of a whole, to which the kāf of comparison was added." In his describing «أي» as being part of a whole there is something to consider, because it is not in the sense of part of a whole; yes, when it is annexed to a definite it takes the ruling of «بعض» (part) in agreement of the khabar and the return of the pronoun, as in «أيُّ الرجلين قام؟» and you do not say «قاما»; but it is not that of «بعض» at all.

Ibn Jinnī held that it is originally the maṣdar of awā yaʾwī, when something is gathered and joined, the origin being awy, like ṭawā yaṭwī ṭayyan, the origin being ṭawy: the yāʾ and wāw met, one of them preceded by sukūn, so the wāw was turned into yāʾ and assimilated into the yāʾ. It is as if Ibn Jinnī looked to the meaning of the root, the gathering, which «أيّ» indicates, for it is for generality, and generality entails gathering.

Is this kāf which enters upon «أي» attached to something, like other prepositions, or not? The sound view is that it is not attached to anything at all, because with «أي» the two became equivalent to a single word, «كم», so it is not attached to anything; for that reason its original meaning, comparison, was abandoned.

Al-Ḥawfī claimed that it is attached to a governor, and his text must be cited so that you may stand upon it, for it is strange speech. He said: "As for the governor in the kāf, if we take it according to the ruling of the origin it is carried on the meaning, the meaning being: 'there afflicted you something like the affliction of those prophets before and their companions'; and if we carry the ruling on the transfer to the meaning of «كم», the governor is by the estimate of inchoation and it is in the position of the nominative, «قُتِل» being the khabar, and «مِنْ» attached to the meaning of residing; and the first estimate is clearer, to carry the speech on the wording rather than the meaning, because of what is necessary of the genitive in «أي»; and if «أي» is in its normal way in treating the wording, «مِنْ» is attached to what the kāf is attached to of the meaning indicated." End.

The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) chose that «كأيِّنْ» is a simple word, not compounded, and that its final nūn is part of the word itself, not tanwīn, because these earlier claims have no evidence standing upon them. The Shaykh took the easier route in that, while the grammarians mentioned these things to preserve their principles, along with the benefits added to that and the sharpening and exercising of the mind. This is what concerns «كأيِّن» in terms of its singularity.

As for what concerns it in terms of syntax, its position is nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and there are four views on its khabar. The first: that it is «قُتِل», for in it is a nominative pronoun governed by it referring back to the mubtadaʾ, the estimate being: "many of the prophets were killed". Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The good form is that the pronoun refer to the wording of «كأيِّنْ», as you say «مئة نبي قُتِل» (a hundred prophets was killed), the pronoun being for the hundred, since it is the mubtadaʾ. If you say: were it so you would have made it feminine and said «قُتِلَتْ». It is said: this is carried on the meaning, because the estimate is: 'many of the men was killed'." End. As if he means by "not good" its referring back to the wording «نبي». On this, «معه ربِّيُّون» is a sentence in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun in «قُتِل» [and it is preferable because it is of the class of singulars, and the origin of the ḥāl, khabar and attribute is to be singular]. It is possible that «معه» alone is the ḥāl and «رِبِّيُّون» its fāʿil, and there is no need here of the wāw of ḥāl, because the pronoun is the link, I mean the pronoun in «معه»; and it may be a ḥāl from «نبي», although it is indefinite, because it is specified by the description then; Makkī mentioned it; and the adverbial phrase operates here because it relies on the owner of the ḥāl.

The Shaykh said: "It is a narration of a past state (ḥikāyat ḥāl māḍiya), and for that reason «ربِّيُّون» is nominative through the adverbial phrase even though the governor is past, because it narrates the past state, as in His saying, the Exalted, {وَكَلْبُهُمْ بَاسِطٌ ذِرَاعَيْهِ} [al-Kahf: 18]; and this is according to the Basrans, whereas al-Kisāʾī makes the active participle devoid of «ال» govern absolutely." There is something to consider in it, because we do not concede that the adverbial phrase is attached to an active participle so that what he said, of interpreting the active participle as a past state, would be necessitated; rather we claim that it is attached to a verb whose estimate is: "there rested with him Rabbis".

The second view: that «قُتِل» is a sentence in the position of the genitive as a naʿt of «نبي», and «معه ربيون» is the khabar, and you have the two earlier views in making it a ḥāl, I mean if you wish you may make «معه» a fronted khabar and «ربيون» a postponed mubtadaʾ, the sentence being the khabar of «كأين»; and if you wish you may make «معه» alone the khabar and «ربيون» its fāʿil, because the adverbial phrase relies on the possessor of a khabar.

The third view: that the khabar is omitted, its estimate being «في الدنيا» ("in the world") or «مضى» ("passed") or «صائر» ("become") and the like. On this his saying «قتل» is in the position of the genitive as an attribute of «نبي», and «معه ربيون» a ḥāl from the pronoun in «قتل» as the explanation preceded; it is also possible that «معه ربيون» is a second attribute of «نبي», it being described with two attributes: its being killed and its having Rabbis with it.

The fourth view: that «قُتِل» is empty of the pronoun, attributed to «ربيون»; in this sentence there are then two possibilities. One: that it is the khabar of «كائن»; the second: that it is in the position of the genitive as an attribute of «نبي», the khabar being omitted as has gone before; and the claim of omitting the khabar is weak because the speech is self-sufficient without it. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It may be that «قُتِل» is an attribute of «ربيين», so there is no pronoun in it on this, and the sentence is an attribute of «نبي»; and it may be a khabar, so there become four views on the khabar; and it may be an attribute of «نبي» with the khabar omitted as we mentioned." As for his saying "an attribute of «ربيين»", he means that being killed is among their attributes in meaning. And his saying "so there become four views", he means with the views he mentioned earlier. His saying "so there is no pronoun in it on this, and the sentence is an attribute of «نبي»" is an error, because it leaves the mubtadaʾ without a khabar. If you say: he claims this only because he estimates an omitted khabar; I say: he mentioned that as another view where he said: "It may be an attribute of «نبي» with the khabar omitted as we mentioned."

The attribution of «قُتِل» to the pronoun of the prophet is supported by the fact that the story is on account of the battle of Uḥud and the believers' dispute when it was said that Muḥammad had died, killed; this is supported by his saying {أَفإِنْ مَّاتَ أَوْ قُتِلَ} [Āl ʿImrān: 144]; to this went Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ṭabarī and a group; and from Ibn ʿAbbās on His saying {وَمَا كَانَ لِنَبِيٍّ أَنْ يَغُلَّ} [Āl ʿImrān: 161]: "The prophet is killed, so how would he not be betrayed?" Al-Ḥasan, Ibn Jubayr and a group held that the killing was of the Rabbis; they said: because no prophet has ever been killed in battle. Al-Zamakhsharī supported this with the reading «قُتِّل» with doubling, meaning that multiplicity does not arise with a single one, who is the prophet. What al-Zamakhsharī mentioned was preceded to it by Ibn Jinnī, and the interpretation of this will come.

Ibn Kathīr, Nāfiʿ and Abū ʿAmr read «قُتِل» as a passive; Qatāda likewise, except that he doubled the تاء; and the rest of the seven read «قاتَل». Each of these verbs can take as its subject the pronoun of «نبي» and can take «ربِّيِّين», as the detail has preceded. Ibn Jinnī said: "In the reading «قُتِّل» with doubling it is necessary that the verb be attributed to the overt noun, I mean «ربيين»." He said: "because there is no multiplicity in a single one." Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is not impossible that it contain the pronoun of the first, because it is in the sense of a group." End. He means that by «من نبي» the genus is meant, so the multiplicity is in relation to the multiplicity of persons, not in relation to each individual, since killing is not multiplied in each individual. This answer that Abū al-Baqāʾ gave was sensed by Abū al-Fatḥ, who answered it. He said: "If it is said: it is attributed to «نبي» in regard to the meaning of «كم», the answer: the wording has spread in the singular in His saying {مِّن نَّبِيٍّ}, and the singular pronoun in «معه» indicates that what is meant is the exemplification by one, so the speech has gone out of the meaning of «كم»." He said: "This reading strengthens the statement of those who said that «قُتِل» and «قاتَل» are attributed to the Rabbis."

The Shaykh said: "It is not apparent, because «كأين» is like «كم», and when you say «كم مِنْ عانٍ فككتُه» ('how many a captive have I freed'), [using the singular], you have regarded its wording, and its meaning is plural; and when you say «فَكَكْتُهم» you have regarded the meaning. So there is no difference between «قُتل معه ربيون» and «قُتِل معهم رِبِّيُّون». Regarding the wording at times and the meaning at others is permissible in «كم» and «كأين» only because their meaning is 'a group' (jamʿ), and for «جمع» that is permissible. The Exalted said: {أَمْ يَقُولُونَ نَحْنُ جَمِيعٌ مُّنتَصِرٌ سَيُهْزَمُ الجمع وَيُوَلُّونَ الدبر} [al-Qamar: 44-45], so He regarded the wording in His saying «منتصِرٌ» and the meaning in His saying «يُوَلُّون»."

Some preferred the reading «قاتل» because of His saying after that {فَمَا وَهَنُواْ}; he said: "If they were killed, how would they be described by this? Only the living are described by this." The answer: its meaning is "some of them were killed", as you say "the sons of so-and-so were killed in such-and-such a battle, then they were victorious". Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The reading of those who read «قاتل» is more general in praise, because it includes those who were killed and those who remained; and it seems good to me on this reading that the verb be attributed to the Rabbis, and on the reading «قُتِل» that it be attributed to «نبي»." The Shaykh said: "Rather «قُتِل» is more praising and more eloquent for the aim of the address, for «قُتِل» entails fighting, without the converse."

And His saying {مِّن نَّبِيٍّ} is a tamyīz for «كأيِّن», because it is like the khabar-type «كم». Some claimed that its genitive with «مِن» is obligatory, and for this nothing but that has come in the Revelation; and this is the most frequent and prevalent, as he said. Its tamyīz has come accusative, he said:

1460 - اطرُدِ اليأسَ بالرجاء فكائِنْ ... آلِماً حُمَّ يُسْرُهُ بعدَ عُسْرِ
(Drive despair away with hope, for how many a sufferer has had ease decreed for him after hardship.)

And another said:

1461 - وكائِنْ لنا فَضْلاً عليكم ورحمةً ... قديماً ولا تَدْرُون ما مَنُّ مُنْعِمِ
(How many a favour and mercy have we shown you of old, and you do not know what a benefactor's bestowal is.)

As for its being genitive by annexation, it is impossible because its end is tanwīn, which does not stay with annexation.

And al-rabbiyyūn is the plural of «رِبِّي», which is the scholar, ascribed to al-rabb (the Lord); its rāʾ was given kasra only as a change in the ascription (nisba), like «إمْسِيّ» with kasra, ascribed to «أَمْس». It is also said: it was given kasra by assimilation; and it is said: there is no change in it, and it is ascribed to al-ribba, which is the group. This reading with kasra on the rāʾ is the reading of the majority. ʿAlī, Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan read «رُبِّيُّون» with ḍamma on the rāʾ, which is from a change in the ascription if we say it is ascribed to al-rabb; it is also said: there is no change, and it is ascribed to al-rubba, which is the group, and it has two dialects: kasra and ḍamma. Ibn ʿAbbās, in the narration of Qatāda, read «رَبِّيُّون» with fatḥa on it, on the origin if we say it is ascribed to al-rabb, otherwise it is from a change in the ascription if we say it is ascribed to al-ribba. Ibn Jinnī said: "The fatḥa is the dialect of Tamīm." Al-Naqqāsh said: "They are those who increase knowledge, from their saying rabā yarbū, when it increases." This is an oversight on his part, because of the difference of the two roots, since that one is of rāʾ, bāʾ and wāw, and this of rāʾ and a doubled bāʾ. And «كثير» is an attribute of «ربّيّون» although it is in the singular wording, because its meaning is plural.

His saying: {فَمَا وَهَنُواْ}: the pronoun in «وَهَنوا» refers back to the Rabbis as a whole if «قُتِل» is attributed to the pronoun of the prophet; likewise in the reading «قاتل», whether attributed to the pronoun of the prophet or to the Rabbis; and if it is attributed to the Rabbis, the pronoun refers back to some of them, as has already gone before in the discussion of preferring the reading «قاتل».

The majority read «وَهَنوا» with fatḥa on the hāʾ, and al-Aʿmash and Abū al-Sammāl with kasra on it; they are two dialects: wahana yahinu like waʿada yaʿidu, and wahina yawhanu like wajila yawjalu. It is also related from Abū al-Sammāl and ʿIkrima: «وَهْنوا» with sukūn on the hāʾ, which is a lightening of faʿila because it is a guttural letter, like naʿm and shahd for naʿima and shahida.

And «لَمَّا» is attached to «وَهَنوا», and «وما» may be a relative noun, a maṣdar particle, or an indefinite noun with a description. The majority read «ضَعُفوا» with ḍamma on the ʿayn, and it was read «ضَعَفوا» with fatḥa on it, which al-Kisāʾī reported as a dialect.

And His saying {وَمَا استكانوا}: there are three statements on it. The first: that it is istafʿala from al-kawn, and al-kawn is humiliation, its origin being istakwana; the vowel of the wāw was transferred to the kāf, then the wāw was turned into alif. [Translator's note: the source gives no label for the second view; the statement of al-Azharī and Abū ʿAlī that follows appears to be the second.] Al-Azharī and Abū ʿAlī said: "It is from the saying of the Arabs «بات فلان بِكَيْنَةِ سوءٍ» on the pattern of «جفنة», i.e. in a bad state", so its alif on this is from a yāʾ, and the origin is istakyana, and what was done with the yāʾ is what was done with its sister.

The third: al-Farrāʾ said: "Its pattern is iftaʿala from al-sukūn, but the fatḥa was extended and an alif was generated from it, as in his saying:

1462 - أعوذُ باللهِ من العَقْرابِ ... الشَّائِلاتِ عُقَدَ الأَذْنَابِ
(I seek refuge in Allah from the scorpions, raising the knots of their tails.)

he means al-ʿaqrab al-shāʾila (the scorpion raising [its tail])." Al-Farrāʾ was refuted in that this alif is retained in all the inflections of the word, like istakāna yastakīnu, so he is mustakīn and mustakān ilayhi, istikāna; and in that extension (ishbāʿ) occurs only in necessity. Neither of the two is binding on him: as for the extension, it occurs in the seven readings, as will pass you; and as for the retention of the alif in the inflections of the word, it is also no proof, because an augment may be fixed; do you not see that the mīm in tamandala and tamadraʿa is augmented, and yet it is retained in all the inflections of the word? They said: tamandala yatamandalu tamandulan, so he is mutamandil and mutamandal bihi, and likewise tamadraʿa, both from al-nadl and al-dirʿ. Abū al-Baqāʾ's wording is better in the refutation, for he said: "because the word in all its inflections has retained its ʿayn, and extension is not on this pattern."

He did not mention what the abasement and weakness are attached to; He did not say "they did not weaken against such and such, nor abase themselves to such and such", either for the sake of working with it, or to limit to the two verbs, like {كُلُواْ واشربوا} [al-Baqara: 60], so that it should include whatever is suitable for them.

semin-durr:173-173.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {الذين قَالَ لَهُمُ الناس}: The aspects in it are those that preceded for the «الذين» before it, except its being nominative as a mubtadaʾ.
