I say: it seems he imagined that since the mention of the people preceded in His saying {ثُمَّ يَقُولَ لِلنَّاسِ}, the composition should have been «ولا يأمرهم» in keeping with what preceded; but it is not so; rather this is a beginning of address in which there is no iltifāt.
His saying: {بَعْدَ إِذْ أَنْتُمْ مُّسْلِمُونَ}: «بعد» is attached to يأمركم, and «بعد» is an adverbial of time annexed to an adverbial of past time, and it has preceded that only time is annexed to it, such as حينئذٍ and يومئذٍ; and {أَنْتُمْ مُّسْلِمُونَ} is in the position of genitive by annexation, because «إذ» is annexed to a clause absolutely, whether nominal or verbal.

semin-durr:153-153.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {إِذْ تُصْعِدُونَ}: As for the governor of «إذ», it is said to be implied, i.e. "remember". Al-Zamakhsharī said: «صَرَفَكم إذ ليبتلِيَكم». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It may be an adverb of «عَصَيْتُم» or «تنازَعْتم» or «فَشِلتم»." It is also said: it is an adverb of «عفَا عنكم». All these views are acceptable; its being an adverb of «صرفكم» is good from the aspect of meaning, and of «عفا» is good from the aspect of nearness. On some of the statements the issue belongs to the chapter of tanāzuʿ (competition of governors), and is on the basis of applying the last of them, because there is no pronoun in the first, and the competition is among more than two governors.

The majority read «تُصْعدون» with ḍamma on the تاء and kasra on the ʿayn, from aṣʿada fī al-arḍ, when he went off in it, the hamza in it being for entering, as in «أصْبح زيدٌ» (Zayd entered the morning); so the meaning is "when you were entering into ascent (ṣuʿūd)". This is made clear by the reading of Ubayy: «تُصْعِدون في الوادي» ("you were going up the valley"). Al-Ḥasan and al-Sulamī read «تَصْعَدون», from ṣaʿida fī al-jabal, i.e. he climbed. The combination of the two readings is that they first went up (aṣʿadū) in the valley, and then when the enemy pressed them, they climbed (ṣaʿidū) the mountain; and this is according to the view of whoever distinguishes between aṣʿada and ṣaʿida. Abū Ḥaywa read «تَصَعَّدُون» with doubling, the origin being tataṣaʿʿadūn, so one of the two tāʾs was dropped, either the tāʾ of the imperfect or the tāʾ of tafaʿʿala; and the combination of his reading and the reading of others is as above. The majority read «تُصْعِدون» with the tāʾ of second person; Ibn Muḥayṣin, and it is also related from Ibn Kathīr, with the yāʾ of third person, on iltifāt, and it is good; and it is possible that the pronoun refer back to the believers, i.e. "and Allah is possessed of bounty upon the believers when they were going up", so the governor in «إذ» is «فَضْل».

One says: aṣʿada, i.e. he went far in going; al-Qutabī said: "as if he went far like the distance of ascending." The poet said:

1466 - ألا أيُّهذا السائلي أينَ أَصْعَدَتْ ... فإنَّ لَها في أهل يَثْربَ مَوْعدا
(O you who ask me where she has gone off to: she has an appointment among the people of Yathrib.)

And another said:

1467 - قد كُنْتِ تبكين على الإِصعادِ ... فاليومَ سُرِّحْتِ وصاح الحادي
(You used to weep over the setting out; today you have been sent off, and the camel-driver cries out.)

Al-Farrāʾ and Abū Ḥātim said: "Al-iṣʿād is the beginning of the journey and the departure, while al-ṣuʿūd is the maṣdar of ṣaʿida [when] he climbed from low to high", so these distinguished between ṣaʿida and aṣʿada. Al-Mufaḍḍal said: "ṣaʿida, ṣaʿʿada and aṣʿada are of one meaning, and al-ṣaʿīd is the surface of the earth."

{وَلاَ تَلْوُونَ}: the majority read «تلْوون» with two wāws. It was also read with the first replaced by a hamza, in dislike of the meeting of two wāws, but this is not analogical because the ḍamma is incidental; and a wāw with ḍamma is replaced by a hamza under conditions mentioned before in al-Baqara: that the ḍamma not be incidental, as in this word; that it not be an augment, as in «تَرَهْوَك»; that it not be possible to lighten it, as in «سُوُر» and «نُوُر», plurals of siwār and nuwār, since it is possible to make it quiescent and say suwr and nuwr so that the wording is lightened; and that it not be assimilated into another, as in «تَعَوُّد», the maṣdar of taʿawwada. So the like of «فُوُوج» is regularly replaced, the conditions being complete.

The meaning of «لا تَلْوون» is: you do not turn back. One says «لَوَى به», i.e. he went off with it, and «لَوَى عليه»: he turned to it. He said:

1468 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... أخو الجَهْد لا يَلْوي على مَنْ تَعَذَّرا
(... the one in distress does not turn back for whoever falls behind.)

The origin of «تَلْوون» is talwiyūn, which underwent weakening by dropping the lām; this has already gone before in His saying {يَلْوُونَ أَلْسِنَتَهُمْ} [Āl ʿImrān: 78].

Al-Aʿmash read, and it is also related from ʿĀṣim, «تُلْوون» with ḍamma on the تاء, from alwā, which is a dialectal form of «لَوَى», so faʿala and afʿala are of one meaning. Al-Ḥasan read «تَلُون» with a single wāw, and they analysed it as: he replaced the wāw with a hamza, then transferred the vowel of the hamza to the lām, then dropped the hamza by the rule, so nothing remained of the word but the fāʾ, which is the lām. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "One of the two wāws was dropped because of the two quiescents," though he had earlier said that this reading is built on the dialect of those who put a hamza for the wāw and transfer the vowel; and this is strange: after making it of the chapter of transferring the vowel of the hamza, how does he go back and say that one of the two wāws was dropped? The reading of al-Ḥasan can be analysed in two other ways. One: it may be said that the ḍamma was found heavy on the wāw because it is its sister, as if three wāws had met, so the ḍamma was transferred to the lām and two quiescents met, the wāw which is the ʿayn of the word and the wāw which is the pronoun, so the first was dropped for the meeting of two quiescents; had Ibn ʿAṭiyya said it thus it would have been better. The second: that «تَلُون» is the imperfect of «ولِيَ كذا» from wilāya (authority), and it is made transitive with «على» only because it is made to include the meaning of turning to.

Ḥumayd ibn Qays read «على أُحُد» with two ḍammas, meaning the mountain, the meaning being "upon the one on Mount Uḥud", namely the Prophet ﷺ. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The well-known reading is stronger, because he was not on the mountain until after the people had fled from him, while their going up occurred while he was calling them."

His saying: {والرسول يَدْعُوكُمْ}: a mubtadaʾ and khabar in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, the governor in it being «تَلْوُون».

His saying: {فَأَثَابَكُمْ}: two views. One: that it is conjoined to «تُصْعِدون» and «تَلْوون»; it does no harm that these are imperfect, because they are past in meaning, since «إذ» annexed to them made them past, so it is as if the meaning were "when you went up and turned". The second: that it is conjoined to «صَرَفكم». Al-Zamakhsharī said: «فأثابكم» is conjoined to «صَرَفَكم». There is remoteness in it, because of the length of separation. On its fāʿil there are two statements: one, that it is the Creator the Exalted; the second, that it is the Prophet ﷺ. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The pronoun in «فأثابكم» may refer to the Messenger, i.e. he shared with you in the distress, and as what befell him of the breaking of his incisor distressed you, what befell you of the loss of the spoils distressed him."

And «غَمَّاً» is a second object, and as for «بغمٍّ» several views are possible for the bāʾ. One: that it is causal, in the sense that what the first distress relates to is the Companions, and what the second distress relates to is the killing of the polytheists on the day of Badr, the meaning being: "so He repaid you with distress for the distress which He brought about through your hands upon the disbelievers on the day of Badr."

It is also said: "What the distress relates to is the Messenger, and the meaning: Allah made you taste distress because of the distress you caused the Messenger and the believers by your faltering"; or "the Messenger repaid you", i.e. he shared with you distress because of a distress you felt on his account. The second: that the bāʾ is of accompaniment, i.e. distress accompanied by distress, and the two distresses are for the Companions: the first distress being the defeat and killing; the second, Khālid's coming upon them with the cavalry of the disbelievers, or the rumour of the killing of the Messenger, peace be upon him. On the first, the bāʾ is attached to «أَثَابكم»; Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is said: the meaning is 'because of a distress', so it is a mafʿūl bihi." On the second it is attached to an omitted element, because it is an attribute of «غَمّ», i.e. distress accompanied by distress, or mixed with distress. Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed that the bāʾ be in the sense of «بعد» (after) or in the sense of «بَدَل» (instead), and made it in these two views an attribute of «غَمَّا»; but its being in the sense of «بعد» or «بدل» is remote, and he seems to intend an explanation of the meaning; likewise al-Zamakhsharī said: "distress after distress."

And His saying {فَأَثَابَكُمْ}: is it literal or figurative? It is said to be figurative, as if He made distress stand in the place of the reward that would have come about had it not been for the flight; so it is like his saying:

1469 - أخافُ زياداً أَنْ يكونَ عَطاؤُه ... أداهِمَ سُوداً أو مُحَدْرَجَةً سُمْرا
(I fear that Ziyād's gift will be black fetters or tightly-twisted brown whips.)

and his saying:

1470 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... تحيةُ بيْنِهم ضَرْبٌ وَجِيعُ
(... their greeting among themselves is a painful beating.)

He made fetters and whips stand in the position of a gift, and beating in the position of a greeting. Al-Farrāʾ said: "Al-ithāba here is in the sense of punishment (muʿāqaba)," and that returns to the figurative.

His saying: {لِّكَيْلاَ}: this is the lām of «كي», and it is a lām of genitive, while the accusative here is by «كي», so that a preposition does not have to enter upon its like. There are two statements on what this lām is attached to. One: that it is «فأثابكم»; on this there are two views on «لا». One: that it is redundant, because grief's non-occurrence does not follow from distress, and the meaning is: He distressed them in order to grieve them as a punishment for them for leaving their positions; Abū al-Baqāʾ said it. The second view: that it is not redundant; al-Zamakhsharī said: "Its meaning is: so that you may not grieve, that you might be trained in swallowing distresses and become accustomed to bearing hardships, so that you do not grieve afterwards over a benefit missed nor over a harm that befalls." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The meaning: what befell you was by your own offence, so you yourselves entangled yourselves, and it is the habit of mankind to be patient with punishment when they have offended; its anxiety increases only when one thinks oneself innocent."

The second: that the lām is attached to «عَفا», because His pardon removed all grief. There is remoteness in it because of the length of separation.

semin-durr:178-178.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَلاَ يَحْسَبَنَّ الذين كَفَرُواْ أَنَّمَا نُمْلِي}: The majority read «يَحْسَبَنَّ» in the third person, Ḥamza in the second person. Al-Zajjāj related from a great many people a reading like Ḥamza's, except that they put kasra on «إنما» and made «خيراً» accusative, and Ibn Mujāhid denied it; clarification of that will come. Yaḥyā ibn Wathāb read it in the third person with kasra on «إنما», and al-Zamakhsharī also related from him that he read with kasra on the first «إنما» and fatḥa on the second, with the third person. These are five readings.
As for the reading of the majority, its analysis is plain: the verb may be ascribed to «الذين», and «أنَّ» with what is attached to it fills the place of the two objects according to Sībawayh, and the place of one of them with the other omitted according to al-Akhfash, as has preceded more than once. It may also be ascribed to a third-person pronoun by which the Prophet ﷺ is meant, that is: "let not the Prophet, peace be upon him, suppose"; on this «الذين كفروا» is the first object. As for the second, discussion of it will come in the reading of Ḥamza, so on this aspect this reading coincides with the reading of Ḥamza, may Allah have mercy on him, whose analysis will come. «ما» may be a relative noun, in which case the returning pronoun is omitted since the conditions are fulfilled, that is: "that what We prolong"; or it may be a maṣdar particle, that is: "Our prolonging", and it is the noun of «أنَّ» and «خير» its khabar. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It is not permissible that it be a restraining or a redundant particle, for if it were so, «خيرٌ» would be accusative by «نُمْلي», and «أنَّ» would need a khabar if «ما» were redundant, or the verb would be implied to follow it, and both are impossible." End of quotation. This is among the plain matters. They wrote «أنما» joined in both places, though the first, by right, should be written separately because it is a relative.
As for the reading of Ḥamza, the views and analyses of people were unsettled about it, so much so that it was transmitted from Abū Ḥātim that it is a solecism. Al-Naḥḥās said: "A great many people followed him in that", and this is not to be heeded, because of its continuous transmission. There are six aspects in its analysis. One: that the agent of «تحسَبَنَّ» is the pronoun of the Prophet ﷺ, {الذين كَفَرُواْ} the first object, and {أَنَّمَا نُمْلِي لَهُمْ خَيْرٌ} the second object. On this analysis a muḍāf must be omitted: either from the first, its implied form being "do not suppose the condition of those who disbelieved", or from the second, its implied form being "the possessors of 'that Our prolonging is good for them'". We needed this interpretation only because «أنما نُمْلي» is in the interpretation of a maṣdar, and the maṣdar is a notion that does not apply to «الذين كفروا», and the second object in this chapter is the first in meaning.
Two: that {أَنَّمَا نُمْلِي لَهُمْ} is a badal for {الذين كَفَرُواْ}. To this al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ went, and a group followed them, among them al-Zamakhsharī, al-Zajjāj and Ibn al-Bādhish.
Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ said: "The aspect of this reading is repetition and emphasis, and the implied form is: 'do not suppose those who disbelieved, and do not suppose that We prolong'." Al-Farrāʾ said: "And its like is {هَلْ يَنظُرُونَ إِلاَّ الساعة أَن تَأْتِيَهُمْ} [الزخرف: 66], that is: they only wait for it to come to them." End of quotation. Some have rejected the statement of al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ, saying that omitting the second object in these verbs is not permissible according to anyone; this rejection is nothing, because what is forbidden is only omission for the sake of restriction (ḥadhf al-iqtiṣār), and verification of that has preceded. Ibn al-Bādhish said: "The second object is omitted because the speech indicates it, and the implied form is: 'do not suppose that those who disbelieved have the goodness of Our prolonging for them established or occurring'."
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: how is the coming of a badal sound when only one of the two objects is mentioned, and restricting a verb of supposing to one object is not permissible? I say: that is sound because reliance is on the badal, and the substituted-for is in the ruling of the set-aside. Do you not see that you say 'I put your goods, some of them on top of others', although silence on 'goods' alone is impossible?"
Is the badal a badal of inclusion, which is the apparent sense, or a badal of the whole for the whole, in which case it would be on the omission of a muḍāf, its implied form being "do not suppose the prolonging of those", omitting «إملاء» and substituting «أنما نملي» for it? Two well-known views.
Three, the strangest of them: that «الذين» is the agent of «تَحْسَبَنَّ», on the interpretation that the tāʾ in the verb is for the feminine, as in His saying: {كَذَّبَتْ قَوْمُ نُوحٍ} [الشعراء: 105], that is: "let not the people who disbelieved suppose", and «الذين» an attribute of «القوم», as in His saying {وَأَوْرَثْنَا القوم الذين كَانُواْ} [الأعراف: 137]. On this, this reading coincides with the reading with the third person, and its analysis is like its analysis. Abū l-Qāsim al-Kirmānī mentioned that in his exegesis called «al-Lubāb». There is room for objection in it, in that «الذين» runs in the course of the sound masculine plural, and the sound masculine plural does not allow feminising its verb according to the Basrans: it is not permissible to say "qāmat al-Zaydūn" nor "taqūmu l-Zaydūn". As for his excuse for this, that «الذين» is an attribute of «القوم», whose verb may be feminised, and that it was omitted, it does not help him, because consideration is given to what is pronounced, not what is implied; none of the Basrans allows "qāmat al-muslimūn" on the intention "the people, the Muslims" at all. Abū l-Ḥasan al-Ḥawfī said: "«أنَّ» and what it governs is in the position of accusative as a badal, «الذين» is the first object, and the second is omitted", which is the meaning of al-Zamakhsharī's statement above.
Four: that {أَنَّمَا نُمْلِي لَهُمْ} is a badal of inclusion for {الذين كَفَرُواْ}, that is "Our prolonging", and «خيرٌ» in the nominative is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is "it is good for themselves", and the sentence is the second object. Shaykh Shihāb al-Dīn Abū Shāma transmitted that from some. He said: I say: and like this reading is the verse of the Ḥamāsa:
1496 - مِنَّا الأَناةُ وبعضُ القوم يَحْسَبُنا ... أنَّا بِطاءٌ وفي إبطائنا سَرَعُ
(Deliberation is ours, and some of the people think us slow, while in our slowness there is speed.)
Thus the narration came, with fatḥa on «أنَّا» after the mention of the first object. On this it is permissible to say "ḥasibtu Zaydan annahu qāʾimun", that is, "I supposed him a possessor of standing". The aspect of the fatḥa is that it occurs as an object, and it and what it governs are in the position of a singular, which is the second object of «حسبت». End of quotation. There is room for objection in what he said, because the grammarians stated explicitly that kasra of «إنَّ» is obligatory when it occurs as a second object and the first is a name of a concrete thing, and they cited the aforementioned verse for that, and justified the obligation of kasra by saying that if we put fatḥa it would be in the position of a maṣdar, so predicating the meaning about the concrete thing would be necessary.
Five: that {الذين كَفَرُواْ} is the first object, and {إِنَّمَا نُمْلِي لَهُمْ ليزدادوا إِثْمَاً} is in the position of the second object, and {أَنَّمَا نُمْلِي لَهُمْ خَيْرٌ} is a mubtadaʾ and khabar, inserted parenthetically between the two objects of «تَحْسَبَنَّ», with fronting and delaying in the speech. That was transmitted from al-Akhfash. Abū Ḥātim said: "I heard al-Akhfash mention the fatḥa of «أَنَّ», arguing by it for the people of qadar (the Qadariyya), because he was one of them, and he placed it on fronting and delaying, as though he said: 'do not suppose those who [disbelieved], "We only prolong for them that they may increase in sin"; that We prolong for them is good for themselves'." End of quotation. It is permissible that the opening «أَنَّ» with fatḥa be used to begin the speech only because that is the position of al-Akhfash, while others forbid it; if its khabar precedes it, as in "in my opinion that you are departing", or the itemising «أما», as in "as for that you are departing, I have…", it is permissible by consensus. Abū Ḥātim's saying "he mentions the fatḥa of «أنَّ»" means by it the one in His saying {أَنَّمَا نُمْلِي لَهُمْ خَيْرٌ}. The aspect of the Qadariyya's holding to it is that Allah the Exalted may only prolong for them what is good for themselves, because, according to them, regard for what is most beneficial is obligatory.
[Six: al-Mahdawī said: "A group said:] {الذين كَفَرُواْ} was put first for emphasis, then their condition came from His saying {أَنَّمَا نُمْلِي لَهُمْ} as a refutation of them, and the implied form is: 'do not suppose that Our prolonging for those who disbelieved is good for themselves'." End of quotation.
As for the reading of Yaḥyā with kasra of «إنما» with the third person, it cannot but be that the verb is ascribed either to «الذين» or to a third-person pronoun. If the first, then «إنما» and what is within its scope is suspended (muʿallaqa) from «يحسبن», and if the lām is not in its khabar in wording it is implied, so «إنما» with kasra is in the position of accusative, because it is suspended from the verb of supposing with the lām intended; its parallel is the suspension of verbs of the heart from two explicit objects by the implying of the lām of inception, in his saying:
1497 - كذاك أُدِّبْتُ حتى صار مِنْ خُلُقي ... إني رأيتُ مِلاكُ الشيمةِ الأَدَبُ
(Thus was I disciplined until it became part of my character: I have seen that the mainstay of good nature is discipline.)
Were it not for the implying of the lām, the accusative of «مِلاك» and «الأدب» would have been obligatory; and likewise in the verse, were it not for the implying of the lām, fatḥa of «إنما» would have been obligatory. It is also possible that the first object is omitted, namely the pronoun of the affair (ḍamīr al-amr wa-l-shaʾn), and this was said in the verse and is the best in it, the origin being "let him not suppose it", that is, the matter, and «إنما نُمْلِي» is in the position of the second object and is the explanation of the pronoun.
If the second, then «الذين» is the first object and «إنما نملي» is in the position of the second.
As for his reading which al-Zamakhsharī related from him, he analysed it himself, saying: "In the sense: 'let not those who disbelieved suppose that Our prolonging is for the increase of sin, as they do, but it is so that they repent and enter into faith'; and His saying {إِنَّمَا نُمْلِي لَهُمْ خَيْرٌ لأَنْفُسِهِمْ} is parenthetical between the verb and its governed word, its meaning being: Our prolonging is good for themselves if they act on it and know Allah's favour to them in extending the period and leaving off hastening the punishment." End of quotation. On this «الذين» is the agent, «أنما» with fatḥa fills the place of the two objects or of one of them, depending on the disagreement, and this sentence is inserted parenthetically between the verb and its governed word. Al-Naḥḥās said: "The reading of Yaḥyā ibn Wathāb with kasra of «إنَّ» is good, as you say: 'ḥasibtu ʿAmran abūhu khārijun'."
As for what al-Zajjāj related as a reading from a great many, which is the accusative of «خيراً» in the apparent sense of his words, he himself mentioned its analysis on the basis that {أَنَّمَا نُمْلِي لَهُمْ خَيْراً لأَنْفُسِهِمْ} is a badal for «الذين», and «خيراً» is the second object. His text must be cited so that it becomes clear to you. May Allah have mercy on him, he said: "Whoever read «ولا تَحْسَبَنَّ» with the tāʾ, only kasra of «إنَّ» was permissible according to the Basrans, and the meaning: 'do not suppose, those who disbelieved: Our prolonging is good for them', and «إنَّ» entered as emphasis; and if you put fatḥa the meaning becomes: 'do not suppose those who disbelieved — Our prolonging — to be good for them'." He said: "And it is permissible, in my view, in this place, as a badal for «الذين»: the meaning: 'do not suppose Our prolonging for those who disbelieved to be good for them', and a great many have read it, and like this reading in poetry is:
1498 - فما كانَ قَيْسٌ هُلْكُه هلكَ واحدٍ ... ولكنه بنيانُ قومٍ تَهَدَّما
(Qays's death was not the death of one man, but the structure of a people collapsed.)
He made «هُلْكُه» a badal for «قيس»; the meaning: 'the death of Qays was not the death of one man'; that is, the first «هُلْك» is a badal for the nominative, leaving «هُلْكَ واحدٍ» accusative as the khabar of «كان». Likewise {أَنَّمَا نُمْلِي لَهُمْ}: «أن» and its noun, which is the relative «ما» with its ṣila, and the khabar, which is «لهم», are in the position of accusative as a badal for «الذين كفروا», leaving «خيراً» accusative as the second object of «تحسبن»."
Al-Fārisī, however, rejected this from Abū Isḥāq, saying that no one read this reading, I mean the accusative of «خيراً». Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī said: "The badal is valid only with the accusative of «خير», since it is the second object of «حسبت»; so as «هلك واحدٍ» in the verse became accusative, when the first was substituted for «قيس», because it is a khabar of «كان», so «خيراً لهم» becomes accusative when «الإملاء» is substituted for {الذين كَفَرُواْ}, because it is a second object of «تحسبَنَّ»." He said: "I asked Aḥmad ibn Mūsā about it and he claimed that no one read it" — by this Aḥmad he means Abū Bakr ibn Mujāhid, the famous imam.
He said in his «al-Ḥujja»: "«الذين كفروا» is in the position of accusative as the first object of «أنَّ», and the second object is the first in this chapter in meaning; so fatḥa of «أنَّ» in His saying {أَنَّمَا نُمْلِي لَهُمْ} is not permissible, because their being prolonged for is not the same as them." He said: "If you say: why is fatḥa of «أنَّ» not permissible, making it a badal for {الذين كَفَرُواْ}, like His saying {وَمَآ أَنْسَانِيهُ إِلاَّ الشيطان أَنْ أَذْكُرَهُ} [الكهف: 63], and as «أنَّ» is in His saying, the Exalted, {وَإِذْ يَعِدُكُمُ الله إِحْدَى الطائفتين أَنَّهَا لَكُمْ} [الأنفال: 7]? It is said: that is not permissible, otherwise you would have to make «خيراً» accusative, on the implied form: do not suppose the prolonging of those who disbelieved to be good for themselves, since it is the second object of «تحسبنَّ»; and it was said that no one read it so. If it is not made accusative it is known that the badal is not valid in it, and if the badal is not valid, only kasra of «إنَّ» is permissible, making «إنَّ» and its khabar in the position of the second object of «تحسبن»." End of what he rejected it with. So nothing remains but to weigh between the transmission of these two men, I mean al-Zajjāj and Ibn Mujāhid. There is no doubt that Ibn Mujāhid was more attentive to the readings, but al-Zajjāj is reliable and says "a great many read it", and this makes his error in it remote; and affirmation takes precedence over denial. As for what Abū ʿAlī mentioned in his saying "and if the badal is not permissible only kasra of «إنَّ» is permissible" to the end, this also is among what no one read. Makkī said: "The aspect of the reading for whoever read with the tāʾ, I mean the tāʾ of address, is to put kasra on «إنما», so the sentence would be in the position of the second object; and no one read it so, as far as I know."
Abū l-Baqāʾ transmitted the accusative of «خيراً» as an irregular reading; he said: "It has been read irregularly with the accusative, so that «لأنفسهم» is the khabar of «أنَّ», and «لهم» is a clarification or a ḥāl from «خيراً»", meaning that when he made the good for themselves, he made «لهم» either a clarification, its implied form being "I mean, for them", or a ḥāl from the postponed indefinite noun, because it was originally an adjective of it. The apparent sense on this reading is what I presented earlier, namely that «لهم» is the khabar, and «لأنفسهم» is in the position of accusative as an adjective of «خيراً», as it was an adjective of it in the reading of the majority. He also transmitted the reading with kasra of «إنَّ», which is the reading of Yaḥyā, and analysed it as the response of an omitted oath, the oath and its response filling the place of the two objects; there is no need for that, and rather its analysis as preceded is preferable, because the origin is the absence of omission.
Imlāʾ is giving respite and extending life; from it comes "malāwat al-dahr" for a long period, and "al-malawān" are night and day, and their saying "malāka llāhu bi-niʿma" means "He granted it to you for a long life". It was said: al-malawān is the recurrence of night and day and their extension, on the evidence of their being annexed to the two in the poet's saying:
1499 - نهارٌ وليلٌ دائمٌ مَلَواهُما ... على كلِّ حالِ المرءِ يَخْتلفان
(Day and night, their succession constant, alternate upon every state of man.)
Were they the night and the day, they would not be annexed to them, since a thing is not annexed to itself. His saying {أَنَّمَا نُمْلِي لَهُمْ}: the origin of the yāʾ is wāw, and it was turned into yāʾ only because it occurs in the fourth position.
His saying: {إِنَّمَا نُمْلِي لَهُمْ ليزدادوا}: It has already preceded that Yaḥyā ibn Wathāb read with kasra on the first and fatḥa on this one, in what al-Zamakhsharī transmitted from him, and its analysis has preceded. The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān), however, said: "No one related it from him except al-Zamakhsharī; rather those who transmitted the reading of Yaḥyā transmitted only his kasra of the first." He said: "It is only that al-Zamakhsharī, because of his fondness for his doctrine, seeks to return everything to it." This is prejudice against him, because he is reliable and does not transmit what has not been narrated.
As for the reading with kasra of it, there are two aspects. One: that it is a resumptive sentence giving a reason for the sentence before it, as though it were said: "What is the matter with them that they suppose the prolonging to be good?" and it was said: "We only prolong for them that they may increase in sin." «إنَّ» here is restrained by «ما», and for that reason it was written joined, on the original. It is not permissible that it be a relative noun or a particle, because the lām of «kay» cannot occur as the khabar of a mubtadaʾ or its operators.
The second aspect: that this sentence is a repetition of the first. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It was said: «أنما» is a repetition of the first, and «ليزدادوا» is the second object of «تَحْسَبَنَّ», this on the reading with the tāʾ, and the implied form: 'do not suppose, O Muḥammad, the prolonging of those who disbelieved to be good so that they increase in sin, but so that they increase in faith', and it is narrated that some of the Companions read it so." End of quotation. I say: there is room for objection in this, in that he made «ليزدادوا» the second object, and it has already preceded that the lām of «kay» does not occur as the khabar of a mubtadaʾ nor of its operators; and because this is complete for him only on the supposition of fatḥa on the second, and it has preceded that no one transmitted it except al-Zamakhsharī from Yaḥyā, and the one who reads «تحسبن» with the tāʾ of address does not put fatḥa on it at all.
As for the lām in «ليزدادوا», there are two views about it. One: that it is the lām of «kay»; the second, that it is the lām of becoming (ṣayrūra).
His saying: {وَلَهْمُ عَذَابٌ} [Translator's note: the source prints «وَلَهْمُ» for «وَلَهُمْ»]: There are two views about this wāw. One: that it is for conjunction; the second: that it is for ḥāl. The apparent sense of al-Zamakhsharī's saying is that it is for ḥāl only in the reading of Yaḥyā ibn Wathāb, for he said: "If you say: what is the meaning of this reading — meaning the reading of Yaḥyā that he transmitted from him — I say: its meaning is 'let him not suppose that Our prolonging is for the increase of sin and punishment', and the wāw is for ḥāl, as though it were said: 'that they may increase in sin, prepared for them being a humiliating punishment'." The Shaykh said, after what he mentioned of his denial of him for transmitting the fatḥa of the second from Yaḥyā as I presented to you: "When he established in this reading that the meaning rests on prohibiting the disbeliever from supposing that Allah prolongs only for the increase of sin, and that He prolongs only for the increase of good, his saying {وَلَهْمُ عَذَابٌ مُّهِينٌ} would contradict this explanation, so he analysed that with the wāw as ḥāl so that this contradiction between this reading and the end of the verse is removed."
The origin of «ليزدادوا» is "liyaztādū" with a tāʾ, because it is an iftiʿāl form from ziyāda, but the tāʾ of iftiʿāl is turned into dāl after three letters: zāy, dhāl and dāl, as in iddakara and iddāna. The verb here is transitive to one object, and originally it was transitive to two, as in {فَزَادَهُمُ الله مَرَضاً} [البقرة: 10], but with iftiʿāl it always loses an object: if the verb before being built on iftaʿala for the reflexive-passive sense was transitive to one, it becomes intransitive after the reflexive sense, as in "I extended the rope and it extended (famtadda)"; and if it was transitive to two, after iftiʿāl it becomes transitive to one, like this verse.
Each of these three verses ended with a description of the punishment different from the one the other ended with, for a fitting meaning. The first included the report of their hastening in disbelief, and hastening in something and hurrying to obtain it implies its importance and greatness, so their recompense was made "a great punishment" in correspondence to them, and that indicates the baseness of what they hastened into. The second included their buying disbelief with faith; the custom is that the buyer is delighted and pleased with what he bought, and when he loses he feels pain, so this verse ended with the pain of punishment, as the cheated buyer feels the pain of his loss. The third included prolonging, which is being given enjoyment of wealth and the adornment of the world, and that implies pride, arrogance and tyranny, so this verse ended with what implies their humiliation and abasement after their might and arrogance.
